I have a complete picture. Here are the findings.

---

# A) Frontend architecture

## A1. `web/` structure, versions, build tooling

**Stack** (`web/package.json`) — Vue **3.5.39**, Vuetify **4.1.2**, Vite **8.1.1**, `@vitejs/plugin-vue` 6, Pinia **4.0.2**, vue-router **4.6.4**, vue-i18n **11.4.8**, axios 1.18, chart.js 4.5, `oidc-client-ts` 3.5, `@microsoft/signalr` 10, `@mdi/font` 7.4. Tests are **plain `node --test src/**/*.test.js`** — no vitest, no jsdom, so every test is over pure JS modules (never `.vue`).

**Build config** — `web/vite.config.js`. Notable: **no path aliases at all, deliberately**, with an explicit comment that the container mounts only `./web` at `/app` so anything resolved from `../` would exist on the host but not in dev. `allowedHosts: ['.localhost', '.cordango.local']` for subdomain tenancy; `VITE_USE_POLLING` gate for Docker HMR. Port 5173.

**Entry** — `web/index.html` (inline pre-boot script that reads `localStorage['ab-branding']` to set the tab title before the bundle loads) → `web/src/main.js`. `main.js` is dense and does, in order: `applyLocale`, kick off `fetchBranding` at module eval, `createPinia()` + `setActivePinia()` at module scope (so non-component modules can reach stores), install **axios interceptors** (Bearer token onto `API`-prefixed URLs only, `X-Cordango-Locale` header, 401→`resetDataCaches`+`redirectToLogin`, 403→toast), `installCacheInvalidation(axios, API)`, then `createVuetify()` with global `components`/`directives`, the vue-i18n locale adapter, `display.mobileBreakpoint: 'sm'`, and `defaults` for VTextField/VTextarea/VSelect/VBtn. Mount order is `pinia → i18n → vuetify → router`.

**Router** — `web/src/router.js`, `createWebHistory`. Routes: `/`, `/login`, `/auth/callback`, `/preview/:handle/...`, `/preview-session/:token/...`, `/book/:slug` (public), `/studio/cocreate/:sessionId?`, `/studio/legacy/:appId/:section?`, `/studio/:appId?/:section?`, `/admin/:section?`, `/account/keys`, **`/a/:handle/:page?/:recordId?` → `RuntimePage.vue`** (the generated-app runtime), catch-all redirect. `meta`: `bare`, `public`, `shell` ('studio'|'admin'), `requiresAdmin`, `hideSidebar`. Global `beforeEach` auth guard + `setPublicMatcher`.

**Pinia stores** — all in `web/src/stores/`, and they are a *read-cache layer*, not domain stores:
- `entities.js` — `useEntities` (`defineStore('entities')`), the row/aggregate cache: coalescing, TTL, stale-while-revalidate. Owns **policy only**; never builds a URL (callers pass a `fetcher`).
- `refdata.js` — `useRefData` + `resetDataCaches` / `dropScopedCaches`.
- `keys.js`, `policy.js`, `invalidation.js`, `composables.js` (`useEntityRows`, `useAggregate`), `buildRefData.js`.
Everything else that looks like state is a **plain reactive module**, not a store: `shell.js` (353 lines, the shell/nav/SignalR/user-settings singleton), `theme.js`, `me.js`, `commands.js`, `refState.js`, `personalViews.js`, `assistant.js`.

**i18n / formatting** — `web/src/i18n/index.js` (vue-i18n `legacy:false`, `SUPPORTED = ['en','de']`, `ab-locale` localStorage key, `applyLocale`, non-component `t`/`tc`, merges Vuetify's own `en`/`de` bundles under `$vuetify`), `web/src/i18n/formatting.js` (memoized `Intl` formatters: `formatDate`, `formatDateTime`, `formatTime`, `formatDatePart`, `formatNumber`, `formatCurrency`, `formatPercent`, `formatRelative`, `isoDate`), `web/src/i18n/locales/{en,de}.json` (~46 KB / ~52 KB), `web/src/i18n/i18n.test.js` (key parity/placeholder/plural guard). **Only depends on `./index.js`** — trivially portable.

Note a wrinkle for a shared package: `manifest.js` has its **own** `fmtMoney` / `fmtNumber` / `fmtDate` / `fmtDateTime` / `fmtAgo` / `fmtSince` / `fmtValue`, separate from `i18n/formatting.js`. Two formatting vocabularies coexist.

## A2. The block renderer

**`web/src/views/BlockRenderer.vue`** (431 lines) is the dispatcher. It is a **v-if/v-else-if chain over `b.kind`**, not a registry — 30+ imports at the top, one branch per kind. It is self-referential (`<BlockRenderer>` inside `tabs`, `section`, `columns`) and hosted by **`web/src/AppRuntime.vue`** (1369 lines — the runtime host that owns the manifest fetch, the shared full-screen detail, the create/edit form, commands, peek, toasts).

Dispatch table (kind → component):
| kind | component |
|---|---|
| `view` (→ `view.type`) | `TableView` / `KanbanView` / `DashboardView` / `CalendarView` / `TimelineView`, preceded by `ViewPresetBar` |
| `widgets` | `WidgetsGrid.vue` |
| `hub` | `HubHeader.vue` |
| `process` | `ProcessBlock.vue` (state stepper + transition commands) |
| `history` / `answers` / `intake` | `HistoryBlock` / `AnswersBlock` / `IntakeBlock` |
| `externalEmbed` / `relatedApps` | `PrimExternalEmbed` / `PrimRelatedApps` |
| `tiles` | `StatTiles.vue` |
| `fields` | `RecordFields.vue` |
| `settings` | `SettingsForm.vue` |
| `child` | `ChildBlock.vue` (674 lines) |
| `tabs` / `section` / `columns` | inline templates + recursion |
| `stack`/`row`/`grid`/`card` (`LAYOUT_PRIMS`) | `PrimBox.vue` |
| `repeat` | `PrimRepeat.vue` |
| `cell` | `PrimCell.vue` |
| `stat` / `chart` | `PrimStat.vue` / `PrimChart.vue` |
| `field`/`text`/`chip`/`avatar`/`progress`/`action` (`LEAF_PRIMS`) | `PrimLeaf.vue` |
| `create` | `UiButton` (emits the same `create` event a table's newButton does) |
| `control` / `filterbar` | `PrimControl.vue` / `PrimFilterBar.vue` |
| `timeline` / `orgchart` | `PrimTimeline.vue` / `PrimOrgChart.vue` |
| `table` / `calendar` / `form` | `PrimTable.vue` / `PrimCalendar.vue` / `PrimForm.vue` |
| `split` / `board` / `gantt` | `PrimSplit.vue` / `PrimBoard.vue` / `PrimGantt.vue` |

Cross-cutting mechanics worth knowing before extraction:
- **`binding`** prop: `{ mode:'collection' }` or `{ mode:'record', record, entityKey }`, plus `scopes`, `access`, `userId`, `routeFilters`, `dense`. Every leaf reads it.
- **Event bubbling contract**: `open`, `openPanel`, `edit`, `create`, `remove`, `changed`, `command` — re-emitted verbatim through every container. This is already a clean host boundary.
- **Edit mode**: when `edit` is non-null each block is wrapped in `BlockFrame.vue`; otherwise a no-render functional `Pass` component so normal rendering is unchanged.
- `visibleWhen` via `resolveExpr` + `matchFilter` from `manifest.js`; `columnsTemplate` via `projectCols` from `responsive.js`.

**`web/src/blockspec/`** (5 files, shared introspection):
- `schema.js` — holds no schema; `configure(schemaDoc)` installs it. Two hosts get the document by different routes.
- `blocks.js` (16.7 KB) — property specs, roles, palette groups, `newBlock` factories, `slotsOf`, all derived from `$defs.block_<kind>`.
- `tree.js` — pure path/splice ops (`atPath`, `scopeEntityOf`, `walkBlocks`, `duplicateAt`, `moveAt`, `removeAt`, `wrapAt`). No store, no reactivity, no undo.
- `vocab.js` — `SCOPE_TOKENS`, curated MDI `ICONS`.
- `load.js` — **web-only** loader: `axios.get(${API}/api/schema/page)` + `/api/catalog` + `/api/schema/platform-entities`, then `configure()`. This is the one file in `blockspec/` that touches the platform.

## A3. Extraction candidates — "nearly standalone" vs "deeply entangled"

The dependency graph is shallow and legible. Three modules are the entanglement:
- **`data.js`** (324 lines) — the *only* place that knows the handle-scoped REST shape. `API` const, `fetchRows`, `useRows`, `fetchRecord`, `fetchAggregate`, `manifestOf`, `refTarget`, `refRoute`, `loadPeople`, `fetchPlatform`, `fetchRefData`, `fetchRefMaps`, `isPersonField`, `mediaUrl`. Imports pinia + axios.
- **`commands.js`** — `fetchAccess`, `invokeCommand`, `resolveActions`, `commandEnabled`, `statusCellMoves`, `processForEntity`, `toast`.
- **`me.js` / `refState.js` / `shell.js` / `theme.js`** — actor identity, deactivated-reference badges, shell singleton, tenant branding.

And one module is the opposite: **`web/src/manifest.js` (496 lines) has ZERO imports.** Its header literally says "Pure manifest helpers … (no Vue deps)". People-directory resolution is injected via `setPeopleDirectory(byId)` specifically to break the cycle with `data.js`. This is the natural core of a controls package.

| Family | Files | Coupling | Call |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pure primitives** | `ui/UiButton`, `UiChip`, `UiSurface`, `UiSwitch`, `UiTextField`, `UiTextarea`, `UiTable`, `UiMeter`, `UiLink`, `UiPeek`, `UiAvatar`, `UiSlugField`, `UiSelect`(+`UiOptionItem`), `views/BlockFrame`, `views/PrimControl`, `views/OrgNode`, `views/DayGrid` | zero or Vue-only imports | **Nearly standalone.** Lift as-is. `UiOptionItem`→`optionAccent.js`→`theme.js#isBrandColor` is a one-function break. `UiSheet`/`UiTimezone` need `responsive.js` / `views/timezones.js` only. |
| **Pure logic modules** | `manifest.js`, `blockspec/{blocks,schema,tree,vocab}.js`, `responsive.js`, `i18n/formatting.js`, `views/timeRange.js`, `views/dayGrid.js`, `views/weeklyHours.js`, `views/chipsEditor.js`, `views/companyGroup.js`, `views/inlineCreate.js`, `filterMemory.js`, `home/layout.js`, `tables/*` composables, `board.js`*, `tableGroups.js`* | pure (starred two import `data.js`) | **Nearly standalone**, and already unit-tested under `node --test` — the tests travel with them. `responsive.js` imports `useDisplay` from Vuetify only. |
| **Data table** | `ui/UiDataTable.vue` (**1231 lines**, the single biggest component) + `tables/CellEditor.vue` + 5 `use*` composables + `tableSettings.js` | `data.js` (`isPersonField`, `loadPeople`, `mediaUrl`), `me.js`, `manifest.js`, `responsive.js`, `tableSettings.js` (axios) | **Moderate.** No router, no pinia, no axios directly. The whole platform surface is: a people directory, an "is this me" predicate, a media URL resolver, and per-user column settings — 4 injectable seams. Highest-value extraction. |
| **Form inputs** | `views/FieldInput.vue` (dispatcher over field type) → `UiTextField/Textarea/Select/Switch/UiRefPicker/UiTimezone/UiSlugField/WeeklyHours` | `manifest.js#optionsOf` + `useI18n` | **Nearly standalone.** `FieldInput` is the cleanest boundary in the repo. |
| **Reference / person pickers** | `ui/UiRefPicker`, `ui/PersonChip`, `ui/PersonAvatar`, `ui/RefLink`, `ui/RefStateBadge`, `ui/RefStateAlert`, `views/ChipsEditor` | `data.js` (`loadPeople`, `isPersonField`, `refRoute`), `me.js` (`isMe`, `hoistMe`, `meLabel`, `meId`), `refState.js` | **Moderate — needs a directory provider.** Same 3 seams over and over: directory, "me", ref-route. `RefLink` uses `inject()` already. |
| **Board / kanban** | `views/KanbanCore.vue` (221, presentational) + `views/KanbanView.vue` / `views/PrimBoard.vue` (loaders) + `board.js` | Core: `manifest.js` + `commands.js`. Loaders: axios + `data.js` | **Already split correctly.** `KanbanCore` is presentational; only `commands.js` (`commandEnabled`, `statusCellMoves`, `toast`) blocks it. Extract Core, leave the two loaders. |
| **Calendar** | `views/CalendarView.vue` (354) + `views/DayGrid.vue` + `dayGrid.js` + `timeRange.js` + `views/QuickAdd.vue` + `PrimCalendar` | `CalendarView` imports axios + `API` directly | **Moderate.** `DayGrid`/`dayGrid.js`/`timeRange.js` are pure and testable; `CalendarView` needs its fetch lifted out. |
| **Timeline / Gantt** | `views/PrimTimeline.vue` (281), `views/PrimGantt.vue` (400), `views/TimelineView.vue` | `data.js`, `commands.js#toast`, `responsive.js`, axios (Gantt, TimelineView) | **Moderate.** Layout maths already in `timeRange.js` (`spanIn`, `packRows`). |
| **Chart** | `ui/ChartCard.vue` (**imports only `vue` + `chart.js/auto`**) + `views/PrimChart.vue` | ChartCard: none. PrimChart: `useRouter` + `data.js` + `blockAggregate.js` + `deeplink.js` | **`ChartCard` is fully standalone — take it today.** `PrimChart` is the platform wrapper. |
| **Process stepper** | `views/ProcessBlock.vue` (only `UiButton` + `commands.js`) | `commands.js` | **Nearly standalone** behind a command-invoker interface. |
| **Command button** | `UiButton` + the `command` event contract + `commands.js` | `commands.js` imports axios + `API` + `manifest.js` | **Interface, not code.** Define `invokeCommand`/`commandEnabled`/`resolveActions` as the injected port. |
| **Filter bar** | `views/PrimFilterBar.vue` + `ui/UiFacetSelect.vue` + `filterMemory.js` | `data.js`, `commands.js`, `me.js`, `responsive.js` | **Moderate.** `filterMemory.js` is pure localStorage. |
| **Money / date inputs** | no dedicated components — money/date live inside `FieldInput` + `manifest.js#fmtMoney/fmtDate/fmtValue` + `i18n/formatting.js` | pure | **Nearly standalone**, but you'd be *creating* the components, and you'd have to reconcile the two formatter families first. |
| **Layout primitives** | `views/PrimBox.vue` (stack/row/grid/card), `columns`/`section`/`tabs` inline in `BlockRenderer`, `responsive.js#projectCols` | `manifest.js` + `responsive.js` | **Nearly standalone.** |
| **Detail / form** | `views/RecordForm.vue` (435), `RecordFields`, `HubHeader`, `SettingsForm`, `CommandDialog`, `PropField` | `RecordForm` pulls axios + `data.js` + `refNarrow.js` + `refScope.js` + `me.js` + `CompanyPicker` | **Deeply entangled.** |
| **The renderer itself** | `views/BlockRenderer.vue`, `views/PrimRepeat/PrimSplit/PrimTable/PrimCell/PrimLeaf/StatTiles/PrimStat/WidgetsGrid/ChildBlock` | every one of them imports `data.js`; several import axios directly | **Deeply entangled** by design — these *are* the data-plane bindings. Extractable only behind a full injected data-plane port. |
| **Platform-only, do not extract** | `AppRuntime.vue` (1369), `App.vue`, `shell/*`, `admin/*`, `studio/*`, `account/*`, `home/*`, `public/*`, `auth.js`, `shell.js`, `theme.js`, `personalViews.js`, `WaffleLauncher`, `AssistantPanel`, `views/CompanyPicker.vue` (635 lines, enrichment-specific) | router + pinia + SignalR + OIDC + tenant branding | **Platform.** |

**Cross-cutting facts that shape the package boundary:**
- **`vue-router` is imported by exactly 4 files** under `views/`+`home/`: `PrimChart.vue`, `PrimStat.vue`, `StatTiles.vue`, `home/HomeWidgetCard.vue` — all four only to push a deep link. Replace with a `navigate` emit/inject and the entire controls surface is router-free.
- **pinia is imported by exactly 7 files**, all in `stores/` plus `home/useWidgetData.js`. **Zero components import pinia.**
- **axios is imported directly by 19 view components** (listed above) — that is the real extraction cost, not the stores.
- **`useI18n`/`$t` appears in 37 of ~68 view/ui components.** A shared package must either ship its own catalogue namespace or take a `t` injection.
- **`web/src/manifest.js` + `web/src/blockspec/` + `i18n/formatting.js` + `responsive.js` + the pure `views/*.js` logic modules are ~2,000 lines that move with zero edits.**

## A4. `/editor` and how blockspec is shared

`editor/` is a **separate Vite app** (`appdef-editor`, port 5174, own `package.json`: Vue 3.5.39 + Vuetify 4.1.2 + `monaco-editor` + `ajv`/`ajv-formats` + `vuedraggable`). It is **not** in a workspace — separate `package.json`, separate `package-lock.json`, separate `node_modules`.

Sharing is by **Vite alias reaching into sibling folders** (`editor/vite.config.js`):
```js
'@'         → ./src
'@schema'   → ../schema
'@blockspec'→ ../web/src/blockspec     // ONE derivation of the contract, two hosts
'@reference'→ ../exploration/reference
server: { fs: { allow: ['..'] } }
```
The config comments state the reasoning explicitly: blockspec **lives in `web/` because that is the shipped product and its container mounts only `./web`**; the editor is a dev tool that already reaches out for `@schema`, so it reaches in for blockspec too.

Consumers on the editor side: `editor/src/schema/blocks.js` and `schema/schema.js` are thin re-export shims over `@blockspec`; `editor/src/designer/ops.js` imports `duplicateAt/moveAt/removeAt/wrapAt` from `@blockspec/tree.js`; `editor/src/model/doc.js` imports `walkBlocks` + re-exports `atPath/scopeEntityOf/resolveScope`; `editor/src/model/completions.js` re-exports `ICONS`/`SCOPE_TOKENS` from `@blockspec/vocab.js`.

**The schema arrives by two different routes** — that is why `blockspec/schema.js` uses `configure()` instead of an import: the editor does `import raw from '@schema/app-definition.schema.json'` at build time; web does `loadBlockSpec()` → `GET /api/schema/page` lazily when the view editor opens (~79 KB, not in the startup bundle).

**Editor ↔ platform integration** is an **iframe + postMessage** protocol, not an import. `web/src/studio/sections/DesignSection.vue` embeds `VITE_EDITOR_URL` (default `http://localhost:5174`) with `?embed=1`; `editor/src/store/embed.js` defines the protocol (`host→editor`: `load`/`theme`/`saved`; `editor→host`: `ready`/`change`/`save`). `change` deliberately carries no document.

**Deliberately NOT shared** (STATUS.md:365-370): the property *controls*. `web/src/views/PropField.vue` and `editor/src/components/PropEditor.vue` are siblings, not one component — "the *derivation* is shared, where drift would mean offering a property the gate rejects; the widgets are not, where drift is cosmetic." Worth knowing: a controls package is the third host that would face the same question.

---

# B) Top-level repo layout

## B1. Top-level directories

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `backend/` | 19 .NET projects + `Directory.Build.props` + **three** `.slnx` files (below) |
| `web/` | The Vue 3 SPA (`src/`, `public/`, `index.html`, `vite.config.js`, `dist/` gitignored) |
| `editor/` | Standalone App Definition editor (`src/{code,components,designer,model,schema,store,workspaces}`, `scripts/check.mjs`) |
| `marketing/` | **Eleventy** site (`cordango-marketing`): `_data`, `_includes`, `blog`, `capabilities`, `de/`, `samples`, `lib`, `*.njk`, `_headers`/`_redirects`, deploys via `wrangler pages` |
| `schema/` | `app-definition.schema.json`, `blueprint.schema.json`, `platform-entities.json`, `src/{root,domain,ui,behavior,security,notifications}.json`, `core/` (versioned core app defs + `registry.json`), `cocreation/`, `examples/`, `compose.py`, `validate.py`, `README.md` |
| `_docs/` | 28 planning docs + `assets/` + `outdated/`; includes `plan_index.md`, `CordyOSS.md`, `COMPONENTS.md`, `LOCAL_SUBDOMAINS.md` |
| `demo/` | Demo world: `seed/` (15 `*.seed.json`), `home/` (3 widget layouts), `load.py`, `check_seed.py`, `derive_core_people.py`, `snapshot.sh`, `restore.sh`, `WORLD.md` |
| `exploration/` | `reference/` (hand-authored app defs), `generator/` (the Python generator: `generate.py`, `gate.py`, `evolve.py`, `providers.py`, `prompts.py`, …), `cord/` (op schemas + `apps/`), budget-planner scripts |
| `bench/` | Generation benchmark: `run.py`, `score.py`, `cord_run.py`, `cord_score.py`, `corpus/`, `requests.json`, `results/` (gitignored), `pilot-checklist.md` |
| `examples/` | `semantic/` (the Budget Planner CordSource specimen) |
| `_utils/` | Python live-acceptance/screenshot scripts (`s3_*.py`, `ref_pickers.py`, …) + `screenshots/` (gitignored) |
| `appdata/` | **gitignored** runtime data root: `apps/`, `genlogs/`, `runtime/` |
| `backup/` | `appdefs-20260806/` (pre-PG18 export) |
| `.claude/` | `settings.json`, `settings.local.json`, `skills/`, **`worktrees/`** (`RAG_Step1`, `blueprint-generation-rework`) |
| `.entire/` | `logs/`, `metadata/`, `settings.json`, `tmp/` (third-party tool) |
| `.venv/`, `.pytest_cache/` | Python env / cache |

Root files: `docker-compose.yml` (23.8 KB, heavily commented), `DOCKER.md`, **`STATUS.md` (205 KB)**, `readme.md` (2 bytes — effectively empty), `.env` (gitignored), `.gitignore`, `test.md`, `transcript.json`, `Cordango_Liquiditaetsplan.xlsx`, and six large PNGs (`hero2/3/4.png`, `v2/3/4.png`, ~3.5 MB each — these are the main repo-size offenders for a public split).

## B2. Submodules / solutions / workspaces / monorepo tooling

- **No git submodules.** No `.gitmodules`. (`git submodule status` errors on `.claude/worktrees/RAG_Step1` — that's a **git worktree**, not a submodule.)
- **No npm workspaces** — none of the three `package.json` files (`web`, `editor`, `marketing`) declares `workspaces`, and there is no root `package.json`. Three independent lockfiles and three `node_modules`.
- **No pnpm/lerna/nx/turbo** — no `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `lerna.json`, `nx.json`, `turbo.json`.
- **Three .NET solutions**, and the OSS boundary is already codified in them:
  - `backend/AppBuilder.slnx` — all 19 projects.
  - **`backend/AppBuilder.Oss.slnx`** — "THE INSTALLABLE PRODUCT BOUNDARY": Definition(+Tests), Localization, AccessTokens, Cord(+Tests), Runtime, Cli(+Tests). Header: *"What is deliberately ABSENT is the point: no Api, no Worker, no ControlPlane, no Generator, no Platform."*
  - **`backend/AppBuilder.Cord.slnx`** — "THE EXTRACTION TEST, as a runnable command rather than a claim": Definition + Cord + Cord.Tests, must pass with no database/containers. *"if that command works, extraction is a copy; the day it stops working, something has been welded on."*
  
  **This is the precedent to copy for `@cordango/web-controls`** — a solution/config whose only job is to fail when the boundary erodes. Nothing equivalent exists on the JS side today.
- Current branch: **`CLI-CodeGen`**; HEAD `6d4bcee`. Two active worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`.

## B3. Docker compose

`docker-compose.yml`, 7 services + 9 named volumes.

| Service | Image | Ports | Host mounts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api` | `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0` | 5215:80 | `./backend:/app/backend`, `./schema:/app/schema`, `./appdata:/app/appdata` (+ `nuget`, `build_api`, `aspnet_keys`, `dotnet_state`, bin/obj shadow volumes) |
| `worker` | same | — | `./backend`, `./schema`, `./appdata` (+ volumes) |
| `ops` | same | 5290:80 | `./backend:/app/backend` (+ `nuget`, `build_ops`, `dotnet_state`) |
| **`web`** | `node:20-bookworm-slim` | 5173:5173 | **`./web:/app` — and nothing else** + `web_node_modules:/app/node_modules` |
| **`editor`** | `node:20-bookworm-slim` | 5174:5174 | **`.:/repo`** (the whole repo root) + `editor_node_modules:/repo/editor/node_modules` + anonymous `/repo/web/node_modules` |
| `mailpit` | `axllent/mailpit` | 8025, 1025 | — |
| `db` | `postgres:18` | 5432:5432 | `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` |

**Confirmed — the "web container mounts only `./web`" note is accurate, and it is asserted in three places:**

# App Definition Pipeline — Map for a Standalone Source Generator

## 1. The App Definition schema

**Location:** `schema/` at the repo root — a real folder, checked in, **and** embedded as a resource.

| Path | Size | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `schema/app-definition.schema.json` | **~213 KB**, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, `$id: https://appbuilder.dev/schemas/app-definition/2.0` | **The composed contract.** The only artifact anything downstream consumes. Generated, but checked in. |
| `schema/src/root.json` | 8.8 KB | Envelope + metadata/archetype/plugins; primitives (`identifier`, `fieldPath`, `filter`, `condition` refs) |
| `schema/src/domain.json` | 32.5 KB | `entities`, `relations` |
| `schema/src/ui.json` | **137.5 KB** | `presentation`, `views`, `pages`, `theme` + the whole 41-kind block system |
| `schema/src/behavior.json` | 28.7 KB | `processes`, `commands`, `workflows`, `condition`, `effect` |
| `schema/src/notifications.json` | 1.4 KB | `effect_notify`, `effect_email` |
| `schema/src/security.json` | 2.6 KB | `roles` |
| `schema/compose.py` | — | `src/*.json` → composed file. `--check` is the CI drift guard. |
| `schema/platform-entities.json` | 4.7 KB | Canonical platform entities (`person`, `department`, `group`) — the `targetApp: "platform"` model |
| `schema/core/registry.json` + `core_*.vN.json` | — | Core apps (`core_people` v1, `core_organizations` v1–v4, `core_calendar` v1–v2) — every shipped version retained |
| `schema/README.md` | — | Authoritative prose on the contract, incl. the explicit "JSON Schema can't do referential integrity, so a semantic validator is a required separate layer" |

**Top-level properties** (required: `schemaVersion`, `key`, `name`, `version`, `entities`):

```
schemaVersion  key  name  version  description  archetype  plugins
entities  relations  presentation  views  pages  theme
processes  commands  workflows  roles
```

**81 `$defs`.** Notable groups:
- Domain: `entity`, `field`, `relation`, `fieldPath`, `filter`, `sort`, `groupBy`
- Behavior: `process`, `command`, `workflow`, `condition`, `effect` + 7 typed effect defs
- Security: `role`
- UI: `view`, `page`, `tab`, `tile`, `theme`, `presentation`, `screenState`, `formBlock`, `visibleWhen`, `deepLink`, `combine`, `statMax`, `timeAxis`, plus **41 `block_*` defs** (`block_view`, `block_tabs`, `block_hub`, `block_grid`, `block_repeat`, `block_stat`, `block_board`, `block_gantt`, `block_orgchart`, `block_history`, `block_relatedApps`, `block_intake`, `block_answers`, `block_externalEmbed`, …)

The block union uses `allOf` / `if`/`then` `const` dispatch (never `unevaluatedProperties` — the composer asserts this; it crashes the JsonSchema.Net host).

**Cocreation contract — yes, present and frozen:** `schema/cocreation/contract.md` (frozen 2026-08-11, v1.1), plus `answer.schema.json`, `artifacts.schema.json` (15 KB), `exchange.schema.json`, `question.schema.json`, `session-state.schema.json`, `sketch.schema.json`, and 14 worked `examples/bp-*.json`. This is the request/response contract between the co-creation backend and `web/src/studio/cocreation/**`, with a byte-identical mirror in `web/`. It is orthogonal to your generator — it governs the authoring conversation, not the app artifact. Three of its files are embedded into `AppBuilder.Generator` (see its `.csproj`).

Also: `schema/blueprint.schema.json` (46.9 KB) — a **separate language** from the App Definition, describing what the user approved in their own vocabulary; lowered into an App Definition by `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Blueprint/BlueprintLowering.cs`.

---

## 2. What "compilation" exists today

There are **three** distinct compilations. This matters a lot for your plan.

### (a) Cord DSL → App Definition (`AppBuilder.Cord`)

There **is** a DSL→AppDefinition compiler, and it is deliberately deterministic and dependency-free.

- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordLower.cs` — `CordApp` → App Definition. Pure, deterministic, and explicitly documented as *"a function of the model ALONE"* — it may never read the definition it came from, a DB, or anything else.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordImport.cs` (+ `CordImportBehaviour.cs`, `CordImportScreens.cs`) — the reverse direction.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordSource.cs` — splits/joins the app into per-aggregate documents; `Join(Split(d)) == d` is a test.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordApp.cs`, `CordDocument.cs`, `CordTransaction.cs`, `CordOps*.cs` — the semantic model and operation vocabulary.
- Syntax lives outside Cord: `backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Workspace/Yaml.cs` owns YAML, `AppFolder.cs` owns the filesystem. Extension: `.cord.yaml`.

Today the **App Definition JSON is still the stored/authored artifact** and Cord is derived from it. `CordLower.cs`'s own header states the intent to invert that: *"the eventual open-source story wants `*.cord` to stand on its own as source with the App Definition demoted to a compiled deployment artifact."*

Worked example: `examples/semantic/budgetPlanner/` — the full Budget Planner in **both** `.cord.yaml` and `.cord.ts` form, with `coverage.json` recording authority hashes and `verify.py` proving exact reconstruction.

Coverage escape hatch: `exploration/cord/raw-allowlist.json` pins every place Cord still carries a raw App Definition fragment instead of modelling it (asserted exactly, not as a subset).

### (b) App Definition → runtime manifest (`AppCompiler`)

`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/AppCompiler.cs` (**1,134 lines**) — the piece your generator most directly parallels. `AppCompiler.Compile(definition, appId, builtAt)` produces a *manifest*, a different shape that is deliberately **not** re-validated against the App Definition schema. What it adds:

- injects base/system fields on every entity (`id` leading; `company_id`, `app_id`, `created_at/by`, `updated_at/by`, `deleted_at`, `record_state` trailing)
- `FlagComputedFields` — marks computed fields read-only/server-owned
- `CanonicalizeProcesses` — derives status-field options from process states, stamps `governedBy`
- `SynthesizeCommands` — creates a command for every command-less transition (naming rule shared with the gate via `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ProcessCommands.cs`)
- `FlagCommandOwnedFields` — fields collected by a command's `input` become non-editable in generic forms
- `InferSubordination` (parent/child IA), `InferConfigEntities` (lookup tables → "Configuration" nav group)
- `DefaultViews`, `DefaultTableColumns`, detail/page synthesis
- stamps `AppSchemaVersion.Stamp` (`"2.0"`; runtime refuses non-`2.` majors)

### (c) Validation — where it lives

**Project:** `AppBuilder.Definition`, **namespace** `AppBuilder.Definition`.

- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Gate.cs` — **3,296 lines**. The class is `Gate`.
  - `Gate.StructuralErrors(JsonNode)` — JSON Schema evaluation with a *hierarchical* walk that prunes valid branches (so failed `if` probes and losing `oneOf` siblings don't produce phantom errors)
  - `Gate.StructuralErrors(JsonNode, JsonNode schema)` — arbitrary-schema overload for tool payloads
  - `Gate.SemanticErrors(JsonNode)` — referential integrity, unique keys, reachability, behavior-layer rules (the behavior section alone spans ~lines 936–2999)
  - `Gate.Validate(JsonNode)` — structural + semantic, the entry point everything calls
  - `Gate.PageErrors`, `Gate.PresetErrors`, `Gate.DesignErrors`
  - `Gate.BaseFields` — the canonical base-field set, shared with `AppCompiler`
  - Documented as a **port of the Python `generator/gate.py`**, so `exploration/generator/gate.py` + the Python examples are the cross-language conformance corpus.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Normalizer.cs` — pre-gate deterministic repair (double-encoded JSON sections, envelope unwrapping, tolerant duplicate-key parsing, authoring-kind lowering)
- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Schemas.cs` — loads embedded schemas; hosts `AppSchemaVersion` (`Current = "2.0"`, `SupportedMajor = "2."`)
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/CandidateValidator.cs` — the *full* pipeline in one uninterruptible call: `parse → Gate.Validate → DesignDefaults fills → Gate.Validate again → AppCompiler.Compile → smoke checks → hash`. Distinguishes **Coherent** (gate-clean + compiles) from **Valid** (also a finished app). Only `Valid` yields a hash.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Workspace/Pipeline.cs` — `Pipeline.Check(LoadedApp)` → `CheckReport`. Wraps `CandidateValidator` for the CLI. **Never spends a token or opens a socket.** Uses `Pipeline.DeterministicBuiltAt = DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch` so equal source produces byte-equal artifacts.

### DefinitionHash

`backend/AppBuilder.Definition/DefinitionHash.cs` — **37 lines**, trivially portable:

```csharp
public static string Of(JsonNode? node) => OfText(Canonical(node)?.ToJsonString() ?? "null");
public static string OfText(string s) => Convert.ToHexStringLower(SHA256.HashData(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(s)));
public static JsonNode? Canonical(JsonNode? node)   // recursively orders object keys ordinally; array order preserved
```

SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex. Key-order-independent (definitions round-trip through a `jsonb` column, which reorders keys); **array order is meaningful and preserved** (field order drives column and render order). A content-only variant excluding `version` lives at `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Services/AppRelease.cs` → `AppRelease.ContentHash`.

---

## 3. The C# model classes — the key finding

**There are no POCO model classes for AppDefinition.** `grep -rn "class AppDefinition|record AppDefinition"` across `backend/` returns nothing. The entire pipeline operates on `System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode` / `JsonObject`. Every one of the 39 files in `AppBuilder.Definition` that touches a definition uses `JsonNode`.

The typed records that *do* exist are for adjacent concerns:
- `ComputedValue`, `ComputedExprValidation` in `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ComputedExpr.cs`
- `CoreApp`, `CoreAppVersion`, `CoreEntity` in `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/CoreAppRegistry.cs`
- The **Cord semantic model** in `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordApp.cs` — `CordEntity`, `CordProcess`, `CordTransition`, `CordAction`, etc. This is the closest thing to a typed object graph over an app, and it is a *different, smaller* vocabulary than the App Definition.
- `AppRecord` in `backend/AppBuilder.Platform/AppRecord.cs` — DTO whose `Definition` is a `JsonNode?`

### Reusability in isolation: excellent

`backend/AppBuilder.Definition/AppBuilder.Definition.csproj`:
- **Zero project references.**
- **One package: `JsonSchema.Net` 9.2.2.**
- `net10.0`, nullable enabled.
- Embeds `app-definition.schema.json`, `platform-entities.json`, `blueprint.schema.json`, `schema/core/*.json`.

No EF, no ASP.NET, no Npgsql, no provider client. `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/AppBuilder.Cord.csproj` references only `AppBuilder.Definition` and calls that ItemGroup *"RULE 0 — this project is independently extractable, and this ItemGroup is the whole claim."* `backend/AppBuilder.Cord.Tests/BoundaryTests.cs` asserts the compiled assembly's reference set against an allowlist.

Two solution files encode the boundaries you care about:
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord.slnx` — `{Definition, Cord, Cord.Tests}`. "THE EXTRACTION TEST, as a runnable command rather than a claim… must pass with no database, no containers, no Platform and no Generator."
- `backend/AppBuilder.Oss.slnx` — adds `Localization`, `AccessTokens`, `Runtime`, `Cli`. "THE INSTALLABLE PRODUCT BOUNDARY… no Api, no Worker, no ControlPlane, no Generator, no Platform."

`AppBuilder.Runtime` adds only `Npgsql` 10.0.3 + `AppBuilder.Localization` — no EF. So `{Definition, Cord, Runtime, Cli}` is a clean, ASP.NET-free base for a standalone generator.

**Note the naming trap:** `backend/AppBuilder.Generator/` is **not** a code generator — it is the LLM/agent layer (`Providers.cs`, `Prompts*.cs`, `DesignSession.cs`, `CoCreationTools.cs`, `CordToolAdapter.cs`). Your project needs a different name.

---

## 4. Runtime semantics a generator must reimplement

### Entity storage — typed Postgres tables, schema-per-tenant. Not jsonb.

- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/PostgresStorage.cs` (220 lines) — pure naming + type mapping, no I/O. Schema = `tenant_{id}`. Table = `{handle}__{entity}`, with `{handle}_{appId8}__{entity}` and `a{appId}__{entity}` collision fallbacks. 63-char Postgres identifier limit enforced.
  - `PgTypeFor`: `integer`→`bigint`, `decimal`/`money`→`numeric`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`→`timestamptz`, `multiselect`→`text[]`, `json`→`jsonb`; everything else (`text`, `longtext`, `email`, `url`, `phone`, `select`, `reference`, `attachment`, `uuid`) → text. `id` is `text PRIMARY KEY`.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/TenantSchemaProvisioner.cs` (224 lines) — `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS`, one typed table per entity, live-migrates by ADDing missing columns only (never drops or retypes). Creates **partial unique indexes** (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`) for `unique` fields. Returns the `storage` block `{engine, tenant, schema, tables}` stamped into the manifest — the store resolves through that stamp, never by re-deriving names.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/PostgresEntityStore.cs` (445 lines), `IEntityStore.cs`, `InMemoryEntityStore.cs` — the seam. Records are `JsonObject` property bags; there is no CLR type per entity. Both stores must return identical results for the same `EntityQuery` (pinned by a test).
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/RuntimeStore.cs` — built manifests at `{dataDir}/runtime/{appId}/app.json` (see `appdata/runtime/`, gitignored).

### Computed expressions

- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ComputedExpr.cs` (565 lines) — a small typed language shared by gate and runtime; **same AST for parse and eval**, so a gate-accepted expression cannot mean something different at runtime. Expressions are data, never handed to an evaluator. Types: `Number`, `Boolean`, `Date`.
  - Arithmetic `+ - * /`, comparisons, `and`/`or`/`not`, parens, `pow(b,e)`, **`min(a,b)`/`max(a,b)`** (the only clamp — there is no `if`), duration funcs `minutes_between`/`hours_between`/`days_between`, and **`prev(field)` / `prev(field, seed)`**.
  - `prev()` reads the PREVIOUS row of an ordered series and is excluded from the cycle guard (so `active = prev(active) + new - churned` is legal).
- **Rollups:** `field.computed.rollup = { entity, via, match?, window? }`. `match` is sibling aggregation (both rows point at a shared parent). `window` is a declarative SUMIFS in two directions — spanning rows (`from`/`to`/`against`) or dated rows (`at`/`within`); bounds may be dates or numbers; an empty bound is always OPEN.
- **Evaluation:** `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/AppDataService.cs` (**2,018 lines**), section `// --- computed fields (expr + rollup) ---` at ~line 1403. Key methods: `ComputeOwnRollups`, `RecomputeParentRollups`, `RecomputeAffectedSeries`, `RecomputeSeries`, `WindowBoundsAreStable`, `RecomputeBatch`. The series rule: *a series partitioned by P is disturbed by a write to P, and by a write to anything else that references P.* `entity.series.partition` declares it.
- **String counterpart:** `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/DerivedFields.cs` — a *closed* set (`companyDedupKey`, `companyCode`), deliberately not an expression language, because the values back unique indexes.

### Commands

`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/CommandExecutor.cs` (179 lines). Order is exact:

> permission → guard (`when`) → process-transition legality → input validation → one record write (input + state) → workflow dispatch → command effects → run log

`CommandResult` returns `Msg` codes, not sentences (localized by the controller); `successMessage` is app content resolved as a template. Grants: commands are **deny-by-default** — `role.grants[].commands` must list the key or `["*"]`.

Schema: `command = { key, label, icon, entity, description, placements, style, when, busy, input, confirm, effects, successMessage, emits }`. `busy` is the "button with state" for background work. `emits` names domain events.

### Processes

`command`/`process` canonicalization: `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/AppCompiler.cs` (`CanonicalizeProcesses`, `SynthesizeCommands`) + `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ProcessCommands.cs` (the shared naming rule, so the gate can validate references to commands the compiler has not yet created).

Schema: `process = { key, entity, stateField, initialState, states[], transitions[] }`.
- `state = { key, label, color, terminal, phase }` where `phase ∈ not_started|active|done|cancelled` (drives generic renderer semantics — late-start, overdue, done affordance).
- `transition = { key, label, from[], to, command?, when?, requiredFields[] }`.
- `stateField` must be the `role:"status"` select field; its options are derived from the states. A process-governed field must not have `default` — `initialState` is that.

### Workflows

`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/WorkflowEngine.cs` (207 lines) — in-process trigger→condition→effect. Effects run sequentially, best-effort. Cascades bounded by `EngineChain` in `Engine/Effects.cs`: `MaxDepth = 5` plus a once-only `workflowKey|recordId` set.

Triggers: `record.created`, `record.updated`, `record.deleted` (require `entity`); `field.changed` (requires `entity` + `field`, derived from the update before/after diff); `schedule` (requires `cron` + `entity`). Scheduled dispatch lives at `backend/AppBuilder.Platform/Jobs/ScheduledWorkflows.cs` and `Jobs/ScheduledWorkflowHandler.cs` — that one is Platform-side.

`RecordEvent` carries `Before`/`After` images, `ActorName`, `EventId`.

### Conditions & templates

- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/ConditionEvaluator.cs` (159 lines) — shared by `command.when`, `transition.when`, `workflow.when`. Nested `all`/`any`, or a leaf `{ field | path, operator, value, endField? }`. Operators: `eq neq gt gte lt lte contains in notIn isEmpty isNotEmpty between overlaps`. `path` hops **one** relation. A malformed condition evaluates to `false`, never throws.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/TemplateResolver.cs` (81 lines) — `{{record.<field>}}`, `{{actor.id}}`, `{{actor.name}}`, `{{app.name}}`, `{{today}}`, `{{now}}`, `{{source.<field>}}` (createForEach), plus offsets like `{{today+7}}`. Grammar shared with `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ExprTokens.cs` so the gate validates exactly what resolves. Unknown tokens → empty string.

### Effects — split across two projects (important)

Runtime (`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/`), no external I/O:
- `DataEffectExecutors.cs` — `UpdateRecordExecutor` (`target: "self"` or `{field}`; `set` with literals/templates/`pick`; `setIfEmpty`) and `createRecord`
- `CreateForEachExecutor.cs` (210 lines) — source is `{entity, filters}` or `{range: {from, count, ...}}`; **copies, never tracks**; idempotent via `key`
- `PickResolver.cs` (123 lines) — `{ pick: { entity, filters, sort, field } }`; blanks sort first ascending (never-taken-a-turn is most overdue); empty match leaves the field alone

Platform (`backend/AppBuilder.Platform/Effects/`) — these are the ones your generator has to substitute:
- `NotifyEffectExecutor.cs` (in-app notifications → `Notifications.cs`)
- `EmailEffectExecutor.cs` (→ `Email.cs`, `RecipientLocale.cs`)
- `WebhookEffectExecutor.cs` (https-only, host allowlist enforced at runtime)
- `EnrichEffectExecutor.cs` (queues a background research job — platform-only, see §5)

### Permissions

- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/PermissionEvaluator.cs` (161 lines) — `PermissionEvaluator.Evaluate(roles, roleKeys, entityKey) → EntityAccess`. Pure, immutable, computed from the definition's `roles`; no request/DB state. `EntityAccess` has `Create/Read/Update/Delete`, `CanReadField`, `CanUpdateField`, `CanRunCommand`, `HiddenReadFields`, `WriteRestrictedFields`, plus `Full`/`None`/`ReadOnly` singletons. Owner/platform-admin bypass entirely.
- Schema: `role = { key, name, description, grants[] }`; `grant = { entity ("*" allowed), create, read, update, delete, commands[], fieldOverrides[{field, read, update}] }`.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/FieldProjection.cs` (73 lines) — **read this one carefully.** Field-level read enforcement across *three* channels: the record itself, a command's `successMessage` template, and an effect's `detail` string. The header documents the bug that produced it: CRUD stripped hidden fields, commands did not. Effects still execute against the *full* record — the projection is caller-facing only.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Security/AppAccessResolver.cs` — HTTP-side resolution (handle → app → caller relationship → `EntityAccess`), shared by the data and commands controllers.

### Runtime REST surface (what your generated app must expose)

`backend/AppBuilder.Api/Controllers/AppRuntimeController.cs` — `[Route("api/app/{handle}")]`:
`GET manifest`, `GET data/{entity}`, `GET data/{entity}/aggregate`, `GET data/{entity}/{id}`, `POST data/{entity}`, `PUT data/{entity}/{id}`, `DELETE data/{entity}/{id}`, `GET openapi.json`, `POST ai/records`.

`backend/AppBuilder.Api/Controllers/AppCommandsController.cs` — same route base:
`POST commands/{entity}/{key}/{recordId}`, `POST commands/{entity}/{key}`, `GET access`, `GET history/{entity}/{id}`, `GET events`, `GET runs/{entity}/{id}`.

`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/OpenApiFromManifest.cs` (125 lines) generates the OpenAPI doc straight from the manifest — useful precedent for your generator, since entities are property bags with no CLR types.

### Frontend (Vue) — what you'd be regenerating

`web/` is Vue 3.5 + **Vuetify 4** + Pinia 4 + vue-router 4 + chart.js + SignalR + oidc-client-ts, built with Vite 8.
- `web/src/views/` — **68 files**, the block renderer: `BlockRenderer.vue`, `BlockFrame.vue`, `Prim*.vue` (Board, Box, Calendar, Cell, Chart, Control, ExternalEmbed, FilterBar, Form, Gantt, Leaf, OrgChart, RelatedApps, Repeat, Split, Stat, Table, Timeline), `TableView.vue`, `KanbanView.vue`, `DashboardView.vue`, `CalendarView.vue`, `TimelineView.vue`, `HistoryBlock.vue`, `ProcessBlock.vue`, `CommandDialog.vue`, `RecordForm.vue`, `SettingsForm.vue`, `WidgetsGrid.vue`
- `web/src/ui/` — 29 primitives (`UiDataTable`, `UiRefPicker`, `UiPeek`, `UiSelect`, …)
- `web/src/blockspec/` — `blocks.js`, `schema.js`, `tree.js`, `vocab.js`: **block introspection read directly out of `$defs.block_<kind>`.** Adding a kind to `schema/src/ui.json` makes it appear in the palette/inspector with no code change. Shared by `/editor` and the personal-view editor. This is the single most reusable asset for a Vue generator.
- Authoring-vs-canonical kind mapping: `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/BlockKinds.cs` (dotted `layout.row` → flat `row`; only at the model boundary).

---

## 5. Platform-only features in the definition JSON

### Cross-app references — `targetApp` / `targetEntity`

Only **2 occurrences** in the schema (both on `field`), but 35 uses across the reference corpus:

```json
{ "key": "organization", "type": "reference",
  "targetApp": "core_organizations", "targetEntity": "organization",
  "onDelete": "setNull" }
```

`targetApp` values in practice: `"platform"` ×29, `"core_organizations"` ×7. `"platform"` means a canonical platform entity from `schema/platform-entities.json` (`person`/`department`/`group`); anything else is another app's **`systemKey`** (never its handle) and is grant-gated.

Runtime handling — `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/AppDataService.cs` lines 841, 959–962, 1098–1106, 1392, 1442, 1567, 1619:
- `targetApp == "platform"` → resolution returns null (runtime can't reach the directory)
- other `targetApp` → resolved only via `DataContext.CoreApps` (a `systemKey → appId` map supplied by the caller, because the runtime deliberately cannot read the control plane). No map = accepted unvalidated.
- **Every rollup, series-partition walk and reference-hop explicitly skips fields with a non-null `targetApp`** (`f["targetApp"] is not null` guards). Cross-app references are pointers only — they never participate in computation.

`AppCompiler.cs` lines 477, 504, 547 similarly skip them for subordination/detail synthesis.

Registry: `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/CoreAppRegistry.cs` + `schema/core/registry.json`.

### `relatedApps` block

`$defs.block_relatedApps` = `{ kind: "relatedApps", label?, empty?, visibleWhen?, grow?, width? }`. **Nothing is named and nothing is configured.** The server walks every built app in the workspace for reference fields targeting this record's entity, re-checking the reader's grants per app.

Implementation: `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Services/RecordLinksService.cs` + `Controllers/RecordLinksController.cs`. Renderer: `web/src/views/PrimRelatedApps.vue`.

**This is unimplementable in a standalone single-app generator** — it is inherently a multi-app workspace scan. Zero occurrences in the reference corpus, so dropping it is cheap.

### `history` block

`$defs.block_history` = `{ kind: "history", label?, limit? (default 30, max 200), visibleWhen?, grow?, width? }`. *"Fed by the runtime automatically — no entity, no fields and no authoring beyond placing the block."*

Backing stores, all in `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/`:
- `FieldHistoryStore.cs` — `FieldChange(Id, TenantId, AppId, Entity, RecordId, Field, From, To, Actor, At, Kind)`. The before-image the runtime already computes, kept instead of discarded. Best-effort: losing an audit row never fails the write.
- `AppEventStore.cs` (241 lines) — append-only domain event log. Two names per event: `Type` (technical — `record.created`, `process.state_entered`) and `SemanticType` (domain — `deal.won`). Carries `Cause`, `CorrelationId`, `CausationId`.
- `EngineLogStore.cs` — `EngineRun` per command invocation / workflow firing, with per-effect outcomes.

All three are Npgsql-backed but sit behind interfaces (`IFieldHistoryStore`, `IEngineLogStore`) with in-memory implementations. **Reimplementable.** One occurrence in the corpus.

### AI blocks — there are none

No `block_ai`, no `block_assistant`. AI in the definition JSON is exactly two things:

1. **`effect: { type: "enrich", target: "self", kind: "full"|"refresh" }`** — queues a background public-web research run. Zero occurrences in the reference corpus. Implementation is a large Platform-only subtree: `backend/AppBuilder.Platform/Enrichment/` (~45 files — connectors, resolvers, corpus builder, embeddings, fact verification) + `Effects/EnrichEffectExecutor.cs` + `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Controllers/EnrichmentController.cs`. It writes `enr_*` fields (`enr_legal_name`, `enr_domain`, `enr_provenance`, `enr_differs`, …) — see `Enrichment/EnrichmentWriter.cs`.
2. **`field.role: "unconfirmed"` / `"differs"`** — a `json` field (max one each per entity) listing field keys the system wrote rather than a person, and an object of field-key → the value the system found where it disagrees with a human. The runtime clears a key the moment a human write touches it. This is *provenance metadata*, and it is cheap and worth keeping.

Also `POST api/app/{handle}/ai/records` on `AppRuntimeController` — an AI-assisted record creation endpoint.

The rest of the AI story (co-creation, design agent, blueprints) lives entirely outside the definition JSON, in `AppBuilder.Generator` and `AppBuilder.Platform`.

### Other platform-shaped constructs to watch

- `field.derived: "companyDedupKey" | "companyCode"` — server-filled; `companyDedupKey` does German normalization (Müller = mueller) in `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/DerivedFields.cs`
- `field.role: "publicShare" | "publicToken"` — the public perimeter (`PublicFormsController`, `PublicBookingController`, `AppBuilder.AccessTokens`)
- Forms archetype roles: `order`, `answerType`, `answerValue`, `answerRequired`, `answerOptions`, `respondentEmail`, `confirmMode`, `targetEntity`, `mapsTo` — driving `block_intake` / `block_answers` and `FormSubmissionService`
- `block_widgets` — the untyped KPI array; deliberately has no authoring name (deprecate-by-omission), but stays canonically legal
- `block_hub` (20 occurrences — the most-used non-trivial block), `block_settings`, `block_orgchart`, `block_externalEmbed`
- `plugins[]` / `$defs.pluginRef` — `{ id, version?, config? }`; only 1 occurrence in the corpus and it is `"plugins": []`
- `entity.kind: "collection" | "config" | "settings"` — nav placement; `settings` is a singleton rendered as a grouped form, never a table

---

## 6. Where published App Definitions live, and how `cord publish` ships one

### Database (the hosted product)

`backend/AppBuilder.ControlPlane/App.cs`:
- **`App`** — `Id` (GUID, stable), `TenantId`, `OwnerId`, `Handle` (per-tenant public address), `Name`, `Status`, `Version`, `SystemKey`, `IsCore`, `CoreMemberRole`, `Visibility`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, `BuiltAt`, `BuiltVersion`, **`Definition` (jsonb string)**, `Versions`
- **`AppVersion`** — `{ Id, AppId, Version, Definition, CreatedAt }`, a snapshot written whenever `Version` changes
- **`CoreAppState`** — per-tenant reconciliation record for core apps

Access: `backend/AppBuilder.Platform/AppStore.cs` (412 lines, EF Core via `IDbContextFactory<ControlPlaneDbContext>`), mapping `AppRecord` ↔ `App`. Compiled **manifests** live separately as files: `appdata/runtime/{appId}/app.json` via `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/RuntimeStore.cs` (`/appdata/` is gitignored).

### `cord publish`

1. `backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Commands/PublishCommand.cs` — resolves the app selection, **builds from source, never from `.cord/`** (a cache is not an authority). Runs `Pipeline.Check` on every selected app **before sending any of them** (all-or-nothing across the workspace, so cross-app references never half-resolve). Bar is *Coherent*, not *Valid* — incomplete apps publish with reasons printed; broken ones don't publish at all. Stops at the first refusal.
2. `backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Remote/Instance.cs` → `PublishAsync` → `POST api/apps/publish` with `{ definition, force }`. Credentials from `backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Remote/Credentials.cs` (`cord login`).
3. `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Controllers/AppsController.cs` line ~291, `[HttpPost("publish")]`:
   - requires `definition.key` (the identity across publishes)
   - `Gate.Validate(def)` → 422 on failure
   - upsert by key within the tenant; new apps take the key **as the handle verbatim** (409 `app.handle_taken` if occupied — no silent suffixing)
   - refuses an unchanged `version` unless `force`, **unless** `DefinitionHash.Of(snapshot) == DefinitionHash.Of(def)` — a byte-identical republish is a reported no-op, so idempotent CI re-runs pass
   - then **builds**: `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Services/AppBuilds.cs` → `Gate.Validate` → `AppSchemaVersion.Stamp` → `AppCompiler.Compile` → `TenantSchemaProvisioner.Provision` → stamp `storage` into the manifest → `RuntimeStore` persist → mark built. Same sequence as the Studio Build button and co-creation Publish.
   - returns `{ ok, id, handle, name, version, created, builtAt, entities }`

Version policy: `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Services/AppRelease.cs` — first publish keeps the declared version; every publish after that is a patch bump. `IsPublished` reads `BuiltVersion`, never `Version`.

`cord build` (`backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Commands/BuildCommand.cs`) writes to `.cord/build/<key>/`:
```
app.definition.json    manifest.json    diagnostics.json
```
`diagnostics.json` deliberately holds everything that must **not** influence the hashed artifacts (real `builtAt`, `cordVersion`, `valid`, `incomplete`, `fills`) — that separation is what makes the other two byte-identical across runs. Written atomically via `Workspace/AtomicFile.cs`. `.cord/` is generated and gitignored.

### Demo apps' definitions

**They are JSON files in the repo, loaded by a Python script.**

- `exploration/reference/*.appdef.json` — **14 hand-maintained reference apps** (9.5 KB – 87 KB): `sales-crm` (86.9 KB, largest), `ventures` (67.2 KB), `people-hr` (43.6 KB), `helpdesk` (34.3 KB), `task-manager`, `room-booking`, `invoicing`, `recruiting`, `timesheets`, `expenses`, `payroll`, `finance`, `time-off`. These are the conformance corpus — `backend/AppBuilder.Definition.Tests/Corpus.cs` enrols every file in this directory into the gate suite, `AppBuilder.Cord.Tests` (round-trip + coverage) and `AppBuilder.Runtime.Tests` (compile + pipeline) simultaneously.
- `schema/examples/crm.appdef.json` — the canonical example, also in the maintained corpus.
- `schema/examples/tests/generated/01-14*.appdef.json` — model-generated fixtures.
- `schema/examples/invalid/broken.appdef.json` — deliberately invalid.
- `exploration/budget-planner.appdef.json` (224.6 KB) — the largest definition in the repo; the authority for `examples/semantic/budgetPlanner/`.
- `exploration/cord/apps/*.{appdef,cord}.json` — paired App Definition + Cord document for three apps (budget-model, crm-pipeline, expense-approval), the Cord round-trip fixtures.
- `backup/appdefs-20260806/cordango__*.appdef.json` — a DB dump (18 apps + `_all-apps.json` + `_all-app-versions.json`); useful as real published-state samples.
- **Loader: `demo/load.py`** (22.6 KB) — `POST /api/apps/import` per definition, then seeds from `demo/seed/<appkey>.seed.json` (16 files) through the normal data API, then sets home widgets from `demo/home/<first>.widgets.json`. Value tokens: `@entity:key`, `@app.entity:key`, `@person:first`, `{T±n}`, `{M-1:05}`, `{NOW}`. Everything deterministic, **no AI tokens**. Also `demo/check_seed.py`, `demo/derive_core_people.py`, `demo/WORLD.md`.

---

## Practical notes for your generator

**Take these near-verbatim** (all in `AppBuilder.Definition`, one NuGet package, zero project refs):
`DefinitionHash.cs` (37 lines), `ComputedExpr.cs` (565), `ExprTokens.cs`, `Gate.cs` (3,296), `Normalizer.cs` (256), `Schemas.cs` (530), `ProcessCommands.cs`, `BlockKinds.cs`, `CoreAppRegistry.cs`.

**Port from `AppBuilder.Runtime`** (adds only Npgsql + Localization):
`AppCompiler.cs` (1,134), `PostgresStorage.cs` (220), `TenantSchemaProvisioner.cs` (224), `PermissionEvaluator.cs` (161), `FieldProjection.cs` (73), `ConditionEvaluator.cs` (159), `TemplateResolver.cs` (81), `PickResolver.cs` (123), `CreateForEachExecutor.cs` (210), `DerivedFields.cs` (150), `OpenApiFromManifest.cs` (125). The hard one is `AppDataService.cs` at 2,018 lines — the computed/rollup/series recompute cascade is the densest logic in the repo and has no smaller equivalent.

**Three semantic gaps you must design around, not port:**
1. The runtime is **manifest-driven and dynamic** — every entity is a `JsonObject` property bag resolved through the manifest's stamped `storage` block. A conventional ASP.NET Core app wants POCOs + EF + typed controllers. That inversion is your whole design problem, and the schema-per-tenant + `{handle}__{entity}` naming exists precisely because dynamic tables can't come from a static EF model (`AppBuilder.Runtime.csproj` says so).
2. **`relatedApps` cannot be generated** — it is a workspace-wide reverse-reference scan across other apps' grants.
3. **`enrich` and the notify/email/webhook executors live in `AppBuilder.Platform`**, not Runtime. You need substitutes (or stubs) for all four.

**Three assets that make the job much easier than it looks:**
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord.slnx` / `backend/AppBuilder.Oss.slnx` — the extraction boundaries already exist as *runnable tests*, with `AppBuilder.Cord.Tests/BoundaryTests.cs` failing the build if the dependency direction inverts.
- `Pipeline.DeterministicBuiltAt = UnixEpoch` + `diagnostics.json` separation — the determinism discipline you need is already established and tested.
- `web/src/blockspec/` — the Vue block palette/inspector is *already* driven by reading `$defs.block_<kind>` out of the schema at runtime. A Vue emitter can follow the same introspection strategy instead of hand-writing 41 block templates.

I have a complete map. Here is the report.

---

# App Definition Pipeline — Map for a Standalone Source Generator

## 1. The App Definition schema

**Location:** `schema/` at the repo root — a real folder, checked in, **and** embedded as a resource.

| Path | Size | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `schema/app-definition.schema.json` | **~213 KB**, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, `$id: https://appbuilder.dev/schemas/app-definition/2.0` | **The composed contract.** The only artifact anything downstream consumes. Generated, but checked in. |
| `schema/src/root.json` | 8.8 KB | Envelope + metadata/archetype/plugins; primitives (`identifier`, `fieldPath`, `filter`, `condition` refs) |
| `schema/src/domain.json` | 32.5 KB | `entities`, `relations` |
| `schema/src/ui.json` | **137.5 KB** | `presentation`, `views`, `pages`, `theme` + the whole 41-kind block system |
| `schema/src/behavior.json` | 28.7 KB | `processes`, `commands`, `workflows`, `condition`, `effect` |
| `schema/src/notifications.json` | 1.4 KB | `effect_notify`, `effect_email` |
| `schema/src/security.json` | 2.6 KB | `roles` |
| `schema/compose.py` | — | `src/*.json` → composed file. `--check` is the CI drift guard. |
| `schema/platform-entities.json` | 4.7 KB | Canonical platform entities (`person`, `department`, `group`) — the `targetApp: "platform"` model |
| `schema/core/registry.json` + `core_*.vN.json` | — | Core apps (`core_people` v1, `core_organizations` v1–v4, `core_calendar` v1–v2) — every shipped version retained |
| `schema/README.md` | — | Authoritative prose on the contract, incl. the explicit "JSON Schema can't do referential integrity, so a semantic validator is a required separate layer" |

**Top-level properties** (required: `schemaVersion`, `key`, `name`, `version`, `entities`):

```
schemaVersion  key  name  version  description  archetype  plugins
entities  relations  presentation  views  pages  theme
processes  commands  workflows  roles
```

**81 `$defs`.** Notable groups:
- Domain: `entity`, `field`, `relation`, `fieldPath`, `filter`, `sort`, `groupBy`
- Behavior: `process`, `command`, `workflow`, `condition`, `effect` + 7 typed effect defs
- Security: `role`
- UI: `view`, `page`, `tab`, `tile`, `theme`, `presentation`, `screenState`, `formBlock`, `visibleWhen`, `deepLink`, `combine`, `statMax`, `timeAxis`, plus **41 `block_*` defs** (`block_view`, `block_tabs`, `block_hub`, `block_grid`, `block_repeat`, `block_stat`, `block_board`, `block_gantt`, `block_orgchart`, `block_history`, `block_relatedApps`, `block_intake`, `block_answers`, `block_externalEmbed`, …)

The block union uses `allOf` / `if`/`then` `const` dispatch (never `unevaluatedProperties` — the composer asserts this; it crashes the JsonSchema.Net host).

**Cocreation contract — yes, present and frozen:** `schema/cocreation/contract.md` (frozen 2026-08-11, v1.1), plus `answer.schema.json`, `artifacts.schema.json` (15 KB), `exchange.schema.json`, `question.schema.json`, `session-state.schema.json`, `sketch.schema.json`, and 14 worked `examples/bp-*.json`. This is the request/response contract between the co-creation backend and `web/src/studio/cocreation/**`, with a byte-identical mirror in `web/`. It is orthogonal to your generator — it governs the authoring conversation, not the app artifact. Three of its files are embedded into `AppBuilder.Generator` (see its `.csproj`).

Also: `schema/blueprint.schema.json` (46.9 KB) — a **separate language** from the App Definition, describing what the user approved in their own vocabulary; lowered into an App Definition by `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Blueprint/BlueprintLowering.cs`.

---

## 2. What "compilation" exists today

There are **three** distinct compilations. This matters a lot for your plan.

### (a) Cord DSL → App Definition (`AppBuilder.Cord`)

There **is** a DSL→AppDefinition compiler, and it is deliberately deterministic and dependency-free.

- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordLower.cs` — `CordApp` → App Definition. Pure, deterministic, and explicitly documented as *"a function of the model ALONE"* — it may never read the definition it came from, a DB, or anything else.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordImport.cs` (+ `CordImportBehaviour.cs`, `CordImportScreens.cs`) — the reverse direction.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordSource.cs` — splits/joins the app into per-aggregate documents; `Join(Split(d)) == d` is a test.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordApp.cs`, `CordDocument.cs`, `CordTransaction.cs`, `CordOps*.cs` — the semantic model and operation vocabulary.
- Syntax lives outside Cord: `backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Workspace/Yaml.cs` owns YAML, `AppFolder.cs` owns the filesystem. Extension: `.cord.yaml`.

Today the **App Definition JSON is still the stored/authored artifact** and Cord is derived from it. `CordLower.cs`'s own header states the intent to invert that: *"the eventual open-source story wants `*.cord` to stand on its own as source with the App Definition demoted to a compiled deployment artifact."*

Worked example: `examples/semantic/budgetPlanner/` — the full Budget Planner in **both** `.cord.yaml` and `.cord.ts` form, with `coverage.json` recording authority hashes and `verify.py` proving exact reconstruction.

Coverage escape hatch: `exploration/cord/raw-allowlist.json` pins every place Cord still carries a raw App Definition fragment instead of modelling it (asserted exactly, not as a subset).

### (b) App Definition → runtime manifest (`AppCompiler`)

`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/AppCompiler.cs` (**1,134 lines**) — the piece your generator most directly parallels. `AppCompiler.Compile(definition, appId, builtAt)` produces a *manifest*, a different shape that is deliberately **not** re-validated against the App Definition schema. What it adds:

- injects base/system fields on every entity (`id` leading; `company_id`, `app_id`, `created_at/by`, `updated_at/by`, `deleted_at`, `record_state` trailing)
- `FlagComputedFields` — marks computed fields read-only/server-owned
- `CanonicalizeProcesses` — derives status-field options from process states, stamps `governedBy`
- `SynthesizeCommands` — creates a command for every command-less transition (naming rule shared with the gate via `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ProcessCommands.cs`)
- `FlagCommandOwnedFields` — fields collected by a command's `input` become non-editable in generic forms
- `InferSubordination` (parent/child IA), `InferConfigEntities` (lookup tables → "Configuration" nav group)
- `DefaultViews`, `DefaultTableColumns`, detail/page synthesis
- stamps `AppSchemaVersion.Stamp` (`"2.0"`; runtime refuses non-`2.` majors)

### (c) Validation — where it lives

**Project:** `AppBuilder.Definition`, **namespace** `AppBuilder.Definition`.

- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Gate.cs` — **3,296 lines**. The class is `Gate`.
  - `Gate.StructuralErrors(JsonNode)` — JSON Schema evaluation with a *hierarchical* walk that prunes valid branches (so failed `if` probes and losing `oneOf` siblings don't produce phantom errors)
  - `Gate.StructuralErrors(JsonNode, JsonNode schema)` — arbitrary-schema overload for tool payloads
  - `Gate.SemanticErrors(JsonNode)` — referential integrity, unique keys, reachability, behavior-layer rules (the behavior section alone spans ~lines 936–2999)
  - `Gate.Validate(JsonNode)` — structural + semantic, the entry point everything calls
  - `Gate.PageErrors`, `Gate.PresetErrors`, `Gate.DesignErrors`
  - `Gate.BaseFields` — the canonical base-field set, shared with `AppCompiler`
  - Documented as a **port of the Python `generator/gate.py`**, so `exploration/generator/gate.py` + the Python examples are the cross-language conformance corpus.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Normalizer.cs` — pre-gate deterministic repair (double-encoded JSON sections, envelope unwrapping, tolerant duplicate-key parsing, authoring-kind lowering)
- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/Schemas.cs` — loads embedded schemas; hosts `AppSchemaVersion` (`Current = "2.0"`, `SupportedMajor = "2."`)
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/CandidateValidator.cs` — the *full* pipeline in one uninterruptible call: `parse → Gate.Validate → DesignDefaults fills → Gate.Validate again → AppCompiler.Compile → smoke checks → hash`. Distinguishes **Coherent** (gate-clean + compiles) from **Valid** (also a finished app). Only `Valid` yields a hash.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Workspace/Pipeline.cs` — `Pipeline.Check(LoadedApp)` → `CheckReport`. Wraps `CandidateValidator` for the CLI. **Never spends a token or opens a socket.** Uses `Pipeline.DeterministicBuiltAt = DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch` so equal source produces byte-equal artifacts.

### DefinitionHash

`backend/AppBuilder.Definition/DefinitionHash.cs` — **37 lines**, trivially portable:

```csharp
public static string Of(JsonNode? node) => OfText(Canonical(node)?.ToJsonString() ?? "null");
public static string OfText(string s) => Convert.ToHexStringLower(SHA256.HashData(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(s)));
public static JsonNode? Canonical(JsonNode? node)   // recursively orders object keys ordinally; array order preserved
```

SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex. Key-order-independent (definitions round-trip through a `jsonb` column, which reorders keys); **array order is meaningful and preserved** (field order drives column and render order). A content-only variant excluding `version` lives at `backend/AppBuilder.Api/Services/AppRelease.cs` → `AppRelease.ContentHash`.

---

## 3. The C# model classes — the key finding

**There are no POCO model classes for AppDefinition.** `grep -rn "class AppDefinition|record AppDefinition"` across `backend/` returns nothing. The entire pipeline operates on `System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode` / `JsonObject`. Every one of the 39 files in `AppBuilder.Definition` that touches a definition uses `JsonNode`.

The typed records that *do* exist are for adjacent concerns:
- `ComputedValue`, `ComputedExprValidation` in `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ComputedExpr.cs`
- `CoreApp`, `CoreAppVersion`, `CoreEntity` in `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/CoreAppRegistry.cs`
- The **Cord semantic model** in `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/CordApp.cs` — `CordEntity`, `CordProcess`, `CordTransition`, `CordAction`, etc. This is the closest thing to a typed object graph over an app, and it is a *different, smaller* vocabulary than the App Definition.
- `AppRecord` in `backend/AppBuilder.Platform/AppRecord.cs` — DTO whose `Definition` is a `JsonNode?`

### Reusability in isolation: excellent

`backend/AppBuilder.Definition/AppBuilder.Definition.csproj`:
- **Zero project references.**
- **One package: `JsonSchema.Net` 9.2.2.**
- `net10.0`, nullable enabled.
- Embeds `app-definition.schema.json`, `platform-entities.json`, `blueprint.schema.json`, `schema/core/*.json`.

No EF, no ASP.NET, no Npgsql, no provider client. `backend/AppBuilder.Cord/AppBuilder.Cord.csproj` references only `AppBuilder.Definition` and calls that ItemGroup *"RULE 0 — this project is independently extractable, and this ItemGroup is the whole claim."* `backend/AppBuilder.Cord.Tests/BoundaryTests.cs` asserts the compiled assembly's reference set against an allowlist.

Two solution files encode the boundaries you care about:
- `backend/AppBuilder.Cord.slnx` — `{Definition, Cord, Cord.Tests}`. "THE EXTRACTION TEST, as a runnable command rather than a claim… must pass with no database, no containers, no Platform and no Generator."
- `backend/AppBuilder.Oss.slnx` — adds `Localization`, `AccessTokens`, `Runtime`, `Cli`. "THE INSTALLABLE PRODUCT BOUNDARY… no Api, no Worker, no ControlPlane, no Generator, no Platform."

`AppBuilder.Runtime` adds only `Npgsql` 10.0.3 + `AppBuilder.Localization` — no EF. So `{Definition, Cord, Runtime, Cli}` is a clean, ASP.NET-free base for a standalone generator.

**Note the naming trap:** `backend/AppBuilder.Generator/` is **not** a code generator — it is the LLM/agent layer (`Providers.cs`, `Prompts*.cs`, `DesignSession.cs`, `CoCreationTools.cs`, `CordToolAdapter.cs`). Your project needs a different name.

---

## 4. Runtime semantics a generator must reimplement

### Entity storage — typed Postgres tables, schema-per-tenant. Not jsonb.

- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/PostgresStorage.cs` (220 lines) — pure naming + type mapping, no I/O. Schema = `tenant_{id}`. Table = `{handle}__{entity}`, with `{handle}_{appId8}__{entity}` and `a{appId}__{entity}` collision fallbacks. 63-char Postgres identifier limit enforced.
  - `PgTypeFor`: `integer`→`bigint`, `decimal`/`money`→`numeric`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`→`timestamptz`, `multiselect`→`text[]`, `json`→`jsonb`; everything else (`text`, `longtext`, `email`, `url`, `phone`, `select`, `reference`, `attachment`, `uuid`) → text. `id` is `text PRIMARY KEY`.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/TenantSchemaProvisioner.cs` (224 lines) — `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS`, one typed table per entity, live-migrates by ADDing missing columns only (never drops or retypes). Creates **partial unique indexes** (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`) for `unique` fields. Returns the `storage` block `{engine, tenant, schema, tables}` stamped into the manifest — the store resolves through that stamp, never by re-deriving names.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/PostgresEntityStore.cs` (445 lines), `IEntityStore.cs`, `InMemoryEntityStore.cs` — the seam. Records are `JsonObject` property bags; there is no CLR type per entity. Both stores must return identical results for the same `EntityQuery` (pinned by a test).
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/RuntimeStore.cs` — built manifests at `{dataDir}/runtime/{appId}/app.json` (see `appdata/runtime/`, gitignored).

### Computed expressions

- `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ComputedExpr.cs` (565 lines) — a small typed language shared by gate and runtime; **same AST for parse and eval**, so a gate-accepted expression cannot mean something different at runtime. Expressions are data, never handed to an evaluator. Types: `Number`, `Boolean`, `Date`.
  - Arithmetic `+ - * /`, comparisons, `and`/`or`/`not`, parens, `pow(b,e)`, **`min(a,b)`/`max(a,b)`** (the only clamp — there is no `if`), duration funcs `minutes_between`/`hours_between`/`days_between`, and **`prev(field)` / `prev(field, seed)`**.
  - `prev()` reads the PREVIOUS row of an ordered series and is excluded from the cycle guard (so `active = prev(active) + new - churned` is legal).
- **Rollups:** `field.computed.rollup = { entity, via, match?, window? }`. `match` is sibling aggregation (both rows point at a shared parent). `window` is a declarative SUMIFS in two directions — spanning rows (`from`/`to`/`against`) or dated rows (`at`/`within`); bounds may be dates or numbers; an empty bound is always OPEN.
- **Evaluation:** `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/AppDataService.cs` (**2,018 lines**), section `// --- computed fields (expr + rollup) ---` at ~line 1403. Key methods: `ComputeOwnRollups`, `RecomputeParentRollups`, `RecomputeAffectedSeries`, `RecomputeSeries`, `WindowBoundsAreStable`, `RecomputeBatch`. `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/CommandExecutor.cs` (179 lines). Order is exact:

> permission → guard (`when`) → process-transition legality → input validation → one record write (input + state) → workflow dispatch → command effects → run log

`CommandResult` returns `Msg` codes, not sentences (localized by the controller); `successMessage` is app content resolved as a template. Grants: commands are **deny-by-default** — `role.grants[].commands` must list the key or `["*"]`.

Schema: `process = { key, entity, stateField, initialState, states[], transitions[] }`.
- `state = { key, label, color, terminal, phase }` where `phase ∈ not_started|active|done|cancelled` (drives generic renderer semantics — late-start, overdue, done affordance).
- `transition = { key, label, from[], to, command?, when?, requiredFields[] }`.
- `stateField` must be the `role:"status"` select field; its options are derived from the states. A process-governed field must not have `default` — `initialState` is that.

`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/WorkflowEngine.cs` (207 lines) — in-process trigger→condition→effect. Effects run sequentially, best-effort. Cascades bounded by `EngineChain` in `Engine/Effects.cs`: `MaxDepth = 5` plus a once-only `workflowKey|recordId` set.

`RecordEvent` carries `Before`/`After` images, `ActorName`, `EventId`.

- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/ConditionEvaluator.cs` (159 lines) — shared by `command.when`, `transition.when`, `workflow.when`. Nested `all`/`any`, or a leaf `{ field | path, operator, value, endField? }`. Operators: `eq neq gt gte lt lte contains in notIn isEmpty isNotEmpty between overlaps`. `path` hops **one** relation. A malformed condition evaluates to `false`, never throws.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/TemplateResolver.cs` (81 lines) — `{{record.<field>}}`, `{{actor.id}}`, `{{actor.name}}`, `{{app.name}}`, `{{today}}`, `{{now}}`, `{{source.<field>}}` (createForEach), plus offsets like `{{today+7}}`. Grammar shared with `backend/AppBuilder.Definition/ExprTokens.cs` so the gate validates exactly what resolves. Unknown tokens → empty string.

### Effects — split across two projects (important)

Runtime (`backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/Engine/`), no external I/O:
- `DataEffectExecutors.cs` — `UpdateRecordExecutor` (`target: "self"` or `{field}`; `set` with literals/templates/`pick`; `setIfEmpty`) and `createRecord`
- `CreateForEachExecutor.cs` (210 lines) — source is `{entity, filters}` or `{range: {from, count, ...}}`; **copies, never tracks**; idempotent via `key`
- `PickResolver.cs` (123 lines) — `{ pick: { entity, filters, sort, field } }`; blanks sort first ascending (never-taken-a-turn is most overdue); empty match leaves the field alone

Platform (`backend/AppBuilder.Platform/Effects/`) — these are the ones your generator has to substitute:
- `NotifyEffectExecutor.cs` (in-app notifications → `Notifications.cs`)
- `EmailEffectExecutor.cs` (→ `Email.cs`, `RecipientLocale.cs`)

- `backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/PermissionEvaluator.cs` (161 lines) — `PermissionEvaluator.Evaluate(roles, roleKeys, entityKey) → EntityAccess`. Pure, immutable, computed from the definition's `roles`; no request/DB state. `EntityAccess` has `Create/Read/Update/Delete`, `CanReadField`, `CanUpdateField`, `CanRunCommand`, `HiddenReadFields`, `WriteRestrictedFields`, plus `Full`/`None`/`ReadOnly` singletons. The header documents the bug that produced it: CRUD stripped hidden fields, commands did not. Effects still execute against the *full* record — the projection is caller-facing only.

### Runtime REST surface (what your generated app must expose)

`GET manifest`, `GET data/{entity}`, `GET data/{entity}/aggregate`, `GET data/{entity}/{id}`, `POST data/{entity}`, `PUT data/{entity}/{id}`, `DELETE data/{entity}/{id}`, `GET openapi.json`, `POST ai/records`.
