## New OSS projects (design summary)

### `Cordango.SourceGen` — SDK + runner (no target knowledge)

```csharp
public record CompilerInfo(string Id, string Version);
public record CompiledAppArtifact(          // the ONE canonical input, built only by the CLI
    JsonObject Definition,                  // from Pipeline.Check — the pair can never mismatch
    JsonObject Manifest,
    string DefinitionHash,
    CompilerInfo Compiler);

public record GenerateRequest(CompiledAppArtifact App, JsonObject Options);
public record GeneratedFile(string RelativePath, string? Content, string? ContentBase64 = null);
public record Diagnostic(string Code, string Message, string? JsonPath);
public record GenerateResult(IReadOnlyList<GeneratedFile> Files,
    IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Warnings, IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Errors);

public interface IAppSourceGenerator {
    string Id { get; }                      // "dotnet-vue"
    string Version { get; }
    GeneratorCapabilities Capabilities { get; }
    GenerateResult Generate(GenerateRequest request);
}
```

- The CLI is the **only** construction site of `CompiledAppArtifact` (from `Pipeline.Check` output) — a mismatched Definition/Manifest is structurally impossible; no second IR is created.
- `GeneratorCapabilities` = declarative data (bools + sets); **one** shared `TargetValidator.Validate(definition, capabilities)` walks the definition Gate-style.
- **CORD21xx catalogue** (greenfield): 2100 cross-app ref, 2101 relatedApps, 2102 history, 2103 enrich, 2104 series, 2105 prev(), 2106 windowed rollup, 2107 unsupported effect, 2108 unsupported trigger, 2109 unsupported platform target, 2110 AI feature, 2111 unsupported block kind, 2112 unsupported field type. Every code carries the JSON path. **Never silently dropped.**
- **Runner** (CLI-side): ordinal sort by RelativePath; reject absolute paths/`..`/drive-colons, normalize `\`→`/`, `Path.GetFullPath` prefix re-check; UTF-8 no BOM, `\n`, AtomicFile pattern; refuses a non-empty output dir unless it holds a previous `cordango.build.json`, then deletes exactly that manifest's files first (deterministic overwrite).
- **`cordango.build.json`**: `{protocolVersion, definitionHash, compiler{id,version}, generator{id,version}, scaffoldVersion, controlsVersion, partial, unsupportedCapabilities[{code,path,feature}], files[{path,sha256}]}` — no timestamps, GUIDs, machine paths. **`--allow-partial-ui` scars the metadata permanently** (`partial: true` + the full list) and the generated README gets a prominent "Partial build" section — a knowingly partial app can never pass as a full build later.
- **Protocol reserved now, adapter later**: external generator = exe; `--describe` → `{protocolVersion:1, id, version, capabilities}`; generate = request JSON stdin → result JSON stdout; `ExternalProcessGenerator : IAppSourceGenerator` built late.

### `Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue` — the generator

Input = `CompiledAppArtifact` (manifest supplies canonical processes, synthesized commands, computed flags, base fields, default views — never re-derived). Pure emitters `(artifact, options) → IEnumerable<GeneratedFile>`.

**Backend shape follows the TCDev.APIGenerator pattern** (generic machinery once in the scaffold, thin generated types per entity):

- **Generated per entity**: POCO implementing `IObjectBase<string>` (definition ids are `text` per `PostgresStorage`; not Guid) + `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<T>)` (table/column names snake_case, required/unique/partial-unique indexes, FKs + delete behavior, type mapping mirroring `PostgresStorage.cs:63-72`: integer→long, decimal/money→decimal, boolean→bool, date→DateOnly, datetime→DateTimeOffset, multiselect→List<string>/text[], json→JsonDocument/jsonb, else string) + lifecycle-hook classes (`IBeforeCreate<T>`/`IBeforeUpdate<T>`-style) carrying computed-field recompute, validation, and command-owned-field enforcement + `AppPermissions.cs` (roles/grants/fieldOverrides/commands as typed static data).
- **Scaffold-generic (written once, in `Cordango.Standalone`)**: generic CRUD controller over `IObjectBase<TKey>` (MVC attribute-routed, house style), generic repository/data service, `CordangoDbContext` doing `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` + auto-registration of unmapped types (GenericDbContext pattern, minus tenant filtering — one app, no tenancy), field-level projection + write-restriction enforcement wired through `Cordango.Authorization`, CSRF, error `{code,error}` mapping.
- **Migrations, EF-native**: the generator invokes **EF Core's own design-time `MigrationsScaffolder` in-process** (Npgsql provider, EF version pinned by the scaffold) with a **pinned migration id** `00000000000001_InitialCreate` — EF authors the migration + snapshot, determinism holds (same model + same EF version → same output; Determinism.Tests enforce). Startup runs `Database.Migrate()`. App evolution after generation = the user's own `dotnet ef migrations add`, documented in the generated README. No hand-rolled snapshot writer.
- Base fields from the manifest **minus `company_id`/`app_id`** (one app, no tenancy).
- **Commands/processes**: manifest's canonicalized processes + synthesized commands → generated `CommandService` (permission → guard → transition legality → input validation → write → events → effects) + state-field validation; command endpoints on the generic controller (`POST .../commands/{key}`).
- **Workflows/effects**: generated `WorkflowRegistrations.cs` + effect methods (updateRecord/createRecord/createForEach via DbContext); scaffold provides post-SaveChanges `RecordEvents` dispatcher, `ScheduleHostedService`, `INotificationService` (table + endpoint), `IEmailSender` (SMTP; log-only dev), `IWebhookSender` (HMAC optional). Condition + template evaluation = the **shared `Cordango.Semantics` implementations** (vendored source), not reimplementations.
- **Computed/rollups**: reuse `Cordango.Definition.ComputedExpr` AST → C# methods; generated dependency table drives scaffold `RecomputeService` (synchronous write-path recompute + transitive parent rollups, depth-guarded). **v1 supports** arithmetic/comparison/boolean, min/max, field refs, single hop, plain rollups (count/sum/avg/min/max). **v1 rejects** prev()/series/windowed rollups (2105/2104/2106) — zero corpus uses.
- **Vue**: one explicit `src/pages/<PascalKey>Page.vue` per manifest page composed from `@cordango/web-controls` + generated api-client modules + router/nav shell. Tier-B blocks → CORD2111 or `--allow-partial-ui` card + metadata scar. Scaffold chrome en+de; definition labels pass through.
- **Seeds — dataset-deterministic by default**: moved `SeedPlan`/`SeedRows` give ordering + grid joins; new `SeedSynthesizer` with PRNG seeded from `(seedValue, entityKey, fieldKey, rowIndex)`, embedded wordlists, states spread across process states, references drawn from seeded pools. `seed/seed.json` records a **fixed anchor date derived deterministically from the seed value** plus relative tokens (demo/load.py grammar: `@entity:key`, `{T+3}`); scaffold `SeedRunner` resolves against the recorded anchor → **definition + seed = same dataset, always**. `--seed-date today` explicitly re-anchors at apply time and is the documented non-reproducible mode.
- **Also emitted**: multi-stage Dockerfile (node build → dotnet → runtime serving SPA from wwwroot), docker-compose.yml (app + pinned postgres), app README (incl. Partial-build section when scarred), small generated test project, `cordango.build.json`.

### `Cordango.Standalone` — the scaffold

Two parts: (a) the **generic API machinery** above (real compiled code, unit-tested in the repo), (b) **static app files** embedded as resources (`Scaffold.Version`, `Scaffold.Files()`; only `{{AppName}}/{{AppKey}}` substitution): ASP.NET Core host (MVC, health+DB check, ILogger), **auth = ASP.NET Core Identity + cookie** for the same-origin SPA+API — with **antiforgery enforced globally on ALL mutating requests** (`AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken` global filter + XSRF cookie/header pattern for the SPA client), SameSite=Lax, login/logout/users/password-reset (via IEmailSender), **local org module** (Organizations, People, Departments, Groups — EF entities + controllers + Vue pages, shapes derived from `schemas/platform-entities.json` + `core_organizations`), `LocalFileStore` + media controller for attachments, en+de, `{code,error}` wire.

**S6 opens with an APIGenerator reuse assessment** (timeboxed): read TCDev.APIGenerator core + Data + Identity and decide per piece **adopt as dependency / absorb code / pattern only**. Default expectation: absorb the generic-controller + GenericDbContext + lifecycle-hook pattern into `Cordango.Standalone` (Cordango-owned, trimmed, net10, no OData/GraphQL/RabbitMQ; our permission model is definition-driven role/field grants rather than scope attributes); take more if the code proves directly liftable. Findings recorded in `oss/cordango/docs/`.

**Platform-ref mapping**: `platform.person→People`, `platform.department→Departments`, `platform.group→Groups`, `core_organizations.organization→Organizations`, `core_organizations.contact→People`; anything else → CORD2109.

# Cordango OSS split + standalone source generator

## Context

Tim's architecture document establishes the next product direction: alongside the existing platform, an open-source toolchain that takes a compiled App Definition JSON and **generates a complete, conventional, standalone application** (ASP.NET Core + EF Core + PostgreSQL + Vue 3 + Vuetify) that the user owns and deploys anywhere. The OSS/commercial boundary: OSS builds **one app** (auth, permissions, local Organizations/People/Departments/Groups, commands, processes, workflows, deterministic seeds); the platform keeps multi-app, cross-app, audit/history, AI, enrichment, platform search, marketplace, managed ops.

Three GitHub repos **already exist** (private until launch): `https://github.com/cordango/cordango` (OSS monorepo), `https://github.com/cordango/web-controls` (`@cordango/web-controls`), `https://github.com/cordango/examples`. They get mounted into AppBuilder as **git submodules** so all work happens here but is committed to the separate repos from day one — the separation is physical, not aspirational.

Branch: `CLI-CodeGen` (freshly cut from main, no work started).

## Decisions locked with Tim

1. **Submodules now** at `oss/cordango`, `oss/web-controls`, `oss/examples` (umbrella avoids the root `examples/` clash; one compose mount covers all three).
2. **Existing portable core moves now**: Definition + Cord + AccessTokens + Cli leave `backend/`, renamed `AppBuilder.*` → `Cordango.*`, into Tim's specified monorepo tree.
3. **CLI binary renames `cord` → `cordango` now**, **and the workspace format renames too**: `cord.yaml` → `cordango.yaml`, `.cord.yaml` → `.cordango.yaml`, `.cord/` → `.cordango/` (one-time legacy reads; zero external users make this the last cheap moment). Token prefixes `cord_pat`/`cord_cxt` do NOT rename (server wire format, issued tokens).
4. **Both run tracks live**: `cordango run` (local interpreted platform simulation, CordyOSS §7 packaged-Postgres track, for platform users) stays on the roadmap, **not scheduled here** and not blocked by anything here. This plan builds the standalone generator track.
5. **Tier-B UI blocks** (timeline, gantt, scheduling, planning, orgchart, intake, embeds): v1 rejects with CORD2111; `--allow-partial-ui` demotes to warning + visible "not supported" card **and a permanent scar in build metadata** (below).
6. **Historical model-generated fixtures publish** into the monorepo test fixtures.
7. **Repos private until launch** → migration is mechanical (dropped Blueprint layer moves along); one deliberate **pre-publication hygiene pass** later (not in these slices).
8. **EF/backend generation follows Tim's TCDev.APIGenerator pattern** (DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api): generic scaffold machinery + thin generated per-entity types, EF-native automated migrations. Details below; S6 opens with a reuse assessment of the APIGenerator codebase itself.

## Review corrections folded in (Tim, 2026-08-20)

- **One canonical generator input** (`CompiledAppArtifact`), never independently supplied Definition + Manifest.
- **Seeds are dataset-deterministic by default** (fixed anchor date); `--seed-date today` is the explicit non-reproducible mode.
- **No reimplemented permission/template semantics** — pure semantic cores are extracted into shared OSS components; platform and standalone both wrap the same implementation.
- **CSRF covers every cookie-authenticated mutation** (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), not just account endpoints.
- **`AppCompiler.CompilerId` stays `appbuilder-runtime/0.1`** — a repo extraction must not mutate platform state; branding is display-only, the fingerprint changes only when compiler behavior changes.
- **`--allow-partial-ui` leaves a scar** in `cordango.build.json` + a prominent generated-README section.
- **Cross-repo moves are not `git mv`**: filesystem move → `git add` in the submodule → `git rm` in the parent → independent commits (both Tim's) → parent submodule-pointer bump.

## Verified facts the design rests on (file:line evidence)

- **The Runtime split is clean**: the compile layer — `AppCompiler.cs`, `CandidateValidator.cs`, `OpenApiFromManifest.cs`, `SeedPlan.cs`, `SeedRows.cs` — imports only `System.Text.Json(.Nodes)` + `AppBuilder.Definition` ([CandidateValidator.cs:1-3](backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/CandidateValidator.cs#L1-L3)); the smoke step is pure JSON walks, no stores/engine. `DesignDefaults` already lives in Definition. `PermissionEvaluator.cs` (161 lines) and `FieldProjection.cs` (73) are pure; `ConditionEvaluator.cs`/`TemplateResolver.cs` look pure (verify at move; if not, split the pure core out).
- **CLI flag parser** hard-codes value-taking flags `app, scope, ops, out, instance, token` at [Cli.cs:96](backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Cli.cs#L96) — `target` and `seed` must be added. Dispatch switch duplicated in `Cli.Tests/Sandbox.cs:60-80`.
- **Definition embeds schemas by relative path** (`..\..\schema\...`, Link + LogicalName, plus `<Watch>` items) — [AppBuilder.Definition.csproj:16-40](backend/AppBuilder.Definition/AppBuilder.Definition.csproj#L16-L40). Paths survive a coordinated move; schema edits require an api/worker restart (embedded at build — the 2026-07-14 stale-schema incident).
- **Docker**: api mounts `./backend`, `./schema`, `./appdata` ([docker-compose.yml:123-126](docker-compose.yml#L123-L126)); worker same (~226-229); ops has **zero** ProjectReferences (no new mount); editor mounts the repo root (sees `oss/` for free); web mounts only `./web`.
- **Corpus**: `Corpus.cs:30` anchors RepoRoot on `schema/app-definition.schema.json`; counts are **floors** (`>= 15` semantic, `>= 10` historical in `CordRoundTripTests.cs:139-141`), not exact; the exact pin is `exploration/cord/raw-allowlist.json` (`CordCoverageTests.cs:190`). 13 reference apps + crm + budget-planner.
- **Capability grounding**: `prev()`, `series`, windowed rollups, `relatedApps`, `enrich` have **zero** uses across `exploration/reference/`; `history` appears once (ventures). `targetApp` in the corpus is only `"platform"` (28×) and `"core_organizations"` (7×).
- **CLI uses no Localization** — after the compile layer moves, the OSS repo needs no Localization; it stays platform-side.
- **Blueprint tests can't move**: their fixtures come from `bench/corpus/development/**` (private benchmark corpus) — blueprint **code** moves with Definition, blueprint **tests** relocate to `backend/AppBuilder.Generator.Tests`.
- **AccessTokens** consumers: exactly Api and Cli. **AppBuilder.Generator is the AI layer** — the naming trap the `Cordango.SourceGen*` names avoid.
- **TCDev.APIGenerator** (Tim's net-dynamic-api, commit 4279e35): `[Api("/people", ApiMethodsToGenerate.All, authorize: true, requiredReadScopes/WriteScopes)]` on POCOs implementing `IObjectBase<TKey>`; `GenericDbContext.OnModelCreating` = `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(asm)` for all discovered assemblies + `builder.Entity(type)` for unmapped types; lifecycle hooks (`IBeforeCreate<T>.BeforeCreate(...)`); generic CRUD controllers per attributed type; pluggable providers (Postgres/SQL/SQLite); Identity/OData/GraphQL as separate modules.

---

## Target end-state

### `cordango/cordango` (mounted `oss/cordango/`)

```
oss/cordango/
├── src/
│   ├── Cordango.Compiler/          # Definition + Cord + compile files + shared semantics, ONE project

│   │                     alongside the ComputedExpr shared parse+eval precedent)

│   ├── Cordango.SourceGen/         # generator SDK: contracts, capabilities, validator, runner, protocol
│   ├── Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue/  # the first-party generator (emitters + vendored controls dist)
│   └── Cordango.Standalone/        # scaffold: generic API machinery + embedded static files
├── schemas/                        # app-definition.schema.json, src/, core/, platform-entities.json,
│                                   # blueprint.schema.json, compose.py, validate.py, README.md
├── samples/
│   ├── reference/                  # the 13 *.appdef.json (from exploration/reference)
│   ├── crm.appdef.json             # from schema/examples
│   ├── budget-planner.appdef.json  # from exploration/
│   └── semantic/budgetPlanner/     # CordSource specimen (from root examples/semantic)
├── tests/

├── docs/  LICENSE(Apache-2.0)  README.md  Cordango.slnx  Directory.Build.props  .gitignore

**Key mapping decisions**
- **One merged `Cordango.Compiler` project** (matches Tim's tree; Cord's only dep was Definition; layering survives as namespaces + a namespace-scoped tripwire in the restated BoundaryTests). Zero ProjectReferences, one PackageReference (JsonSchema.Net 9.2.2), embeds `..\..\schemas\...` with the **same LogicalNames**, Watch items follow.
- **`Cordango.Authorization`** = the pure grant-resolution + field-projection semantics moved out of Runtime (Tim's "Authorization.Core" component). Platform `AppBuilder.Runtime` references it (adapter); the standalone scaffold wraps the **same implementation** — vendored as source into generated apps (provenance headers) until NuGet packages exist. One semantic implementation, never two conformance-tested twins. Same treatment for condition/template semantics via `Cordango.Semantics`.
- `Cordango.Cli.csproj`: refs AccessTokens + Compiler (+ SourceGen from S4) — **the Runtime wart dies**. YamlDotNet stays.

- **Credentials migration** (Cordango.Cli): resolution `CORDANGO_CONFIG_DIR` → `CORD_CONFIG_DIR` (compat) → `%APPDATA%\cordango`; `Load()` falls back to reading `%APPDATA%\cord\credentials.json` when the new path is empty (read-only, same FormatVersion guard); `Flush()` writes only the new path. Test via env-var override.
- **Workspace format rename** (full): loader accepts `cord.yaml`/`.cord.yaml` as legacy and reports them via `doctor`/`fmt`; `new`/scaffold/save write only `cordango.yaml`/`.cordango.yaml`; build dir `.cordango/`; `.gitignore` templates updated. Ripples: `WorkspaceFile.cs`, `AppFolder.cs`, `Templates/Scaffold.cs`, Cli.Tests, budgetPlanner specimen files, `exploration/cord/apps` fixtures, `bench/cord_run.py`, docs spellings.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Oss.slnx` and `backend/AppBuilder.Cord.slnx` **are deleted** — superseded by `oss/cordango/Cordango.slnx` (the physical extraction test: must build/test from a standalone clone). Their header-comment intent moves to the submodule README.
- Submodule `Directory.Build.props` mirrors backend's obj/bin redirect keyed on **`CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT`**, including the do-not-set-for-tests warning.

### Move mechanics (applies to every migration slice)

`oss/*` are separate repositories — a cross-repo move is **never `git mv`**. Per batch: filesystem move/copy → `git add` inside the submodule → `git rm` (delete) in the parent → **two independent commits, both Tim's** → parent commit also bumps the submodule pointer. Fresh history in the public repos is the accepted consequence (and the history-hygiene guarantee: AppBuilder's history never leaves the private repo).

### What stays in AppBuilder

Root `examples/` empties (Tim deletes when convenient).

---

## New OSS projects (design summary)

### `Cordango.SourceGen` — SDK + runner (no target knowledge)

```csharp
public record CompilerInfo(string Id, string Version);
public record CompiledAppArtifact(          // the ONE canonical input, built only by the CLI
    JsonObject Definition,                  // from Pipeline.Check — the pair can never mismatch
    JsonObject Manifest,
    string DefinitionHash,
    CompilerInfo Compiler);

public record GenerateRequest(CompiledAppArtifact App, JsonObject Options);
public record GeneratedFile(string RelativePath, string? Content, string? ContentBase64 = null);
public record Diagnostic(string Code, string Message, string? JsonPath);
public record GenerateResult(IReadOnlyList<GeneratedFile> Files,
    IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Warnings, IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Errors);

public interface IAppSourceGenerator {
    string Id { get; }                      // "dotnet-vue"
    string Version { get; }
    GeneratorCapabilities Capabilities { get; }
    GenerateResult Generate(GenerateRequest request);
}
```

- The CLI is the **only** construction site of `CompiledAppArtifact` (from `Pipeline.Check` output) — a mismatched Definition/Manifest is structurally impossible; no second IR is created.
- `GeneratorCapabilities` = declarative data (bools + sets); **one** shared `TargetValidator.Validate(definition, capabilities)` walks the definition Gate-style.
- **CORD21xx catalogue** (greenfield): 2100 cross-app ref, 2101 relatedApps, 2102 history, 2103 enrich, 2104 series, 2105 prev(), 2106 windowed rollup, 2107 unsupported effect, 2108 unsupported trigger, 2109 unsupported platform target, 2110 AI feature, 2111 unsupported block kind, 2112 unsupported field type. Every code carries the JSON path. **Never silently dropped.**
- **Runner** (CLI-side): ordinal sort by RelativePath; reject absolute paths/`..`/drive-colons, normalize `\`→`/`, `Path.GetFullPath` prefix re-check; UTF-8 no BOM, `\n`, AtomicFile pattern; refuses a non-empty output dir unless it holds a previous `cordango.build.json`, then deletes exactly that manifest's files first (deterministic overwrite).
- **`cordango.build.json`**: `{protocolVersion, definitionHash, compiler{id,version}, generator{id,version}, scaffoldVersion, controlsVersion, partial, unsupportedCapabilities[{code,path,feature}], files[{path,sha256}]}` — no timestamps, GUIDs, machine paths. **`--allow-partial-ui` scars the metadata permanently** (`partial: true` + the full list) and the generated README gets a prominent "Partial build" section — a knowingly partial app can never pass as a full build later.
- **Protocol reserved now, adapter later**: external generator = exe; `--describe` → `{protocolVersion:1, id, version, capabilities}`; generate = request JSON stdin → result JSON stdout; `ExternalProcessGenerator : IAppSourceGenerator` built late.

### `Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue` — the generator

Input = `CompiledAppArtifact` (manifest supplies canonical processes, synthesized commands, computed flags, base fields, default views — never re-derived). Pure emitters `(artifact, options) → IEnumerable<GeneratedFile>`.

**Backend shape follows the TCDev.APIGenerator pattern** (generic machinery once in the scaffold, thin generated types per entity):

- **Generated per entity**: POCO implementing `IObjectBase<string>` (definition ids are `text` per `PostgresStorage`; not Guid) + `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<T>)` (table/column names snake_case, required/unique/partial-unique indexes, FKs + delete behavior, type mapping mirroring `PostgresStorage.cs:63-72`: integer→long, decimal/money→decimal, boolean→bool, date→DateOnly, datetime→DateTimeOffset, multiselect→List<string>/text[], json→JsonDocument/jsonb, else string) + lifecycle-hook classes (`IBeforeCreate<T>`/`IBeforeUpdate<T>`-style) carrying computed-field recompute, validation, and command-owned-field enforcement + `AppPermissions.cs` (roles/grants/fieldOverrides/commands as typed static data).
- **Scaffold-generic (written once, in `Cordango.Standalone`)**: generic CRUD controller over `IObjectBase<TKey>` (MVC attribute-routed, house style), generic repository/data service, `CordangoDbContext` doing `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` + auto-registration of unmapped types (GenericDbContext pattern, minus tenant filtering — one app, no tenancy), field-level projection + write-restriction enforcement wired through `Cordango.Authorization`, CSRF, error `{code,error}` mapping.
- **Migrations, EF-native**: the generator invokes **EF Core's own design-time `MigrationsScaffolder` in-process** (Npgsql provider, EF version pinned by the scaffold) with a **pinned migration id** `00000000000001_InitialCreate` — EF authors the migration + snapshot, determinism holds (same model + same EF version → same output; Determinism.Tests enforce). Startup runs `Database.Migrate()`. App evolution after generation = the user's own `dotnet ef migrations add`, documented in the generated README. No hand-rolled snapshot writer.
- Base fields from the manifest **minus `company_id`/`app_id`** (one app, no tenancy).
- **Commands/processes**: manifest's canonicalized processes + synthesized commands → generated `CommandService` (permission → guard → transition legality → input validation → write → events → effects) + state-field validation; command endpoints on the generic controller (`POST .../commands/{key}`).
- **Workflows/effects**: generated `WorkflowRegistrations.cs` + effect methods (updateRecord/createRecord/createForEach via DbContext); scaffold provides post-SaveChanges `RecordEvents` dispatcher, `ScheduleHostedService`, `INotificationService` (table + endpoint), `IEmailSender` (SMTP; log-only dev), `IWebhookSender` (HMAC optional). Condition + template evaluation = the **shared `Cordango.Semantics` implementations** (vendored source), not reimplementations.
- **Computed/rollups**: reuse `Cordango.Definition.ComputedExpr` AST → C# methods; generated dependency table drives scaffold `RecomputeService` (synchronous write-path recompute + transitive parent rollups, depth-guarded). **v1 supports** arithmetic/comparison/boolean, min/max, field refs, single hop, plain rollups (count/sum/avg/min/max). **v1 rejects** prev()/series/windowed rollups (2105/2104/2106) — zero corpus uses.
- **Vue**: one explicit `src/pages/<PascalKey>Page.vue` per manifest page composed from `@cordango/web-controls` + generated api-client modules + router/nav shell. Tier-B blocks → CORD2111 or `--allow-partial-ui` card + metadata scar. Scaffold chrome en+de; definition labels pass through.
- **Seeds — dataset-deterministic by default**: moved `SeedPlan`/`SeedRows` give ordering + grid joins; new `SeedSynthesizer` with PRNG seeded from `(seedValue, entityKey, fieldKey, rowIndex)`, embedded wordlists, states spread across process states, references drawn from seeded pools. `seed/seed.json` records a **fixed anchor date derived deterministically from the seed value** plus relative tokens (demo/load.py grammar: `@entity:key`, `{T+3}`); scaffold `SeedRunner` resolves against the recorded anchor → **definition + seed = same dataset, always**. `--seed-date today` explicitly re-anchors at apply time and is the documented non-reproducible mode.

### `Cordango.Standalone` — the scaffold

# Cordango OSS split + standalone source generator

## Context

Tim's architecture document establishes the next product direction: alongside the existing platform, an open-source toolchain that takes a compiled App Definition JSON and **generates a complete, conventional, standalone application** (ASP.NET Core + EF Core + PostgreSQL + Vue 3 + Vuetify) that the user owns and deploys anywhere. The OSS/commercial boundary: OSS builds **one app** (auth, permissions, local Organizations/People/Departments/Groups, commands, processes, workflows, deterministic seeds); the platform keeps multi-app, cross-app, audit/history, AI, enrichment, platform search, marketplace, managed ops.

Three GitHub repos **already exist** (private until launch): `https://github.com/cordango/cordango` (OSS monorepo), `https://github.com/cordango/web-controls` (`@cordango/web-controls`), `https://github.com/cordango/examples`. They get mounted into AppBuilder as **git submodules** so all work happens here but is committed to the separate repos from day one — the separation is physical, not aspirational.

Branch: `CLI-CodeGen` (freshly cut from main, no work started).

## Decisions locked with Tim

1. **Submodules now** at `oss/cordango`, `oss/web-controls`, `oss/examples` (umbrella avoids the root `examples/` clash; one compose mount covers all three).
2. **Existing portable core moves now**: Definition + Cord + AccessTokens + Cli leave `backend/`, renamed `AppBuilder.*` → `Cordango.*`, into Tim's specified monorepo tree.
3. **CLI binary renames `cord` → `cordango` now**, **and the workspace format renames too**: `cord.yaml` → `cordango.yaml`, `.cord.yaml` → `.cordango.yaml`, `.cord/` → `.cordango/` (one-time legacy reads; zero external users make this the last cheap moment). Token prefixes `cord_pat`/`cord_cxt` do NOT rename (server wire format, issued tokens).
4. **Both run tracks live**: `cordango run` (local interpreted platform simulation, CordyOSS §7 packaged-Postgres track, for platform users) stays on the roadmap, **not scheduled here** and not blocked by anything here. This plan builds the standalone generator track.
5. **Tier-B UI blocks** (timeline, gantt, scheduling, planning, orgchart, intake, embeds): v1 rejects with CORD2111; `--allow-partial-ui` demotes to warning + visible "not supported" card **and a permanent scar in build metadata** (below).
6. **Historical model-generated fixtures publish** into the monorepo test fixtures.
7. **Repos private until launch** → migration is mechanical (dropped Blueprint layer moves along); one deliberate **pre-publication hygiene pass** later (not in these slices).
8. **EF/backend generation follows Tim's TCDev.APIGenerator pattern** (DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api): generic scaffold machinery + thin generated per-entity types, EF-native automated migrations. Details below; S6 opens with a reuse assessment of the APIGenerator codebase itself.

## Review corrections folded in (Tim, 2026-08-20)

- **One canonical generator input** (`CompiledAppArtifact`), never independently supplied Definition + Manifest.
- **Seeds are dataset-deterministic by default** (fixed anchor date); `--seed-date today` is the explicit non-reproducible mode.
- **No reimplemented permission/template semantics** — pure semantic cores are extracted into shared OSS components; platform and standalone both wrap the same implementation.
- **CSRF covers every cookie-authenticated mutation** (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), not just account endpoints.
- **`AppCompiler.CompilerId` stays `appbuilder-runtime/0.1`** — a repo extraction must not mutate platform state; branding is display-only, the fingerprint changes only when compiler behavior changes.
- **`--allow-partial-ui` leaves a scar** in `cordango.build.json` + a prominent generated-README section.
- **Cross-repo moves are not `git mv`**: filesystem move → `git add` in the submodule → `git rm` in the parent → independent commits (both Tim's) → parent submodule-pointer bump.

Paths survive a coordinated move; schema edits require an api/worker restart (embedded at build — the 2026-07-14 stale-schema incident).

## New OSS projects (design summary)

### `Cordango.SourceGen` — SDK + runner (no target knowledge)

```csharp
public record CompilerInfo(string Id, string Version);
public record CompiledAppArtifact(          // the ONE canonical input, built only by the CLI
    JsonObject Definition,                  // from Pipeline.Check — the pair can never mismatch
    JsonObject Manifest,
    string DefinitionHash,
    CompilerInfo Compiler);

public record GenerateRequest(CompiledAppArtifact App, JsonObject Options);
public record GeneratedFile(string RelativePath, string? Content, string? ContentBase64 = null);
public record Diagnostic(string Code, string Message, string? JsonPath);
public record GenerateResult(IReadOnlyList<GeneratedFile> Files,
    IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Warnings, IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Errors);

public interface IAppSourceGenerator {
    string Id { get; }                      // "dotnet-vue"
    string Version { get; }
    GeneratorCapabilities Capabilities { get; }
    GenerateResult Generate(GenerateRequest request);
}
```

- The CLI is the **only** construction site of `CompiledAppArtifact` (from `Pipeline.Check` output) — a mismatched Definition/Manifest is structurally impossible; no second IR is created.
- `GeneratorCapabilities` = declarative data (bools + sets); **one** shared `TargetValidator.Validate(definition, capabilities)` walks the definition Gate-style.
- **CORD21xx catalogue** (greenfield): 2100 cross-app ref, 2101 relatedApps, 2102 history, 2103 enrich, 2104 series, 2105 prev(), 2106 windowed rollup, 2107 unsupported effect, 2108 unsupported trigger, 2109 unsupported platform target, 2110 AI feature, 2111 unsupported block kind, 2112 unsupported field type. Every code carries the JSON path. **Never silently dropped.**
- **Runner** (CLI-side): ordinal sort by RelativePath; reject absolute paths/`..`/drive-colons, normalize `\`→`/`, `Path.GetFullPath` prefix re-check; UTF-8 no BOM, `\n`, AtomicFile pattern; refuses a non-empty output dir unless it holds a previous `cordango.build.json`, then deletes exactly that manifest's files first (deterministic overwrite).
- **`cordango.build.json`**: `{protocolVersion, definitionHash, compiler{id,version}, generator{id,version}, scaffoldVersion, controlsVersion, partial, unsupportedCapabilities[{code,path,feature}], files[{path,sha256}]}` — no timestamps, GUIDs, machine paths. **`--allow-partial-ui` scars the metadata permanently** (`partial: true` + the full list) and the generated README gets a prominent "Partial build" section — a knowingly partial app can never pass as a full build later.
- **Protocol reserved now, adapter later**: external generator = exe; `--describe` → `{protocolVersion:1, id, version, capabilities}`; generate = request JSON stdin → result JSON stdout; `ExternalProcessGenerator : IAppSourceGenerator` built late.

### `Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue` — the generator

Input = `CompiledAppArtifact` (manifest supplies canonical processes, synthesized commands, computed flags, base fields, default views — never re-derived). Pure emitters `(artifact, options) → IEnumerable<GeneratedFile>`.

**Backend shape follows the TCDev.APIGenerator pattern** (generic machinery once in the scaffold, thin generated types per entity):

- **Generated per entity**: POCO implementing `IObjectBase<string>` (definition ids are `text` per `PostgresStorage`; not Guid) + `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<T>)` (table/column names snake_case, required/unique/partial-unique indexes, FKs + delete behavior, type mapping mirroring `PostgresStorage.cs:63-72`: integer→long, decimal/money→decimal, boolean→bool, date→DateOnly, datetime→DateTimeOffset, multiselect→List<string>/text[], json→JsonDocument/jsonb, else string) + lifecycle-hook classes (`IBeforeCreate<T>`/`IBeforeUpdate<T>`-style) carrying computed-field recompute, validation, and command-owned-field enforcement + `AppPermissions.cs` (roles/grants/fieldOverrides/commands as typed static data).
- **Scaffold-generic (written once, in `Cordango.Standalone`)**: generic CRUD controller over `IObjectBase<TKey>` (MVC attribute-routed, house style), generic repository/data service, `CordangoDbContext` doing `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` + auto-registration of unmapped types (GenericDbContext pattern, minus tenant filtering — one app, no tenancy), field-level projection + write-restriction enforcement wired through `Cordango.Authorization`, CSRF, error `{code,error}` mapping.
- **Migrations, EF-native**: the generator invokes **EF Core's own design-time `MigrationsScaffolder` in-process** (Npgsql provider, EF version pinned by the scaffold) with a **pinned migration id** `00000000000001_InitialCreate` — EF authors the migration + snapshot, determinism holds (same model + same EF version → same output; Determinism.Tests enforce). Startup runs `Database.Migrate()`. App evolution after generation = the user's own `dotnet ef migrations add`, documented in the generated README. No hand-rolled snapshot writer.
- Base fields from the manifest **minus `company_id`/`app_id`** (one app, no tenancy).
- **Commands/processes**: manifest's canonicalized processes + synthesized commands → generated `CommandService` (permission → guard → transition legality → input validation → write → events → effects) + state-field validation; command endpoints on the generic controller (`POST .../commands/{key}`).
- **Workflows/effects**: generated `WorkflowRegistrations.cs` + effect methods (updateRecord/createRecord/createForEach via DbContext); scaffold provides post-SaveChanges `RecordEvents` dispatcher, `ScheduleHostedService`, `INotificationService` (table + endpoint), `IEmailSender` (SMTP; log-only dev), `IWebhookSender` (HMAC optional). Condition + template evaluation = the **shared `Cordango.Semantics` implementations** (vendored source), not reimplementations.
- **Computed/rollups**: reuse `Cordango.Definition.ComputedExpr` AST → C# methods; generated dependency table drives scaffold `RecomputeService` (synchronous write-path recompute + transitive parent rollups, depth-guarded). **v1 supports** arithmetic/comparison/boolean, min/max, field refs, single hop, plain rollups (count/sum/avg/min/max). **v1 rejects** prev()/series/windowed rollups (2105/2104/2106) — zero corpus uses.
- **Vue**: one explicit `src/pages/<PascalKey>Page.vue` per manifest page composed from `@cordango/web-controls` + generated api-client modules + router/nav shell. Tier-B blocks → CORD2111 or `--allow-partial-ui` card + metadata scar. Scaffold chrome en+de; definition labels pass through.
- **Seeds — dataset-deterministic by default**: moved `SeedPlan`/`SeedRows` give ordering + grid joins; new `SeedSynthesizer` with PRNG seeded from `(seedValue, entityKey, fieldKey, rowIndex)`, embedded wordlists, states spread across process states, references drawn from seeded pools. `seed/seed.json` records a **fixed anchor date derived deterministically from the seed value** plus relative tokens (demo/load.py grammar: `@entity:key`, `{T+3}`); scaffold `SeedRunner` resolves against the recorded anchor → **definition + seed = same dataset, always**. `--seed-date today` explicitly re-anchors at apply time and is the documented non-reproducible mode.
- **Also emitted**: multi-stage Dockerfile (node build → dotnet → runtime serving SPA from wwwroot), docker-compose.yml (app + pinned postgres), app README (incl. Partial-build section when scarred), small generated test project, `cordango.build.json`.

### `Cordango.Standalone` — the scaffold

Two parts: (a) the **generic API machinery** above (real compiled code, unit-tested in the repo), (b) **static app files** embedded as resources (`Scaffold.Version`, `Scaffold.Files()`; only `{{AppName}}/{{AppKey}}` substitution): ASP.NET Core host (MVC, health+DB check, ILogger), **auth = ASP.NET Core Identity + cookie** for the same-origin SPA+API — with **antiforgery enforced globally on ALL mutating requests** (`AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken` global filter + XSRF cookie/header pattern for the SPA client), SameSite=Lax, login/logout/users/password-reset (via IEmailSender), **local org module** (Organizations, People, Departments, Groups — EF entities + controllers + Vue pages, shapes derived from `schemas/platform-entities.json` + `core_organizations`), `LocalFileStore` + media controller for attachments, en+de, `{code,error}` wire.

**S6 opens with an APIGenerator reuse assessment** (timeboxed): read TCDev.APIGenerator core + Data + Identity and decide per piece **adopt as dependency / absorb code / pattern only**. Default expectation: absorb the generic-controller + GenericDbContext + lifecycle-hook pattern into `Cordango.Standalone` (Cordango-owned, trimmed, net10, no OData/GraphQL/RabbitMQ; our permission model is definition-driven role/field grants rather than scope attributes); take more if the code proves directly liftable. Findings recorded in `oss/cordango/docs/`.

**Platform-ref mapping**: `platform.person→People`, `platform.department→Departments`, `platform.group→Groups`, `core_organizations.organization→Organizations`, `core_organizations.contact→People`; anything else → CORD2109.

input.content:
# Cordango

Cordango is an open application language and deterministic compiler for building complete business
applications. Define what your application should do, generate conventional source code, own it, and
deploy it anywhere.

There is no runtime dependency on Cordango in what you generate. No license server, no account, no
model API. The generated project is an ordinary ASP.NET Core and Vue application that keeps working
whether or not this project does.

> Status: pre-alpha. The standalone generator is under construction and nothing here is stable yet.

## What is in this repository

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `src/Cordango.Compiler` | The App Definition contract: schema gate, semantic validation, normalizer, the Cord semantic model, and the compiler that turns a definition into a runtime manifest. |
| `src/Cordango.Authorization` | Permission semantics: role grants, entity access, field-level read and write rules. One implementation, shared by every host. |
| `src/Cordango.AccessTokens` | The access token format used when the CLI talks to a Cordango instance. |
| `src/Cordango.Cli` | The `cordango` command. |
| `src/Cordango.SourceGen` | The generator SDK: capabilities, target validation, the file runner, the external generator protocol. |
| `src/Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue` | The first-party generator. ASP.NET Core, EF Core, PostgreSQL, Vue 3, Vuetify. |
| `src/Cordango.Standalone` | The scaffold every generated application is built on: authentication, authorization, Organizations, People, infrastructure. |
| `schemas/` | The App Definition JSON Schema and its composed sources. |
| `samples/` | Application definitions used as the conformance corpus. |
| `tests/` | Compiler, generator, determinism and compatibility suites. |

## The two products

Cordango Open Source builds **one application**. It has its own backend, frontend, database, users,
authentication, permissions, Organizations and People. It is not multi-tenant, it contains no AI at
runtime, and it belongs to whoever generated it.

Cordango Platform connects, operates and governs **many applications** as one company system: shared
people and organizations across apps, cross-app references, audit and record history, governance, AI,
search, marketplace and managed hosting. That is a separate, commercial product.

The same application definition works in both places. What differs is what each target supports, and
every target says so out loud rather than silently dropping what it cannot do.

## How it fits together

```
Human or AI
     |
Cordango source
     |
  compiler
     |
App Definition          the canonical contract
     |
     +----------------------+
     |                      |
Cordango Platform     Standalone generator
                            |
                     complete source project
                            |
                      deploy anywhere
```

## Determinism

The generator is deterministic. The same App Definition, generator version, scaffold version and
controls version produce the same files, byte for byte. No timestamps, no random identifiers, no
machine paths, no locale-dependent formatting in generated output. CI generates the same fixture
twice and compares.

Seed data works the same way. `cordango build --seed 42` produces the same dataset every time,
including dates. If you want data anchored to today instead, `--seed-date today` says so explicitly
and gives up reproducibility on purpose.

## Building

Requires the .NET 10 SDK.

```
dotnet build Cordango.slnx
dotnet test Cordango.slnx
```

The test suite needs no database, no containers and no network.

## License

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Source generated by this toolchain belongs to the person or organization that generated it and is not
covered by this license. Generate it, modify it, ship it.

CORDANGO is a trademark. The license covers the software, not the name.

<Project>

  <!--
    Where each project puts obj/ and bin/.

    THE PROBLEM THIS SOLVES. A host may bind-mount this repository into a container that runs
    `dotnet watch` while a developer also builds the same tree from the host. Both SDKs then build the
    SAME source into the SAME obj/ directories and corrupt each other: NuGet's
    `project.assets.json already exists`, and MSBuild's `ResolvePackageAssets` failing to read its own
    cache file.

    WITH CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT SET, intermediate and output paths move to a container-local volume and
    the bind-mounted tree is never written to. WITHOUT it (a developer's machine, CI, a plain clone),
    nothing changes and obj/bin sit where every .NET tool expects them.

    It has to live in Directory.Build.props rather than each .csproj: BaseIntermediateOutputPath is
    read during restore, before the SDK's own props are imported, and setting it any later is silently
    ignored for restore while still applying to build, which produces a worse failure than the one it
    fixes.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT)' != ''">
    <BaseIntermediateOutputPath>$(CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT)/$(MSBuildProjectName)/obj/</BaseIntermediateOutputPath>
    <BaseOutputPath>$(CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT)/$(MSBuildProjectName)/bin/</BaseOutputPath>

    <!--
      And exclude the CONVENTIONAL obj/bin, which is no longer excluded automatically.

      The SDK's default source glob skips $(BaseIntermediateOutputPath) and $(BaseOutputPath). Move
      those elsewhere and the ordinary ./obj suddenly looks like ordinary source: a container reading
      the bind-mounted tree compiles the host's leftover generated AssemblyInfo.cs alongside its own
      and fails with CS0579 "duplicate attribute", an error that names a file nobody wrote and points
      at neither cause.
    -->
    <DefaultItemExcludes>$(DefaultItemExcludes);obj/**;bin/**</DefaultItemExcludes>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    DO NOT set CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT to run TESTS. It is for app hosts only.

    `Corpus.RepoRoot()` finds the repository by walking up from the test assembly's location, so an
    output directory outside the repo makes it throw and takes every corpus-driven theory down with
    it. Said here because the failure names a missing repo root and gives no hint that an environment
    variable caused it.
  -->

</Project>

# @cordango/web-controls

Generic Vue 3 and Vuetify controls shared by Cordango Platform and by the standalone applications the
Cordango generator produces.

> Status: pre-alpha. Nothing here is published to npm yet and the surface changes without notice.

## What belongs here

Low-level building blocks that any business application needs and that carry no product opinion:

data table, form inputs, field renderer, reference picker, person picker, organization picker, board,
calendar, timeline, chart, process stepper, command button, money and date inputs, filter controls,
layout primitives.

## What does not belong here

Anything that only makes sense inside the commercial platform: audit center, AI assistant,
marketplace administration, governance, cross-app explorer, platform administration, platform search.
Those live in the product, not in a generic controls package.

Also deliberately absent: the REST client, the router, and any global store. A control never decides
where data comes from. Everything a control needs from its host arrives through the plugin options
or through props, which is what lets the same component serve a multi-tenant platform and a
single-tenant generated app without knowing which one it is in.

## Using it

```js
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { CordangoControls } from '@cordango/web-controls'
import '@cordango/web-controls/styles'

createApp(App).use(CordangoControls, {
  // The seams. Every one of these is optional and has a boring default.
  peopleDirectory,   // (ids) => Promise<Map<id, person>>
  isMe,              // (id) => boolean
  mediaUrl,          // (ref) => string
  tableSettings,     // per-user column preferences: { load, save }
  commandInvoker,    // { invoke, enabled }
})
```

Vue, Vuetify and vue-i18n are peer dependencies. The host owns those versions.

## Development

```
npm install
npm run build
npm test
```

Tests are plain `node --test` over the pure modules. Components are verified by the applications that
consume them rather than by a headless DOM here.

# @cordango/web-controls

Generic Vue 3 and Vuetify controls shared by Cordango Platform and by the standalone applications the
Cordango generator produces.

> Status: pre-alpha. Nothing here is published to npm yet and the surface changes without notice.

## What belongs here

Low-level building blocks that any business application needs and that carry no product opinion:

data table, form inputs, field renderer, reference picker, person picker, organization picker, board,
calendar, timeline, chart, process stepper, command button, money and date inputs, filter controls,
layout primitives.

## What does not belong here

Anything that only makes sense inside the commercial platform: audit center, AI assistant,
marketplace administration, governance, cross-app explorer, platform administration, platform search.
Those live in the product, not in a generic controls package.

Also deliberately absent: the REST client, the router, and any global store. A control never decides
where data comes from. Everything a control needs from its host arrives through the plugin options
or through props, which is what lets the same component serve a multi-tenant platform and a
single-tenant generated app without knowing which one it is in.

## Using it

```js
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { CordangoControls } from '@cordango/web-controls'
import '@cordango/web-controls/styles'

createApp(App).use(CordangoControls, {
  // The seams. Every one of these is optional and has a boring default.
  peopleDirectory,   // (ids) => Promise<Map<id, person>>
  isMe,              // (id) => boolean
  mediaUrl,          // (ref) => string
  tableSettings,     // per-user column preferences: { load, save }
  commandInvoker,    // { invoke, enabled }
})
```

Vue, Vuetify and vue-i18n are peer dependencies. The host owns those versions.

## Development

```
npm install
npm run build
npm test
```

Tests are plain `node --test` over the pure modules. Components are verified by the applications that
consume them rather than by a headless DOM here.

## License

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# Cordango examples

Complete Cordango application definitions you can read, generate, run and change.

> Status: pre-alpha. Definitions here track the App Definition schema in
> [cordango/cordango](https://github.com/cordango/cordango) and will move while that schema settles.

Every example is a real application, not a fragment: entities and relations, processes, commands,
workflows, permissions and screens. The same definition works two ways. Generate it into a standalone
project you own:

```
cordango build --app expenses --target standalone --out ./expenses-app
cd expenses-app
docker compose up
```

or install it into Cordango Platform, where it shares people, organizations and permissions with
every other app in the company.

## The examples

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `expenses/` | Expense claims with an approval process. The smallest complete example, and the one to read first. |
| `time-off/` | Absence requests, balances and a team calendar. |
| `task-manager/` | Projects, tasks and subtasks, with rollups from children to parents. |
| `room-booking/` | Rooms, bookings and conflict handling. |

## Contributing

Improvements to an example benefit everyone using it, in either environment. Useful contributions
include better field labels, more realistic permissions, missing states in a process, and clearer
screens.

Two things to check before opening a pull request:

```
cordango check --app <name>
cordango check --app <name> --target standalone
```

The first asks whether the definition is a valid Cordango application. The second asks whether it is
also compatible with the standalone generator, which supports less than the platform does and says
exactly what it cannot do.

## Relationship to the compiler repository

`cordango/cordango` carries its own `samples/` directory. That one is the conformance corpus: it is
pinned by the test suite and changes only when the contract does. This repository is the one meant
for people, and it is allowed to grow, improve and diverge.

## License

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="coverlet.collector" Version="6.0.4" />
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.14.1" />
    <PackageReference Include="xunit" Version="2.9.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="3.1.4" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Using Include="Xunit" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="..\AppBuilder.Definition\AppBuilder.Definition.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- The Python spec's example corpus = cross-language conformance fixtures. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <Content Include="..\..\schema\examples\crm.appdef.json" Link="fixtures\crm.appdef.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <Content Include="..\..\schema\examples\invalid\broken.appdef.json" Link="fixtures\broken.appdef.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <Content Include="..\..\schema\platform-entities.json" Link="fixtures\platform-entities.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <!-- Every hand-authored reference app (COMPOSITION_REFRAME_FINAL.md Phase 1 + the Cordango
         demo suite): the wildcard registers new apps automatically — ReferenceSuiteTests walks the
         whole folder, so dropping a new .appdef.json in is enough to pin it. -->
    <Content Include="..\..\exploration\reference\*.appdef.json" Link="fixtures\%(Filename)%(Extension)" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- The evaluation corpus. Hand-written blueprints are the M1 proof that the spec model can
       express each archetype at all, and the M2 input that must lower gate-clean. They live in
       bench/corpus so the benchmark and the tests measure the SAME artifacts — a fixture copied
       into the test project would drift from the corpus the moment either changed. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- `**` is load-bearing: with a single `*`, %(RecursiveDir) is EMPTY and all five archetypes
         would collide on one output path. The archetype directory name is the fixture's identity. -->
    <Content Include="..\..\bench\corpus\development\**\blueprint.json"
             Link="fixtures\blueprints\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)"
             CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <Content Include="..\..\bench\corpus\development\**\requirements.json"
             Link="fixtures\blueprints\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)"
             CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

content.text: `core.autocrlf=true` system-wide with no `.gitattributes` anywhere would hand a fresh Windows clone CRLF files and break the byte-determinism promise. Adding `.gitattributes` to all three repos.

input.content:
# Byte-for-byte determinism is a promise this repository makes, and a checkout that rewrites line
# endings quietly breaks it. The generator writes LF; Git for Windows ships core.autocrlf=true in its
# system config, so without this file a Windows clone hands those files back as CRLF and the
# double-generation comparison fails on a difference nobody introduced. Normalize in the repository
# AND in the working tree, on every platform, so "same inputs, same bytes" survives the clone.
* text=auto eol=lf

# Windows batch files are the one thing that genuinely needs CRLF.
*.cmd text eol=crlf
*.bat text eol=crlf

# Never touch these.
*.png  binary
*.jpg  binary
*.jpeg binary
*.gif  binary
*.ico  binary
*.pdf  binary
*.woff binary
*.woff2 binary
*.ttf  binary
*.otf  binary
*.zip  binary
*.snk  binary

    <Using Include="Xunit" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="..\AppBuilder.Definition\AppBuilder.Definition.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- The Python spec's example corpus = cross-language conformance fixtures. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <Content Include="..\..\schema\examples\crm.appdef.json" Link="fixtures\crm.appdef.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <Content Include="..\..\schema\examples\invalid\broken.appdef.json" Link="fixtures\broken.appdef.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <Content Include="..\..\schema\platform-entities.json" Link="fixtures\platform-entities.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <!-- Every hand-authored reference app (COMPOSITION_REFRAME_FINAL.md Phase 1 + the Cordango
         demo suite): the wildcard registers new apps automatically — ReferenceSuiteTests walks the
         whole folder, so dropping a new .appdef.json in is enough to pin it. -->
    <Content Include="..\..\exploration\reference\*.appdef.json" Link="fixtures\%(Filename)%(Extension)" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- The evaluation corpus. Hand-written blueprints are the M1 proof that the spec model can
       express each archetype at all, and the M2 input that must lower gate-clean. They live in
       bench/corpus so the benchmark and the tests measure the SAME artifacts — a fixture copied
       into the test project would drift from the corpus the moment either changed. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- `**` is load-bearing: with a single `*`, %(RecursiveDir) is EMPTY and all five archetypes
         would collide on one output path. The archetype directory name is the fixture's identity. -->
    <Content Include="..\..\bench\corpus\development\**\blueprint.json"
             Link="fixtures\blueprints\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)"
             CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
    <Content Include="..\..\bench\corpus\development\**\requirements.json"
             Link="fixtures\blueprints\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)"
             CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

"""Derive the core People app from the people_hr reference app by removing on/offboarding.

Done as a transform rather than by hand so the trim is auditable and the 6 surviving entities keep
their exact field definitions — retyping any of them later is a breaking change the compatibility
validator would reject, so v1 has to be right.
"""
import json, sys

SRC = 'exploration/reference/people-hr.appdef.json'
OUT = 'schema/core/core_people.v1.json'

# On/offboarding is a PROCESS an HR app runs, not the record of who works here. It is the one part
# of people_hr that a company would want to model its own way, so it stays available as a separate
# app and the core app is the part everyone needs identically.
DROP_ENTITIES = {'onboarding', 'onboarding_task', 'offboarding'}
DROP_PAGES = {'onboarding', 'offboarding'}
DROP_COMMANDS = {'offboard', 'begin_onboarding', 'complete_onboarding',
                 'progress_offboarding', 'complete_offboarding'}

d = json.load(open(SRC, encoding='utf-8'))

d['key'] = 'core_people'
d['version'] = '1.0.0'
d['description'] = (
    "Who works here, and everything a company needs to keep about them: the employee record, "
    "employment history, compensation, emergency contacts, documents and HR notes. Provided by the "
    "platform in every workspace, so an app that needs to point at a colleague has something real to "
    "point at instead of inventing its own staff list. Onboarding and offboarding are deliberately "
    "NOT here — those are a process every company runs differently, and they belong to an HR app "
    "built for the way this one runs them."
)

d['entities'] = [e for e in d['entities'] if e['key'] not in DROP_ENTITIES]
kept = {e['key'] for e in d['entities']}

d['pages'] = [p for p in d.get('pages', []) if p['key'] not in DROP_PAGES]
d['views'] = [v for v in d.get('views', []) if v.get('entity') in kept]
d['processes'] = [p for p in d.get('processes', []) if p.get('entity') in kept]
d['commands'] = [c for c in d.get('commands', []) if c['key'] not in DROP_COMMANDS]

for r in d.get('roles', []):
    r['grants'] = [g for g in r.get('grants', []) if g.get('entity') in kept or g.get('entity') == '*']
    # A role may also whitelist commands by name.
    for g in r['grants']:
        if isinstance(g.get('commands'), list):
            g['commands'] = [c for c in g['commands'] if c not in DROP_COMMANDS]


def strip_actions(node):
    """Blocks offer commands by key in `actions`. A dropped command left there renders a button that
    resolves to nothing — the gate catches it, but only if we look everywhere it can appear."""
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        if isinstance(node.get('actions'), list):
            node['actions'] = [a for a in node['actions']
                               if not (isinstance(a, str) and a in DROP_COMMANDS)]
        for v in node.values():
            strip_actions(v)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for v in node:
            strip_actions(v)


strip_actions(d)

# Role descriptions are shown to whoever assigns them, so one that still promises onboarding would
# be a lie about what the grant does.
ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS = {
    'hr': 'Owns employee files, employment history and compensation.',
}
for r in d.get('roles', []):
    if r['key'] in ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS:
        r['description'] = ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS[r['key']]

# The tagline is the app's one-line pitch in the launcher and Studio — it must not advertise the
# one thing this app deliberately does not do.
d['presentation']['tagline'] = 'Who works here, and their records'
d['presentation']['category'] = 'Core'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# EVERY USER IS IN HERE, AND NOT EVERYONE IN HERE IS A USER.
#
# The source app assumed the two sets were the same: `person` was a REQUIRED link to the login
# directory and also the display name, so an employee who cannot sign in was unrepresentable, and a
# user with no HR file simply did not appear. Both halves are wrong for a core app — a workshop hires
# people who never touch a laptop, and a colleague who was invited yesterday should already be
# listed.
#
# So the employee record carries its own name and the login link becomes optional:
#   person set   -> a colleague with a login; the platform keeps full_name in step with their user
#   person null  -> someone who works here without an account; HR types their name
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
employee = next(e for e in d['entities'] if e['key'] == 'employee')

employee['fields'].insert(0, {
    'key': 'full_name',
    'label': 'Name',
    'type': 'text',
    'required': True,
    'indexed': True,
    'help': "Kept in step with the sign-in directory for anyone who has a login; typed by hand for "
            "everyone else.",
})

# Fields that can only be known AFTER someone files the paperwork cannot be required, or the
# platform could not list a colleague the moment they are invited.
for key in ('person', 'job_title', 'start_date'):
    next(f for f in employee['fields'] if f['key'] == key).pop('required', None)

next(f for f in employee['fields'] if f['key'] == 'person')['help'] = (
    "The sign-in identity this record belongs to, when there is one. Empty for people who work here "
    "without an account."
)

# The name now comes off the record, not through the reference. The AVATAR still resolves through
# `person` — someone without a login has no photo, which is the honest rendering.
employee['displayField'] = 'full_name'


def repoint_name(node):
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        if node.get('title') == 'person' and node.get('kind') == 'hub':
            node['title'] = 'full_name'
        if node.get('kind') == 'field' and node.get('field') == 'person':
            node['field'] = 'full_name'
        if isinstance(node.get('columns'), list):
            node['columns'] = ['full_name' if c == 'person' else c for c in node['columns']]
        if isinstance(node.get('search'), list):
            node['search'] = ['full_name' if c == 'person' else c for c in node['search']]
        for v in node.values():
            repoint_name(v)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for v in node:
            repoint_name(v)


repoint_name(d)

# Any reference field pointing at a dropped entity would now dangle. (There are none today; the
# check stays so a future re-run of this transform cannot silently produce a broken definition.)
for e in d['entities']:
    for f in e['fields']:
        if f.get('type') == 'reference' and not f.get('targetApp') and f.get('targetEntity') in DROP_ENTITIES:
            sys.exit(f"ERROR: {e['key']}.{f['key']} references dropped entity {f['targetEntity']}")

# Nothing anywhere may still name a dropped entity or command.
blob = json.dumps(d)
leftover = sorted({n for n in DROP_ENTITIES | DROP_COMMANDS if f'"{n}"' in blob})
if leftover:
    sys.exit(f"ERROR: dropped names still referenced: {leftover}")

for e in d['entities']:
    if not e['fields']:
        sys.exit(f"ERROR: entity {e['key']} has no fields")

with open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(d, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    f.write('\n')

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The demo seed, derived from the same source for the same reason: the two must not drift.
#
# The employee block MERGES rather than inserts. Those 24 records already exist by the time the
# loader runs — the platform files one per user at startup — so seeding them as new rows would give
# the demo 48 employees, half of them empty.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEED_SRC = 'demo/seed/people_hr.seed.json'
SEED_OUT = 'demo/seed/core_people.seed.json'

seed = json.load(open(SEED_SRC, encoding='utf-8'))
seed['app'] = 'core_people'
seed['entities'] = [b for b in seed['entities'] if b['entity'] not in DROP_ENTITIES]

# Who does what. Core apps get no blanket grant — every member already reads the directory through
# the `employee` role, so anything more has to be given to somebody in particular, which is both the
# correct configuration and the more interesting demo.
seed['grants'] = [
    {'roleKey': 'hr', 'team': 'HR'},
    {'roleKey': 'manager', 'people': 'managers'},
]

emp_block = next(b for b in seed['entities'] if b['entity'] == 'employee')
emp_block['mergeOn'] = 'person'
for rec in emp_block['records']:
    # full_name is required, and on a cold database (no sync yet) the merge falls back to an insert,
    # so every record has to be able to stand on its own.
    if rec.get('person', '').startswith('@person:'):
        rec['full_name'] = rec['person'].replace('@person:', '@person_name:', 1)

# Reorder so full_name reads first, matching the field order in the definition.
for rec in emp_block['records']:
    if 'full_name' in rec:
        ordered = {k: rec[k] for k in ('_key', 'actAs', 'full_name') if k in rec}
        ordered.update({k: v for k, v in rec.items() if k not in ordered})
        rec.clear()
        rec.update(ordered)

with open(SEED_OUT, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(seed, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    f.write('\n')

print(f"wrote {SEED_OUT}")
print("  blocks:", [(b['entity'], len(b['records'])) for b in seed['entities']])
print()
print(f"wrote {OUT}")
print("  entities:", [e['key'] for e in d['entities']])
print("  pages   :", [p['key'] for p in d['pages']])
print("  views   :", [v['key'] for v in d['views']])
print("  commands:", [c['key'] for c in d['commands']])
print("  roles   :", {r['key']: [g['entity'] for g in r['grants']] for r in d['roles']})

﻿<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="JsonSchema.Net" Version="9.2.2" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- The App Definition schema + canonical platform entities are the single source of
       truth (shared with the Python spec); embed them so the gate is self-contained.

       They live in the `cordango` SUBMODULE (oss/cordango/schemas) because the contract is
       open source and this project follows it there. A clone without submodules initialised
       fails here with "file not found" rather than building against a stale copy: run
       `git submodule update --init` and the paths resolve. The LogicalNames are unchanged,
       so no code that reads a resource had to learn about the move. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\oss\cordango\schemas\app-definition.schema.json" Link="app-definition.schema.json" LogicalName="app-definition.schema.json" />
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\oss\cordango\schemas\platform-entities.json" Link="platform-entities.json" LogicalName="platform-entities.json" />
    <!-- The BLUEPRINT schema: a different language from the App Definition (what the user approved,
         in their vocabulary, with stable identity). Embedded for the same reason - BlueprintGate
         validates structurally against it, and the proposer tool schemas are sliced from it so a
         proposer can never emit definition structures and undo an approval. -->
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\oss\cordango\schemas\blueprint.schema.json" Link="blueprint.schema.json" LogicalName="blueprint.schema.json" />
    <!-- Core apps: the registry plus EVERY shipped version of each definition (the compatibility
         validator replays the real upgrade path, so old versions are not dead weight). Flat file
         names — schema/core/<systemKey>.<version>.json — keep the logical resource names stable
         across platforms; MSBuild's RecursiveDir would bake in Windows separators. -->
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\oss\cordango\schemas\core\*.json" LogicalName="core/%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- These live OUTSIDE the project tree, so `dotnet watch` (which the api container runs) never saw
       them change: no rebuild, no restart, no warning. And an embedded resource can't be hot-reloaded
       anyway — Gate.RawSchema is a `static readonly` parsed once per process. The result was a
       long-lived container silently validating against an ANCIENT schema: on 2026-07-14 it rejected a
       correctly-composed matrix (`as` = "false schema") AND valid domains (`target:"self"`), which
       reads as "the model failed" when the model was right. Watch them so any edit forces a restart. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <Watch Include="..\..\oss\cordango\schemas\*.json" />
    <Watch Include="..\..\oss\cordango\schemas\src\*.json" />
    <Watch Include="..\..\oss\cordango\schemas\core\*.json" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

    <RootNamespace>AppBuilder.AccessTokens</RootNamespace>

  <!--
    NO ProjectReference, NO PackageReference, and that is the whole point of the project existing.

    One credential format has to be written by the API and read by the `cord` CLI. Those two live on
    opposite sides of a boundary the OSS solution enforces on purpose — the CLI must never learn to
    depend on the control plane — so the format cannot live in either of them. A second
    implementation was the alternative, and a security-relevant encoding with two implementations
    drifts at the checksum first and at the hash second, where neither drift shows up as an error:
    it shows up as tokens that verify on one side and not the other.

    BCL only, so it joins both AppBuilder.slnx and AppBuilder.Oss.slnx without carrying anything
    into the portable boundary.
  -->

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <RootNamespace>Cordango</RootNamespace>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    RULE 0 — this project is the portable core, and this ItemGroup is the whole claim.

    ZERO ProjectReferences and exactly ONE package. Everything an application definition means lives
    here and can be reasoned about without a database, a container, a web host or a model provider:

      Definition/   the contract. Schema gate, semantic validation, normalizer, computed-expression
                    language, core-app registry, definition hash.
      Cord/         the semantic model authored source is written in, and the lowering to a
                    definition. A function of the model ALONE.
      Compile/      definition to runtime manifest, plus the one validation pipeline every caller
                    goes through.
      Semantics/    condition and template evaluation, shared by every host that runs an app.

    MUST NOT be added here, ever: any web framework, EF or Npgsql, any AI or provider client, any
    tenant or hosting concern. Hosts adapt to this project; it never reaches back.

    Not a convention anyone has to remember: tests/Compiler.Tests/BoundaryTests.cs asserts the
    compiled assembly's reference set against an allowlist and this file's shape against the rule.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="JsonSchema.Net" Version="9.2.2" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- The App Definition schema + canonical platform entities are the single source of truth
       (shared with the Python spec in ../../schemas); embed them so the gate is self-contained. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\schemas\app-definition.schema.json" Link="app-definition.schema.json" LogicalName="app-definition.schema.json" />
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\schemas\platform-entities.json" Link="platform-entities.json" LogicalName="platform-entities.json" />
    <!-- The BLUEPRINT schema: a different language from the App Definition (what the user approved,
         in their vocabulary, with stable identity). Embedded for the same reason - BlueprintGate
         validates structurally against it, and the proposer tool schemas are sliced from it so a
         proposer can never emit definition structures and undo an approval. -->
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\schemas\blueprint.schema.json" Link="blueprint.schema.json" LogicalName="blueprint.schema.json" />
    <!-- Core apps: the registry plus EVERY shipped version of each definition (the compatibility
         validator replays the real upgrade path, so old versions are not dead weight). Flat file
         names — schemas/core/<systemKey>.<version>.json — keep the logical resource names stable
         across platforms; MSBuild's RecursiveDir would bake in Windows separators. -->
    <EmbeddedResource Include="..\..\schemas\core\*.json" LogicalName="core/%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- These live OUTSIDE the project tree, so `dotnet watch` (which a dev container may run) never
       saw them change: no rebuild, no restart, no warning. And an embedded resource cannot be
       hot-reloaded anyway — Gate.RawSchema is a `static readonly` parsed once per process. The
       result was a long-lived container silently validating against an ANCIENT schema: on
       2026-07-14 it rejected a correctly-composed matrix (`as` = "false schema") AND valid domains
       (`target:"self"`), which reads as "the model failed" when the model was right. Watch them so
       any edit forces a restart. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <Watch Include="..\..\schemas\*.json" />
    <Watch Include="..\..\schemas\src\*.json" />
    <Watch Include="..\..\schemas\core\*.json" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <InternalsVisibleTo Include="Cordango.Compiler.Tests" />
    <!-- The private monorepo's suites still exercise this code until they move; listing both names
         means neither side of that move needs a same-commit change on the other. -->
    <InternalsVisibleTo Include="AppBuilder.Definition.Tests" />
    <InternalsVisibleTo Include="AppBuilder.Cord.Tests" />
    <InternalsVisibleTo Include="AppBuilder.Runtime.Tests" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

"""S2b platform side: point every backend consumer at Cordango.Compiler.

Namespace rewrite is a SINGLE regex pass with an alternation ordered longest-first, so that
`AppBuilder.Definition.Tests` (a test project that is NOT moving yet) is matched and preserved
before the shorter `AppBuilder.Definition` can rewrite its prefix.
"""
import io, os, re, glob

SEP = chr(92)

def norm(p):
    return p.replace(SEP, '/')

# Ordered longest-first. Identity entries are load-bearing: they consume the token so a shorter
# pattern cannot rewrite a prefix of it.
MAP = [
    ('AppBuilder.Definition.Tests',      'AppBuilder.Definition.Tests'),

19	/// satisfied while a transitive reference smuggles the dependency in anyway.</para>
