# Cordango OSS split + standalone source generator

## Context

Tim's architecture document establishes the next product direction: alongside the existing platform, an open-source toolchain that takes a compiled App Definition JSON and **generates a complete, conventional, standalone application** (ASP.NET Core + EF Core + PostgreSQL + Vue 3 + Vuetify) that the user owns and deploys anywhere. The OSS/commercial boundary: OSS builds **one app** (auth, permissions, local Organizations/People/Departments/Groups, commands, processes, workflows, deterministic seeds); the platform keeps multi-app, cross-app, audit/history, AI, enrichment, platform search, marketplace, managed ops.

Three GitHub repos **already exist** (private until launch): `https://github.com/cordango/cordango` (OSS monorepo), `https://github.com/cordango/web-controls` (`@cordango/web-controls`), `https://github.com/cordango/examples`. They get mounted into AppBuilder as **git submodules** so all work happens here but is committed to the separate repos from day one — the separation is physical, not aspirational.

Branch: `CLI-CodeGen` (freshly cut from main, no work started).

## Decisions locked with Tim

1. **Submodules now** at `oss/cordango`, `oss/web-controls`, `oss/examples` (umbrella avoids the root `examples/` clash; one compose mount covers all three).
2. **Existing portable core moves now**: Definition + Cord + AccessTokens + Cli leave `backend/`, renamed `AppBuilder.*` → `Cordango.*`, into Tim's specified monorepo tree.
3. **CLI binary renames `cord` → `cordango` now**, **and the workspace format renames too**: `cord.yaml` → `cordango.yaml`, `.cord.yaml` → `.cordango.yaml`, `.cord/` → `.cordango/` (one-time legacy reads; zero external users make this the last cheap moment). Token prefixes `cord_pat`/`cord_cxt` do NOT rename (server wire format, issued tokens).
4. **Both run tracks live**: `cordango run` (local interpreted platform simulation, CordyOSS §7 packaged-Postgres track, for platform users) stays on the roadmap, **not scheduled here** and not blocked by anything here. This plan builds the standalone generator track.
5. **Tier-B UI blocks** (timeline, gantt, scheduling, planning, orgchart, intake, embeds): v1 rejects with CORD2111; `--allow-partial-ui` demotes to warning + visible "not supported" card **and a permanent scar in build metadata** (below).
6. **Historical model-generated fixtures publish** into the monorepo test fixtures.
7. **Repos private until launch** → migration is mechanical (dropped Blueprint layer moves along); one deliberate **pre-publication hygiene pass** later (not in these slices).
8. **EF/backend generation follows Tim's TCDev.APIGenerator pattern** (DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api): generic scaffold machinery + thin generated per-entity types, EF-native automated migrations. Details below; S6 opens with a reuse assessment of the APIGenerator codebase itself.

## Corrections after the restructure landed (Tim, 2026-08-20, second pass)

- **Standalone security is DELIBERATELY SEPARATE, and this is now settled rather than deferred.**
  Two things were conflated and they need separating:

  **Authentication** — who the caller is: login, sessions, password hashing, tokens. Stock ASP.NET
  Core Identity (plus OpenIddict only if a generated app ever needs to be an OAuth server, which v1
  does not). None of the platform's authentication was ever going to be shared, and none should be.
  Nothing to decide.

  **Authorization** — what the definition's `roles[]` mean: union across roles, specific grant beats
  `*`, field override else role default, commands deny-by-default. I argued this belonged in a
  shared component and I was wrong about the framing. It is not security infrastructure, it is
  definition interpretation, in the same family as computed expressions and conditions. But sharing
  it still creates the thing Tim is right to refuse: a coupling where a change made for standalone
  reasons alters platform enforcement. Blast radius, not secrecy.

  **So: the scaffold gets its OWN permission code, and drift is DETECTED rather than prevented.**
  A conformance fixture — `tests/fixtures/permissions/*.json`, a list of
  `(definition, roles, entity, field, operation) → expected decision` — is generated once from the
  platform evaluator, checked into the public repo as DATA, and asserted by both the platform suite
  and the generated app's own suite. No shared assembly, no coupling, and a divergence becomes a red
  test instead of a wrong answer in production. Cheap: the rules are small and finite.

  `PermissionEvaluator` and `FieldProjection` stay in `AppBuilder.Runtime` and are not published.
- **No one-file assemblies.** `Cordango.AccessTokens` folded into `Cordango.Compiler/Tokens/`. The
  format still cannot live in the CLI alone — a server writes it and the CLI reads it.
- **`samples/` → `tests/corpus/`.** `cordango/examples` is the examples repository; the compiler's
  copy is the conformance corpus and is now named that way.
- **Every source file carries a licence header** (SPDX + copyright + project + URL), enforced by
  `LicenceHeaderTests` rather than a one-time sweep. Example application source (the specimen's
  `.cord.ts`) is exempt — stamping our copyright on the thing a reader is meant to copy says the
  wrong thing. **The generator must apply the same reasoning at S7–S9: generated output belongs to
  the user and gets no Cordango header.**

## Review corrections folded in (Tim, 2026-08-20)

- **One canonical generator input** (`CompiledAppArtifact`), never independently supplied Definition + Manifest.
- **Seeds are dataset-deterministic by default** (fixed anchor date); `--seed-date today` is the explicit non-reproducible mode.
- **No reimplemented template/condition semantics** — `ConditionEvaluator` and `TemplateResolver` moved into `Cordango.Compiler/Semantics`, wrapped by both hosts. (The same argument was applied to PERMISSIONS and then reversed — see the second-pass corrections above. Standalone gets its own permission code and its own stock Identity auth; drift is caught by shared decision fixtures rather than prevented by shared code.)
- **CSRF covers every cookie-authenticated mutation** (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), not just account endpoints.
- **`AppCompiler.CompilerId` stays `appbuilder-runtime/0.1`** — a repo extraction must not mutate platform state; branding is display-only, the fingerprint changes only when compiler behavior changes.
- **`--allow-partial-ui` leaves a scar** in `cordango.build.json` + a prominent generated-README section.
- **Cross-repo moves are not `git mv`**: filesystem move → `git add` in the submodule → `git rm` in the parent → independent commits (both Tim's) → parent submodule-pointer bump.

## Verified facts the design rests on (file:line evidence)

- **The Runtime split is clean**: the compile layer — `AppCompiler.cs`, `CandidateValidator.cs`, `OpenApiFromManifest.cs`, `SeedPlan.cs`, `SeedRows.cs` — imports only `System.Text.Json(.Nodes)` + `AppBuilder.Definition` ([CandidateValidator.cs:1-3](backend/AppBuilder.Runtime/CandidateValidator.cs#L1-L3)); the smoke step is pure JSON walks, no stores/engine. `DesignDefaults` already lives in Definition. `PermissionEvaluator.cs` (161 lines) and `FieldProjection.cs` (73) are pure; `ConditionEvaluator.cs`/`TemplateResolver.cs` look pure (verify at move; if not, split the pure core out).
- **CLI flag parser** hard-codes value-taking flags `app, scope, ops, out, instance, token` at [Cli.cs:96](backend/AppBuilder.Cli/Cli.cs#L96) — `target` and `seed` must be added. Dispatch switch duplicated in `Cli.Tests/Sandbox.cs:60-80`.
- **Definition embeds schemas by relative path** (`..\..\schema\...`, Link + LogicalName, plus `<Watch>` items) — [AppBuilder.Definition.csproj:16-40](backend/AppBuilder.Definition/AppBuilder.Definition.csproj#L16-L40). Paths survive a coordinated move; schema edits require an api/worker restart (embedded at build — the 2026-07-14 stale-schema incident).
- **Docker**: api mounts `./backend`, `./schema`, `./appdata` ([docker-compose.yml:123-126](docker-compose.yml#L123-L126)); worker same (~226-229); ops has **zero** ProjectReferences (no new mount); editor mounts the repo root (sees `oss/` for free); web mounts only `./web`.
- **Corpus**: `Corpus.cs:30` anchors RepoRoot on `schema/app-definition.schema.json`; counts are **floors** (`>= 15` semantic, `>= 10` historical in `CordRoundTripTests.cs:139-141`), not exact; the exact pin is `exploration/cord/raw-allowlist.json` (`CordCoverageTests.cs:190`). 13 reference apps + crm + budget-planner.
- **Capability grounding**: `prev()`, `series`, windowed rollups, `relatedApps`, `enrich` have **zero** uses across `exploration/reference/`; `history` appears once (ventures). `targetApp` in the corpus is only `"platform"` (28×) and `"core_organizations"` (7×).
- **CLI uses no Localization** — after the compile layer moves, the OSS repo needs no Localization; it stays platform-side.
- **Blueprint tests can't move**: their fixtures come from `bench/corpus/development/**` (private benchmark corpus) — blueprint **code** moves with Definition, blueprint **tests** relocate to `backend/AppBuilder.Generator.Tests`.
- **AccessTokens** consumers: exactly Api and Cli. **AppBuilder.Generator is the AI layer** — the naming trap the `Cordango.SourceGen*` names avoid.
- **TCDev.APIGenerator** (Tim's net-dynamic-api, commit 4279e35): `[Api("/people", ApiMethodsToGenerate.All, authorize: true, requiredReadScopes/WriteScopes)]` on POCOs implementing `IObjectBase<TKey>`; `GenericDbContext.OnModelCreating` = `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(asm)` for all discovered assemblies + `builder.Entity(type)` for unmapped types; lifecycle hooks (`IBeforeCreate<T>.BeforeCreate(...)`); generic CRUD controllers per attributed type; pluggable providers (Postgres/SQL/SQLite); Identity/OData/GraphQL as separate modules.

---

## Target end-state

### `cordango/cordango` (mounted `oss/cordango/`)

```
oss/cordango/
├── src/
│   ├── Cordango.Compiler/          # Definition + Cord + compile files + shared semantics, ONE project
│   │   ├── Definition/  (ns Cordango.Definition, incl. Blueprint/)
│   │   ├── Cord/        (ns Cordango.Cord)
│   │   ├── Compile/     (ns Cordango.Compile: AppCompiler, CandidateValidator,
│   │   │                 OpenApiFromManifest, SeedPlan, SeedRows)
│   │   ├── Semantics/   (ns Cordango.Semantics: ConditionEvaluator, TemplateResolver)
│   │   └── Tokens/      (ns Cordango.AccessTokens: the credential format a server writes
│   │                     and the CLI reads — no assembly of its own)
│   ├── Cordango.Cli/               # AssemblyName=cordango
│   ├── Cordango.SourceGen/         # generator SDK: contracts, capabilities, validator, runner, protocol
│   ├── Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue/  # the first-party generator (emitters + vendored controls dist)
│   └── Cordango.Standalone/        # scaffold: generic API machinery + embedded static files
├── schemas/                        # app-definition.schema.json, src/, core/, platform-entities.json,
│                                   # blueprint.schema.json, compose.py, validate.py, README.md
├── tests/
│   ├── corpus/                     # the conformance corpus (NOT "samples" — cordango/examples
│   │                               # is the examples repository): 13 reference apps, crm,
│   │                               # budget-planner, and the CordSource specimen
│   ├── Compiler.Tests/             # Definition.Tests + Cord.Tests + compile-layer Runtime tests + Corpus.cs
│   ├── Cli.Tests/
│   ├── Generator.Tests/            # SourceGen SDK + DotNetVue unit tests (new)
│   ├── Determinism.Tests/          # double-build byte-compare, runner ordering/traversal (new)
│   ├── Compatibility.Tests/        # CoreDefinitionCompatibilityTests + expected pass/fail table (new)
│   └── fixtures/                   # invalid/broken.appdef.json, historical/ (generated fixtures), raw-allowlist.json
├── docs/  LICENSE(Apache-2.0)  README.md  Cordango.slnx  Directory.Build.props  .gitignore
```

**Key mapping decisions**
- **One merged `Cordango.Compiler` project** (matches Tim's tree; Cord's only dep was Definition; layering survives as namespaces + a namespace-scoped tripwire in the restated BoundaryTests). Zero ProjectReferences, one PackageReference (JsonSchema.Net 9.2.2), embeds `..\..\schemas\...` with the **same LogicalNames**, Watch items follow.
- **`Cordango.Authorization`** = the pure grant-resolution + field-projection semantics moved out of Runtime (Tim's "Authorization.Core" component). Platform `AppBuilder.Runtime` references it (adapter); the standalone scaffold wraps the **same implementation** — vendored as source into generated apps (provenance headers) until NuGet packages exist. One semantic implementation, never two conformance-tested twins. Same treatment for condition/template semantics via `Cordango.Semantics`.
- `Cordango.Cli.csproj`: refs AccessTokens + Compiler (+ SourceGen from S4) — **the Runtime wart dies**. YamlDotNet stays.
- **Unchanged on purpose**: `AppSchemaVersion` ("2.0"), `DefinitionHash`, embedded LogicalNames, token prefixes, **and `AppCompiler.CompilerId` (`"appbuilder-runtime/0.1"`)** — the CoreAppProvisioner fingerprint must not change from a repo extraction; any human-facing "Cordango Compiler" naming is display-only; the fingerprint changes only when compiler behavior changes, deliberately.
- **Corpus.cs** moves into Compiler.Tests, re-anchored to walk up to `schemas/app-definition.schema.json` (works from a standalone clone AND inside AppBuilder); floors (`>=15`, `>=10`) restated verbatim with a move comment — never loosened.
- **Blueprint tests** (8 Definition.Tests files + `Runtime.Tests/BlueprintBuildConformanceTests.cs`) → `backend/AppBuilder.Generator.Tests/` (bench fixture Content items come along). `CoCreationContractTests.cs` → `backend/AppBuilder.Api.Tests/`.
- **BoundaryTests restated twice**: in Compiler.Tests (assembly refs allowlist; csproj zero ProjectReferences / one PackageReference; type tripwire scoped to `Cordango.Cord` namespace) and platform-side `backend/AppBuilder.Api.Tests/OssBoundaryTests.cs` (no csproj under `oss/` mentions `backend\`; no `oss/` assembly references `AppBuilder.*`) — **dependency direction backend→submodule only, asserted**.
- **Credentials migration** (Cordango.Cli): resolution `CORDANGO_CONFIG_DIR` → `CORD_CONFIG_DIR` (compat) → `%APPDATA%\cordango`; `Load()` falls back to reading `%APPDATA%\cord\credentials.json` when the new path is empty (read-only, same FormatVersion guard); `Flush()` writes only the new path. Test via env-var override.
- **Workspace format rename** (full): loader accepts `cord.yaml`/`.cord.yaml` as legacy and reports them via `doctor`/`fmt`; `new`/scaffold/save write only `cordango.yaml`/`.cordango.yaml`; build dir `.cordango/`; `.gitignore` templates updated. Ripples: `WorkspaceFile.cs`, `AppFolder.cs`, `Templates/Scaffold.cs`, Cli.Tests, budgetPlanner specimen files, `exploration/cord/apps` fixtures, `bench/cord_run.py`, docs spellings.
- `backend/AppBuilder.Oss.slnx` and `backend/AppBuilder.Cord.slnx` **are deleted** — superseded by `oss/cordango/Cordango.slnx` (the physical extraction test: must build/test from a standalone clone). Their header-comment intent moves to the submodule README.
- Submodule `Directory.Build.props` mirrors backend's obj/bin redirect keyed on **`CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT`**, including the do-not-set-for-tests warning.

### Move mechanics (applies to every migration slice)

`oss/*` are separate repositories — a cross-repo move is **never `git mv`**. Per batch: filesystem move/copy → `git add` inside the submodule → `git rm` (delete) in the parent → **two independent commits, both Tim's** → parent commit also bumps the submodule pointer. Fresh history in the public repos is the accepted consequence (and the history-hygiene guarantee: AppBuilder's history never leaves the private repo).

### What stays in AppBuilder

`backend/`: Localization, **Runtime (data plane only**: stores, Engine/ minus the moved pure semantics, AppDataService, DerivedFields, PostgresStorage, TenantSchemaProvisioner, RuntimeStore**)**, ControlPlane, Generator (AI), Platform, Api, Worker, Ops, Diagnostics + platform tests. `schema/` shrinks to `schema/cocreation/` only. Root `examples/` empties (Tim deletes when convenient).

---

## Platform-side changes

- **csproj path+name edits**: Api (AccessTokens+Definition refs → submodule Cordango.AccessTokens/Compiler), Worker, Generator (Definition+Cord → one Compiler ref), Runtime (Definition → Compiler; + new ref Cordango.Authorization; keeps Localization+Npgsql). Using-renames: `AppBuilder.Definition`→`Cordango.Definition` (97 files), `AppBuilder.Cord`→`Cordango.Cord` (51), `AppBuilder.AccessTokens`→`Cordango.AccessTokens` (8), + `using Cordango.Compile/Semantics/Authorization;` where the moved types are used (~20 files).
- **`backend/AppBuilder.slnx`**: remove moved projects, add submodule projects by relative path — `dotnet test backend/AppBuilder.slnx` stays the one green bar covering both sides.
- **Platform corpus access**: new `PlatformCorpus.cs` (Runtime.Tests) anchored on `oss/cordango/schemas/app-definition.schema.json`, paths → `oss/cordango/samples/...`; consumers: Runtime.Tests (CordHandAuthoredApps/CordPipeline/SynthesisRedundancy), Api.Tests (OffDomain/ResearchGatherer).
- **docker-compose.yml — propose; Tim applies + restarts**: api + worker each gain `- ./oss:/app/oss` volume and `CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT: /build` env; `./schema` mount **stays** (cocreation). ops/editor/web unchanged.
- **editor**: `'@schema'` → `../oss/cordango/schemas`, `'@reference'` → `../oss/cordango/samples/reference` in [editor/vite.config.js](editor/vite.config.js); `editor/src/store/samples.js` globs likewise.
- **Python**: `demo/load.py:66-81` + `demo/derive_core_people.py` corpus paths; schema drift-guard invocations become `python oss/cordango/schemas/compose.py --check`.
- **Docs spellings**: `cord ` command examples → `cordango ` in STATUS.md, `_docs/CordyOSS.md`, `_docs/plan_index.md` (leave `.claude/worktrees/*` copies alone). "Cord" the DSL/product-layer name (CordSource, CordApp) **stays**.

---

## New OSS projects (design summary)

### `Cordango.SourceGen` — SDK + runner (no target knowledge)

```csharp
public record CompilerInfo(string Id, string Version);
public record CompiledAppArtifact(          // the ONE canonical input, built only by the CLI
    JsonObject Definition,                  // from Pipeline.Check — the pair can never mismatch
    JsonObject Manifest,
    string DefinitionHash,
    CompilerInfo Compiler);

public record GenerateRequest(CompiledAppArtifact App, JsonObject Options);
public record GeneratedFile(string RelativePath, string? Content, string? ContentBase64 = null);
public record Diagnostic(string Code, string Message, string? JsonPath);
public record GenerateResult(IReadOnlyList<GeneratedFile> Files,
    IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Warnings, IReadOnlyList<Diagnostic> Errors);

public interface IAppSourceGenerator {
    string Id { get; }                      // "dotnet-vue"
    string Version { get; }
    GeneratorCapabilities Capabilities { get; }
    GenerateResult Generate(GenerateRequest request);
}
```

- The CLI is the **only** construction site of `CompiledAppArtifact` (from `Pipeline.Check` output) — a mismatched Definition/Manifest is structurally impossible; no second IR is created.
- `GeneratorCapabilities` = declarative data (bools + sets); **one** shared `TargetValidator.Validate(definition, capabilities)` walks the definition Gate-style.
- **CORD21xx catalogue** (greenfield): 2100 cross-app ref, 2101 relatedApps, 2102 history, 2103 enrich, 2104 series, 2105 prev(), 2106 windowed rollup, 2107 unsupported effect, 2108 unsupported trigger, 2109 unsupported platform target, 2110 AI feature, 2111 unsupported block kind, 2112 unsupported field type. Every code carries the JSON path. **Never silently dropped.**
- **Runner** (CLI-side): ordinal sort by RelativePath; reject absolute paths/`..`/drive-colons, normalize `\`→`/`, `Path.GetFullPath` prefix re-check; UTF-8 no BOM, `\n`, AtomicFile pattern; refuses a non-empty output dir unless it holds a previous `cordango.build.json`, then deletes exactly that manifest's files first (deterministic overwrite).
- **`cordango.build.json`**: `{protocolVersion, definitionHash, compiler{id,version}, generator{id,version}, scaffoldVersion, controlsVersion, partial, unsupportedCapabilities[{code,path,feature}], files[{path,sha256}]}` — no timestamps, GUIDs, machine paths. **`--allow-partial-ui` scars the metadata permanently** (`partial: true` + the full list) and the generated README gets a prominent "Partial build" section — a knowingly partial app can never pass as a full build later.
- **Protocol reserved now, adapter later**: external generator = exe; `--describe` → `{protocolVersion:1, id, version, capabilities}`; generate = request JSON stdin → result JSON stdout; `ExternalProcessGenerator : IAppSourceGenerator` built late.

### `Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue` — the generator

Input = `CompiledAppArtifact` (manifest supplies canonical processes, synthesized commands, computed flags, base fields, default views — never re-derived). Pure emitters `(artifact, options) → IEnumerable<GeneratedFile>`.

**Backend shape follows the TCDev.APIGenerator pattern** (generic machinery once in the scaffold, thin generated types per entity):

- **Generated per entity**: POCO implementing `IObjectBase<string>` (definition ids are `text` per `PostgresStorage`; not Guid) + `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<T>)` (table/column names snake_case, required/unique/partial-unique indexes, FKs + delete behavior, type mapping mirroring `PostgresStorage.cs:63-72`: integer→long, decimal/money→decimal, boolean→bool, date→DateOnly, datetime→DateTimeOffset, multiselect→List<string>/text[], json→JsonDocument/jsonb, else string) + lifecycle-hook classes (`IBeforeCreate<T>`/`IBeforeUpdate<T>`-style) carrying computed-field recompute, validation, and command-owned-field enforcement + `AppPermissions.cs` (roles/grants/fieldOverrides/commands as typed static data).
- **Scaffold-generic (written once, in `Cordango.Standalone`)**: generic CRUD controller over `IObjectBase<TKey>` (MVC attribute-routed, house style), generic repository/data service, `CordangoDbContext` doing `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` + auto-registration of unmapped types (GenericDbContext pattern, minus tenant filtering — one app, no tenancy), field-level projection + write-restriction enforcement wired through `Cordango.Authorization`, CSRF, error `{code,error}` mapping.
- **Migrations, EF-native**: the generator invokes **EF Core's own design-time `MigrationsScaffolder` in-process** (Npgsql provider, EF version pinned by the scaffold) with a **pinned migration id** `00000000000001_InitialCreate` — EF authors the migration + snapshot, determinism holds (same model + same EF version → same output; Determinism.Tests enforce). Startup runs `Database.Migrate()`. App evolution after generation = the user's own `dotnet ef migrations add`, documented in the generated README. No hand-rolled snapshot writer.
- Base fields from the manifest **minus `company_id`/`app_id`** (one app, no tenancy).
- **Commands/processes**: manifest's canonicalized processes + synthesized commands → generated `CommandService` (permission → guard → transition legality → input validation → write → events → effects) + state-field validation; command endpoints on the generic controller (`POST .../commands/{key}`).
- **Workflows/effects**: generated `WorkflowRegistrations.cs` + effect methods (updateRecord/createRecord/createForEach via DbContext); scaffold provides post-SaveChanges `RecordEvents` dispatcher, `ScheduleHostedService`, `INotificationService` (table + endpoint), `IEmailSender` (SMTP; log-only dev), `IWebhookSender` (HMAC optional). Condition + template evaluation = the **shared `Cordango.Semantics` implementations** (vendored source), not reimplementations.
- **Computed/rollups**: reuse `Cordango.Definition.ComputedExpr` AST → C# methods; generated dependency table drives scaffold `RecomputeService` (synchronous write-path recompute + transitive parent rollups, depth-guarded). **v1 supports** arithmetic/comparison/boolean, min/max, field refs, single hop, plain rollups (count/sum/avg/min/max). **v1 rejects** prev()/series/windowed rollups (2105/2104/2106) — zero corpus uses.
- **Vue**: one explicit `src/pages/<PascalKey>Page.vue` per manifest page composed from `@cordango/web-controls` + generated api-client modules + router/nav shell. Tier-B blocks → CORD2111 or `--allow-partial-ui` card + metadata scar. Scaffold chrome en+de; definition labels pass through.
- **Seeds — dataset-deterministic by default**: moved `SeedPlan`/`SeedRows` give ordering + grid joins; new `SeedSynthesizer` with PRNG seeded from `(seedValue, entityKey, fieldKey, rowIndex)`, embedded wordlists, states spread across process states, references drawn from seeded pools. `seed/seed.json` records a **fixed anchor date derived deterministically from the seed value** plus relative tokens (demo/load.py grammar: `@entity:key`, `{T+3}`); scaffold `SeedRunner` resolves against the recorded anchor → **definition + seed = same dataset, always**. `--seed-date today` explicitly re-anchors at apply time and is the documented non-reproducible mode.
- **Also emitted**: multi-stage Dockerfile (node build → dotnet → runtime serving SPA from wwwroot), docker-compose.yml (app + pinned postgres), app README (incl. Partial-build section when scarred), small generated test project, `cordango.build.json`.

### `Cordango.Standalone` — the scaffold

Two parts: (a) the **generic API machinery** above (real compiled code, unit-tested in the repo), (b) **static app files** embedded as resources (`Scaffold.Version`, `Scaffold.Files()`; only `{{AppName}}/{{AppKey}}` substitution): ASP.NET Core host (MVC, health+DB check, ILogger), **auth = ASP.NET Core Identity + cookie** for the same-origin SPA+API — with **antiforgery enforced globally on ALL mutating requests** (`AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken` global filter + XSRF cookie/header pattern for the SPA client), SameSite=Lax, login/logout/users/password-reset (via IEmailSender), **local org module** (Organizations, People, Departments, Groups — EF entities + controllers + Vue pages, shapes derived from `schemas/platform-entities.json` + `core_organizations`), `LocalFileStore` + media controller for attachments, en+de, `{code,error}` wire.

**S6 opens with an APIGenerator reuse assessment** (timeboxed): read TCDev.APIGenerator core + Data + Identity and decide per piece **adopt as dependency / absorb code / pattern only**. Default expectation: absorb the generic-controller + GenericDbContext + lifecycle-hook pattern into `Cordango.Standalone` (Cordango-owned, trimmed, net10, no OData/GraphQL/RabbitMQ; our permission model is definition-driven role/field grants rather than scope attributes); take more if the code proves directly liftable. Findings recorded in `oss/cordango/docs/`.

**Platform-ref mapping**: `platform.person→People`, `platform.department→Departments`, `platform.group→Groups`, `core_organizations.organization→Organizations`, `core_organizations.contact→People`; anything else → CORD2109.

### v1 capability matrix (pinned by Compatibility.Tests over `samples/`)

| Capability | v1 | Rejection |
|---|---|---|
| Entities, all scalar types, multiselect, json, attachment | ✓ | — |
| In-app refs; platform/core_organizations refs (mapped local) | ✓ | 2100/2109 |
| Computed (arith/min-max/hop), plain rollups | ✓ | — |
| prev(), series, windowed rollups | ✗ | 2105/2104/2106 |
| Processes, synthesized + authored commands | ✓ | — |
| Workflows: record.*, field.changed, schedule | ✓ | 2108 |
| Effects: update/create/createForEach/notify/email/webhook | ✓ | 2107 |
| enrich, history, relatedApps, AI, platform search, tenancy | ✗ | 2103/2102/2101/2110 |
| Roles incl. field-level + command grants | ✓ | — |
| Blocks Tier A (section,row,columns,stack,tabs,fields,field,text,view table/board/calendar,child,stat,chart,process,progress,tiles,hub,repeat) | ✓ | — |
| Blocks Tier B (gantt,planning,timeline,scheduling,intake,orgchart,embeds) | ✗ / `--allow-partial-ui` card + metadata scar | 2111 |

Expected: **expenses = full pass**; time-off + task-manager = full behavior, partial UI; ventures fails on history (by design); budget-planner fails on 2104/05/06.

---

## `oss/web-controls` — `@cordango/web-controls` v1

- Vite library mode (ESM+cjs), `vue`/`vuetify`/`vue-i18n` as **peerDependencies**, `node --test` for pure modules, no Pinia. Install plugin `CordangoControls` with injected seams: `{ i18n, peopleDirectory, isMe, mediaUrl, tableSettings, commandInvoker }`.
- **Moves first**: pure modules (`manifest.js`, `i18n/formatting.js`, `responsive.js`, `filterMemory.js`, `views/{timeRange,dayGrid,weeklyHours,chipsEditor,companyGroup,inlineCreate}.js`, `tables/use*` + their tests) and seam-cut components: `ChartCard`→`CordangoChartCard` (already standalone), `UiDataTable`→`CordangoDataTable`, `FieldInput`→`CordangoFieldInput`, `KanbanCore`→`CordangoKanban`, `ProcessBlock`→`CordangoProcess`, `UiRefPicker`/Person* (directory injected), pure `Ui*` primitives. Each moved file notes its `web/` origin (drift greppable).
- **Stays out**: `data.js`/`commands.js`/`me.js` (REST shape belongs to the app), vue-router (deep links → emitted events), `blockspec/`, `BlockRenderer.vue`.
- **Consumption before npm publish**: generator emits `vendor/cordango-web-controls/` (built dist, `controlsVersion` in build metadata); generated `package.json` uses `"file:./vendor/cordango-web-controls"`. Self-contained, offline, deterministic. npm publish later flips one dependency line (vendoring stays as `--vendor-controls`).
- **Platform `web/` migration is NOT a prerequisite** and not scheduled here.

## `oss/examples`

Seed with copies + READMEs of 4 curated apps: `task-manager/`, `expenses/`, `time-off/`, `room-booking/` (each `app.definition.json` from `samples/reference/`). `oss/cordango/samples/` stays the **tested** source of truth (corpus floors live in Compiler.Tests); examples repo is the user-facing showcase and may diverge (its README says so).

---

## Slice sequence

Every slice ends with `dotnet test backend/AppBuilder.slnx` green (db-backed suites: `docker compose up -d db` first) and `cd web && npm test` untouched-green. All commits/pushes are **Tim's** (submodule commit + parent pointer bump per the move mechanics above); container restarts are **Tim's**.

- **S0 (S) — Mounts + skeletons.** `git submodule add https://github.com/cordango/{cordango,web-controls,examples}.git` at `oss/…` (if a repo is empty, create its initial skeleton commit inside for Tim to push). In `oss/cordango`: LICENSE (Apache-2.0), README stub, `.gitignore`, `Directory.Build.props` (CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT), empty `Cordango.slnx`. Package stub in web-controls; README in examples. *Accept*: `git submodule status` lists three; platform suite untouched-green.
- **S1 (S) — Schema move.** Filesystem-move the schema set → `oss/cordango/schemas/` (add in submodule, `git rm` in parent); update Definition csproj embed/Watch paths (project not yet moved); editor `@schema` alias; propose compose mount+env (Tim applies, **restarts api/worker** — embedded schema). *Accept*: `python oss/cordango/schemas/compose.py --check` = 0; full suite green; Tim confirms api healthy.
- **S2 (L) — Compiler + Authorization extraction.** Move Definition (all, incl. Blueprint) + Cord + AccessTokens + the 5 compile files + the pure semantics (PermissionEvaluator, FieldProjection → `Cordango.Authorization`; ConditionEvaluator, TemplateResolver → `Cordango.Compiler/Semantics`, purity verified at move) into `src/`; namespace renames (~150 files); platform Runtime/Engine now wraps the moved semantics (adapter, no behavior change); tests → `tests/Compiler.Tests` (Corpus re-anchored, floors restated), blueprint tests → Generator.Tests, CoCreationContractTests → Api.Tests; corpus/fixtures/allowlist per mapping; platform rewires (csprojs, usings, PlatformCorpus.cs, demo py, editor `@reference`, slnx add/remove); BoundaryTests restated both sides; delete Oss.slnx + Cord.slnx. **CompilerId untouched.** *Accept*: platform suite green with same test count ±0; **`dotnet test oss/cordango/Cordango.slnx` green from a standalone temp clone** (the physical extraction test); raw-allowlist still exact; Tim restarts api/worker once.
- **S3 (M→L) — CLI move + full rename.** Move Cli + Cli.Tests; `AssemblyName cordango`; ref Cordango.Compiler (wart dies); **workspace format rename** (`cordango.yaml`/`.cordango.yaml`/`.cordango/` + legacy reads + doctor/fmt reporting + specimen/fixture/bench file renames); help/error strings; credentials fallback chain + test; Sandbox.cs; docs spellings. *Accept*: `dotnet run --project oss/cordango/src/Cordango.Cli -- version` prints cordango; scratch workspace with legacy `cord.yaml` loads + reports; old-credentials fallback test passes; full suite green.
- **S4 (M) — SourceGen SDK + capability gate. ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-20.** Delivered as planned plus
  `cordango targets`; two defects found by its own tests and fixed (the block walker missed
  `entities[].detail`, and the writer hashed pre-normalisation content). **The measured
  first-pass capability declaration was REJECTED by Tim and rewritten**: scope is set from the
  language, not from what emitters exist. **Every screen and the whole calculation plane are in
  scope** (gantt, timeline, orgchart, intake, answers, embeds, widgets; ordered series, `prev()`,
  windowed and matched rollups). Out of scope is only what needs OTHER applications or a model:
  cross-app references, `relatedApps`, `enrich`, and record history (§21, platform-only, with an
  upsell-shaped message a test pins). All 15 corpus apps build; ventures and budget-planner stop at
  the audit block alone.

  **This makes S8 materially bigger**: the recompute cascade is now in scope, and it is the hardest
  thing in the platform runtime (two passes to make fast: edit >180s→1.5s, grid 12min→67s). Tim's
  call is to follow the plan order and deal with it at S8 rather than de-risking it early, with the
  requirement that it must come out as **generic, deterministic generated code** rather than a
  hand-tuned engine. Budget Planner is the acceptance case. Original scope follows.
- **S4 (original) — SourceGen SDK + capability gate.** `Cordango.SourceGen` (CompiledAppArtifact contracts, TargetValidator, CORD21xx, runner incl. partial-scar metadata, protocol shapes/docs); CLI: `--target` on `check`/`build` + `validate` alias, `target`+`seed`+`seed-date` in the flag list, Sandbox mirrored; `run --seed` reserved in help. New Determinism.Tests (runner) + Compatibility.Tests (expected pass/fail table incl. ventures→2102, budget-planner→2104/05/06). *Accept*: `cordango validate --app expenses --target standalone` = 0; ventures = 1 naming CORD2102.
- **S5 (M) — web-controls v1.** Extract per plan; package builds; ported `node --test` green; smoke consumer renders CordangoDataTable. Platform web/ untouched.
- **S6 (L) — Standalone scaffold.** Opens with the **APIGenerator reuse assessment** (adopt/absorb/pattern per piece, recorded in docs/). Then `Cordango.Standalone` per design (generic controller/DbContext/hooks machinery, Identity auth with global antiforgery on all mutations, org module, media, health, logging, docker packaging, en+de, vendored controls dist); scaffold-instantiation test: materialize → `dotnet build` + `npm ci && npm run build` green; authorization is the scaffold's OWN code, checked against the shared decision fixtures (below).
- **S7 (L) — DotNetVue backend emitters.** POCOs + EntityTypeConfigurations + hook classes + AppPermissions + CommandService + EF-scaffolder migration (pinned id) + DbContext registration. *Accept*: `cordango build --app expenses --target standalone --out <tmp>` → emitted backend `dotnet build` green; double-build byte-identical (incl. the EF-authored migration); generated tests pass.
- **S8 (L) — Workflows, effects, computed.** WorkflowRegistrations + effects + ComputedExpr translation + RecomputeService. *Accept*: task-manager's 10 rollups correct in generated-app unit tests; a field.changed workflow fires in a docker-gated smoke.
- **S9 (L) — Vue emitters + seeds + metadata.** Tier-A pages, api clients, router/nav, `--allow-partial-ui` (card + scar), SeedSynthesizer + anchored seed.json + SeedRunner (`--seed-date today` opt-in), `cordango.build.json`. *Accept*: build expenses twice with `--seed 42` → byte-identical trees; two seeded databases from the same seed are identical (dataset determinism); generated app `docker compose up` → login → seeded table (**live run proposed to Tim**).
- **S10 (M) — Acceptance + ecosystem seeding.** time-off + task-manager through the pipeline (partial-UI, scars verified in their build.json); seed `oss/examples`; submodule READMEs/docs; **STATUS.md "What's next" + `_docs/plan_index.md` updated**; CLAUDE.md submodule-workflow note. *Accept*: Compatibility.Tests table fully green; three generated apps build.

## Verification

- Per slice: `dotnet test backend/AppBuilder.slnx` (with `docker compose up -d db`), `dotnet test oss/cordango/Cordango.slnx` (S2+, including from a standalone clone), `cd web && npm test`, `python oss/cordango/schemas/compose.py --check` (S1+).
- Generator: Determinism.Tests double-generation byte-compare (incl. EF-authored migration files); dataset-determinism test (same seed → identical rows); generated app `dotnet build` + `npm run build`; docker-gated smokes.
- Live checks (`docker compose up` of a generated app, api restarts) are proposed to Tim, never run unprompted.

## Risks & open questions

1. **`cordango run` tension** (noted, unresolved): CordyOSS §7 has `run` supervising closed platform binaries + packaged Postgres — a distribution/licensing story for later. Nothing here blocks it; `run` stays reserved.
2. **EF MigrationsScaffolder determinism**: in-process scaffolding with a pinned id should be byte-stable for the same model + pinned EF version; Determinism.Tests prove it in S7 — if EF output turns out unstable, fallback is committing the once-scaffolded migration as generator template data (still EF-authored, still no hand-rolled snapshot writer).
3. **Submodule friction** (Windows + `.claude/worktrees/*`): detached HEADs, two-step commits (submodule → umbrella pin, both Tim's), per-worktree `git submodule update --init`. Mitigate: CLAUDE.md note, suggest `git config submodule.recurse true`; umbrella slnx keeps one test command. A stale submodule pin now fails platform tests — desired loudness, new failure mode to recognize.
4. **Corpus floors/allowlist** restated deliberately in S2, never loosened.
5. **Schema-embed restarts**: S1 and S2 each need one Tim-driven api/worker restart; Watch items keep protecting dotnet-watch.
6. **Blueprint layer (5,407 lines)** moves into the (private-until-launch) public repo; **pre-publication hygiene pass** (prune blueprint or keep, sweep `_docs/`/bench references from moved comments, licensing sentence that generated output is unencumbered) is a scheduled-later item, not in these slices.
7. **npm publish timing**: vendored dist means no slice depends on the registry.
8. **History hygiene**: moot by construction — submodules receive fresh commits of current content only; AppBuilder's history (3.5MB PNGs, STATUS.md, appdata) never leaves the private repo.

<Project>

  <!--
    Where each project puts obj/ and bin/.

    THE PROBLEM THIS SOLVES. A host may bind-mount this repository into a container that runs
    `dotnet watch` while a developer also builds the same tree from the host. Both SDKs then build the
    SAME source into the SAME obj/ directories and corrupt each other: NuGet's
    `project.assets.json already exists`, and MSBuild's `ResolvePackageAssets` failing to read its own
    cache file.

    WITH CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT SET, intermediate and output paths move to a container-local volume and
    the bind-mounted tree is never written to. WITHOUT it (a developer's machine, CI, a plain clone),
    nothing changes and obj/bin sit where every .NET tool expects them.

    It has to live in Directory.Build.props rather than each .csproj: BaseIntermediateOutputPath is
    read during restore, before the SDK's own props are imported, and setting it any later is silently
    ignored for restore while still applying to build, which produces a worse failure than the one it
    fixes.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT)' != ''">
    <BaseIntermediateOutputPath>$(CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT)/$(MSBuildProjectName)/obj/</BaseIntermediateOutputPath>
    <BaseOutputPath>$(CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT)/$(MSBuildProjectName)/bin/</BaseOutputPath>

    <!--
      And exclude the CONVENTIONAL obj/bin, which is no longer excluded automatically.

      The SDK's default source glob skips $(BaseIntermediateOutputPath) and $(BaseOutputPath). Move
      those elsewhere and the ordinary ./obj suddenly looks like ordinary source: a container reading
      the bind-mounted tree compiles the host's leftover generated AssemblyInfo.cs alongside its own
      and fails with CS0579 "duplicate attribute", an error that names a file nobody wrote and points
      at neither cause.
    -->
    <DefaultItemExcludes>$(DefaultItemExcludes);obj/**;bin/**</DefaultItemExcludes>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    DO NOT set CORDANGO_BUILD_ROOT to run TESTS. It is for app hosts only.

    `Corpus.RepoRoot()` finds the repository by walking up from the test assembly's location, so an
    output directory outside the repo makes it throw and takes every corpus-driven theory down with
    it. Said here because the failure names a missing repo root and gives no hint that an environment
    variable caused it.
  -->

</Project>
=== slnx ===
<!--
  THE EXTRACTION TEST, as a runnable command rather than a claim.

      dotnet test Cordango.slnx

  must pass in a plain clone of this repository: no database, no containers, no platform, nothing
  from the private monorepo this code was lifted out of. That is the whole promise of an open
  toolchain, so it is a command rather than a paragraph.

  Run it alongside the private suite in every slice. It is seconds, and it is the only check that
  notices the boundary eroding before somebody actually tries to build from a fresh clone.
-->

mkdir -p oss/cordango/docs && cat > oss/cordango/docs/apigenerator-assessment.md <<'DOC'
# What the standalone scaffold takes from TCDev.APIGenerator

Cordango's standalone target generates a conventional ASP.NET Core application. The question this
document answers, once, is how much of that application should be *generated per entity* and how
much should be *written once and shared* — and whether an existing answer to that question could be
adopted rather than rewritten.

The existing answer assessed here is [DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api][repo] (`TCDev.APIGenerator`), read at
commit `4279e35`, February 2023, .NET 6. It solves a neighbouring problem: turn annotated POCOs into
a REST API at runtime. Verdicts below are **adopt** (take the package as a dependency), **absorb**
(lift the code), or **pattern** (take the idea, write our own).

[repo]: https://github.com/DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api

## The verdict in one line

**Pattern, throughout. Nothing is adopted as a dependency and nothing is lifted verbatim.** The
shape of the thing — generic machinery once, thin types per entity — is exactly right and is the
architecture of `Cordango.Standalone`. The mechanism underneath it is built for a problem we do not
have, and the code has defects a generator would replicate into every application it produced.

## Why not adopt the package

The library targets .NET 6 and its last release is `0.7.1-rc1`. It pulls in Swashbuckle,
Newtonsoft.Json, EntityFramework.Triggers and `EFCore.AutomaticMigrations` transitively, and its
optional modules add OData, GraphQL and RabbitMQ. A generated Cordango application should have a
dependency list its owner can read in one screen and audit themselves; inheriting a stack to get one
generic controller inverts that.

The deeper reason is the one below.

## The mechanism we do not need

`TCDev.APIGenerator` discovers its entities **at runtime, by reflection**: `AddAssembly` scans for
`[Api]`, `GenericTypeControllerFeatureProvider` closes `GenericController<T,TId>` over each
discovered type, `GenericControllerRouteConvention` rewrites the route from the attribute, and
`GenericDbContext.OnModelCreating` calls `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` plus `builder.Entity(t)`
for whatever else it found.

That machinery exists to answer a question at startup that **we answer at generation time**. We know
every entity, every route and every key type when we emit the code. Reflection buys us nothing there
and costs three things that matter for a generated artifact:

- **Determinism.** Registration order becomes assembly-scan order. Our whole build contract is that
  the same definition produces byte-identical output that behaves identically.
- **Legibility.** The user owns this code. `services.AddCordangoEntity<Expense>()` in a generated
  registration file is greppable; a controller conjured by a feature provider is not, and the first
  time someone wants to add a custom endpoint they have to understand the conjuring.
- **Startup cost and failure mode.** A mis-registration surfaces as a missing route at runtime
  rather than a compile error.

So `Cordango.Standalone` keeps the generic controller and the generic store, and the generator emits
**explicit registration** for them. The `[Api]` attribute, the assembly scanner, the feature provider
and the route convention have no counterpart.

## Piece by piece

| Piece | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `IObjectBase<TId>` | **pattern** | Becomes `IRecord`, non-generic: Cordango record ids are `text`. One type parameter fewer everywhere. |
| `IHasTrackingFields` | **pattern** | Kept, near-verbatim in shape (`Created`/`CreatedBy`/`LastModified`/`LastModifiedBy`). Set centrally — see the defect below. |
| `IHasQueryFields` (`IIsQueryable`) | **dropped** | It declares which fields are queryable as a `string[]` on the entity. Ours is in the definition already; the generator emits the filter surface from it. |
| `ISoftDelete`, `SoftDeletable` | **dropped for v1** | No Cordango definition expresses soft delete. Adding the interface without the language to reach it is scaffolding for a feature nobody can request. |
| `IHasTenantId` | **dropped, by product boundary** | Standalone builds one application for one organisation. Multi-tenancy is the platform. |
| `[Api]` attribute, `ApiMethodsToGenerate` | **dropped** | Configuration for runtime discovery. We generate the controller registration and the method set directly. |
| `GenericDbContext` + `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` | **pattern, and the best idea here** | `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` per entity is exactly the seam we want: EF's own extension point, one generated file per entity, no reflection needed once we call it explicitly. |
| `GenericRepository<T,TId>` | **pattern** | The shape is right, the implementation is not (below). |
| Lifecycle hooks `IBeforeCreate<T>` … | **pattern, relocated** | The idea is essential — it is where computed recompute, validation and command-owned-field enforcement will live at S7/S8. But see "hooks belong in DI". |
| `GenericController<T,TId>` | **pattern** | Route/verb shape carries over. Error handling, permission enforcement and status codes are ours. |
| Feature provider, route convention, application part | **dropped** | See above. |
| `ApplicationDataService` | **dropped** | A holder for two `DbContext`s and `HttpContext`. Injecting `DbContext` directly is clearer and testable without an HTTP context. |
| `ExceptionMiddleware` | **pattern** | The idea (one place turns an exception into a JSON body) is right. Ours emits the Cordango `{code, error}` wire, not `ValidationProblemDetails`, and does not put `ex.Message` on the wire. |
| Scope-based authorization (`ApiAuthAttribute`, `ValidateScopes`) | **dropped** | Ours is definition-driven: roles, entity grants, per-field overrides, command grants. Not expressible as static scope strings on a type. |
| `EFCore.AutomaticMigrations` | **rejected, deliberately** | See below. |
| OData, GraphQL, RabbitMQ, Redis, DbFirst | **out of scope** | |

## Hooks belong in DI, not on the entity

In `TCDev.APIGenerator` a hook is an interface **the POCO itself implements**, and the sample shows
business logic in the entity class:

```csharp
public class Student : IObjectBase<int>, IBeforeCreate<Student>
{
    public Task<Student> BeforeCreate(Student newItem, IApplicationDataService<...> data) { ... }
}
```

For a hand-written application that is a reasonable convenience. For a **generated** one it is a
trap: the entity file is the file the generator overwrites on every build, so the one place the
framework invites you to put your logic is the one place that cannot survive a rebuild.

`Cordango.Standalone` therefore resolves hooks from the service container:

```csharp
public interface IBeforeCreate<T> { Task BeforeCreateAsync(T record, RecordContext ctx, CancellationToken ct); }
```

Generated hooks land in their own files and register themselves; a user's hand-written hook is
another registration next to them, and both run. The entity stays a POCO — pure data, safe to
regenerate — and a hook can be unit-tested with no entity graph and no HTTP context.

## Migrations: EF-native, not automatic

The sample application calls `app.UseAutomaticApiMigrations()`, which uses `EFCore.AutomaticMigrations`
to diff the model against the live database at every startup. The implementation hard-codes
`AutomaticMigrationDataLossAllowed = true` on its first call regardless of the `allowDataLoss`
argument, and swallows the resulting exception to `Console.WriteLine`.

We do the opposite, and it is a decision rather than a preference. The generator invokes EF's own
`MigrationsScaffolder` with a pinned migration id, so the migration is a **file in the user's
repository that they can read, edit, and review in a pull request**; startup runs
`Database.Migrate()`. After generation the application evolves by `dotnet ef migrations add` like any
other EF project — which is the whole promise of the standalone target: the user gets an ordinary
application, not one that only our toolchain understands.

## Defects found, and what they change

These are recorded because a generator amplifies: a bug lifted from here would ship in every
application Cordango ever emits.

**The `IsAssignableFrom` inversion.** Six sites test `typeof(TEntity).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(IHasTrackingFields))`
where they mean `IsAssignableTo` — the operands are the wrong way round, so the condition is false
for every entity. The consequences are silent: **tracking fields are never populated**, and in
`GenericRepository.Delete` the soft-delete branch is never taken, so an entity that opts into
`ISoftDelete` is **hard-deleted instead**. The same inversion in `GenericDbContext.OnModelCreating`
means the tenant query filter is never applied, which in a multi-tenant deployment is a data-exposure
bug rather than a missing feature.

The lesson we take: a type-relationship test written by hand, in a place with no test covering the
negative case, is worth eliminating rather than getting right. `Cordango.Standalone` sets tracking
fields in **one** place — `SaveChanges`, over `ChangeTracker.Entries<IHasTrackingFields>()` — where
the compiler enforces the relationship and the wrong direction will not compile.

**`async void`.** `GenericRepository.Create` and `.Update` are `async void`. The controller's
`repository.Create(record, data); await repository.SaveAsync();` therefore does not await the
create — the `BeforeCreate` hook races the save, and any exception the hook throws is unobservable
and terminates the process rather than returning a 400. Our equivalents are `Task`-returning and
awaited.

**`Update` assigns a local.** `oldRecord = newRecord;` after `Attach(oldRecord)` writes a parameter,
not the tracked entity; the line has no effect. The controller separately does
`ChangeTracker.Clear(); Update(record)`, which is what actually persists — and which also means the
`BeforeUpdate` hook's changes to the *old* record are discarded, and a client that omits a field
writes `null` over it.

**`IAfterCreate` calls `BeforeCreate`.** The after-create branch casts to `IBeforeCreate<TEntity>`
and invokes `BeforeCreate` a second time.

**`Find` dereferences `cacheOptions` unconditionally.** `string.Format(cacheOptions.cacheKey, id)`
runs whenever an `ICacheService` is registered, but `cacheOptions` is only non-null when the entity
carries `[Cachable]` — a NullReferenceException for every uncached entity in a Redis-enabled app.

**`Get(id)` compares `e.Id.ToString() == id.ToString()`.** Either it fails to translate to SQL and
loads the table, or it translates to a cast that cannot use the primary key index.

**Exception detail on the wire.** Both the controller (`return BadRequest(ex.Message)`) and
`ExceptionMiddleware` (`Detail = ex.Message`) return raw exception text to the caller. Ours maps to a
stable `{code, error}` pair and logs the exception server-side.

**The Postgres provider does not use Postgres.** `TCDev.APIGenerator.Data.Postgres`'s
`ProviderConfig.OnConfiguring` calls `optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(...)`, and its `AddDataContextSQL`
extension is `private`, so it is unreachable from outside the assembly. The `src/Data/**` tree looks
like a half-finished restructure of `src/TCDev.APIGenerator.*` — both copies are in the solution.

## What this leaves us

The architecture is Tim's, and it survives the assessment intact:

> generic machinery written once and compiled into a library; thin, regenerable, per-entity types;
> `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as the mapping seam; lifecycle hooks as the extension point;
> EF migrations as the schema story.

What changes is that **registration is generated rather than discovered**, **hooks live in the
container rather than on the entity**, **tracking fields are set once where the type system can check
it**, and **migrations are files the user owns**. Those four are the difference between a runtime

# What the standalone scaffold takes from TCDev.APIGenerator

Cordango's standalone target generates a conventional ASP.NET Core application. The question this
document answers, once, is how much of that application should be *generated per entity* and how
much should be *written once and shared* — and whether an existing answer to that question could be
adopted rather than rewritten.

The existing answer assessed here is [DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api][repo] (`TCDev.APIGenerator`), read at
commit `4279e35`, February 2023, .NET 6. It solves a neighbouring problem: turn annotated POCOs into
a REST API at runtime. Verdicts below are **adopt** (take the package as a dependency), **absorb**
(lift the code), or **pattern** (take the idea, write our own).

[repo]: https://github.com/DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api

## The verdict in one line

**Pattern, throughout. Nothing is adopted as a dependency and nothing is lifted verbatim.** The
shape of the thing — generic machinery once, thin types per entity — is exactly right and is the
architecture of `Cordango.Standalone`. The mechanism underneath it is built for a problem we do not
have, and the code carries defects a generator would replicate into every application it produced.

## Why not adopt the package

The library targets .NET 6 and its last release is `0.7.1-rc1`. It pulls in Swashbuckle,
Newtonsoft.Json, EntityFramework.Triggers and `EFCore.AutomaticMigrations` transitively, and its
optional modules add OData, GraphQL and RabbitMQ. A generated Cordango application should have a
dependency list its owner can read in one screen and audit themselves; inheriting a stack to get one
generic controller inverts that.

The deeper reason is the one below.

## The mechanism we do not need

`TCDev.APIGenerator` discovers its entities **at runtime, by reflection**: `AddAssembly` scans for
`[Api]`, `GenericTypeControllerFeatureProvider` closes `GenericController<T,TId>` over each
discovered type, `GenericControllerRouteConvention` rewrites the route from the attribute, and
`GenericDbContext.OnModelCreating` calls `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` plus `builder.Entity(t)`
for whatever else it found.

That machinery exists to answer a question at startup that **we answer at generation time**. We know
every entity, every route and every key type when we emit the code. Reflection buys us nothing there
and costs three things that matter for a generated artifact:

- **Determinism.** Registration order becomes assembly-scan order. The whole build contract is that
  the same definition produces byte-identical output that behaves identically.
- **Legibility.** The user owns this code. `services.AddRecord<Expense>()` in a generated
  registration file is greppable; a controller conjured by a feature provider is not, and the first
  time somebody wants to add an endpoint of their own they have to understand the conjuring first.
- **Failure mode.** A mis-registration surfaces as a missing route at runtime rather than as a
  compile error.

So `Cordango.Standalone` keeps the generic controller and the generic store, and the generator emits
**explicit registration** for them. The `[Api]` attribute, the assembly scanner, the feature provider
and the route convention have no counterpart here.

## Piece by piece

| Piece | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `IObjectBase<TId>` | **pattern** | Becomes `IRecord`, non-generic: Cordango record ids are `text`. One type parameter fewer everywhere. |
| `IHasTrackingFields` | **pattern** | Kept, near-verbatim in shape (`Created`/`CreatedBy`/`LastModified`/`LastModifiedBy`). Set centrally — see the defect below. |
| `IHasQueryFields` (`IIsQueryable`) | **dropped** | It declares queryable fields as a `string[]` on the entity. Ours are in the definition already, and the generator emits the filter surface from it. |
| `ISoftDelete`, `SoftDeletable` | **dropped for v1** | No Cordango definition expresses soft delete. Adding the interface without the language to reach it is scaffolding for a feature nobody can request. |
| `IHasTenantId` | **dropped, by product boundary** | Standalone builds one application for one organisation. Multi-tenancy is the platform. |
| `[Api]` attribute, `ApiMethodsToGenerate` | **dropped** | Configuration for runtime discovery. We generate the registration and the method set directly. |
| `GenericDbContext` + `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` | **pattern, and the best idea here** | `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` per entity is exactly the seam we want: EF's own extension point, one generated file per entity, no reflection needed once we call it explicitly. |
| `GenericRepository<T,TId>` | **pattern** | The shape is right, the implementation is not (below). |
| Lifecycle hooks `IBeforeCreate<T>` … | **pattern, relocated** | The idea is essential — it is where computed recompute, validation and command-owned-field enforcement live at S7/S8. But see "hooks belong in the container". |
| `GenericController<T,TId>` | **pattern** | Route and verb shape carry over. Error handling, permission enforcement and status codes are ours. |
| Feature provider, route convention, application part | **dropped** | See above. |
| `ApplicationDataService` | **dropped** | A holder for two `DbContext`s and an `HttpContext`. Injecting the `DbContext` directly is clearer and testable with no HTTP context in sight. |
| `ExceptionMiddleware` | **pattern** | One place turning an exception into a JSON body is right. Ours emits the Cordango `{code, error}` wire rather than `ValidationProblemDetails`, and does not put `ex.Message` on it. |
| Scope-based authorization (`ApiAuthAttribute`, `ValidateScopes`) | **dropped** | Ours is definition-driven: roles, entity grants, per-field overrides, command grants. Not expressible as static scope strings on a type. |
| `EFCore.AutomaticMigrations` | **rejected, deliberately** | See below. |
| OData, GraphQL, RabbitMQ, Redis, DbFirst | **out of scope** | |

## Hooks belong in the container, not on the entity

In `TCDev.APIGenerator` a hook is an interface **the POCO itself implements**, and the sample puts
business logic in the entity class:

```csharp
public class Student : IObjectBase<int>, IBeforeCreate<Student>
{
    public Task<Student> BeforeCreate(Student newItem, IApplicationDataService<...> data) { ... }
}
```

For a hand-written application that is a reasonable convenience. For a **generated** one it is a
trap: the entity file is the file the generator overwrites on every build, so the one place the
framework invites you to put your logic is the one place that cannot survive a rebuild.

`Cordango.Standalone` therefore resolves hooks from the service container:

```csharp
public interface IBeforeCreate<T> { Task BeforeCreateAsync(T record, RecordContext context, CancellationToken ct); }
```

Generated hooks land in their own files and register themselves; a hand-written hook is another
registration next to them, and both run. The entity stays a POCO — pure data, safe to regenerate —
and a hook can be unit-tested with no entity graph and no HTTP context.

## Migrations: EF-native, not automatic

The sample application calls `app.UseAutomaticApiMigrations()`, which uses `EFCore.AutomaticMigrations`
to diff the model against the live database at every startup. The implementation hard-codes
`AutomaticMigrationDataLossAllowed = true` on its first call regardless of the `allowDataLoss`
argument it was given, and swallows the resulting exception to `Console.WriteLine`.

We do the opposite, and it is a decision rather than a preference. The generator invokes EF's own
`MigrationsScaffolder` with a pinned migration id, so the migration is a **file in the user's
repository that they can read, edit and review in a pull request**; startup runs `Database.Migrate()`.
After generation the application evolves by `dotnet ef migrations add` like any other EF project —
which is the whole promise of the standalone target: an ordinary application, not one that only our
toolchain understands.

## Defects found, and what they change

Recorded because a generator amplifies: a bug lifted from here would ship in every application
Cordango ever emits.

**The `IsAssignableFrom` inversion.** Six sites test `typeof(TEntity).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(IHasTrackingFields))`
where they mean `IsAssignableTo` — the operands are the wrong way round, so the condition is false
for every entity. The consequences are silent: **tracking fields are never populated**, and in
`GenericRepository.Delete` the soft-delete branch is never taken, so an entity that opts into
`ISoftDelete` is **hard-deleted instead**. The same inversion in `GenericDbContext.OnModelCreating`
means the tenant query filter is never applied, which in a multi-tenant deployment is a
data-exposure bug rather than a missing feature.

The lesson we take: a hand-written type-relationship test, in a place with no test covering the
negative case, is worth eliminating rather than getting right. `Cordango.Standalone` sets tracking
fields in **one** place — `SaveChanges`, over `ChangeTracker.Entries<IHasTrackingFields>()` — where
the compiler enforces the relationship and the wrong direction does not compile.

**`async void`.** `GenericRepository.Create` and `.Update` are `async void`. The controller's
`repository.Create(record, data); await repository.SaveAsync();` therefore does not await the create
— the `BeforeCreate` hook races the save, and any exception the hook throws is unobservable and
terminates the process rather than returning a 400. Our equivalents return `Task` and are awaited.

**`Update` assigns a local.** `oldRecord = newRecord;` after `Attach(oldRecord)` writes a parameter,
not the tracked entity; the line has no effect. The controller separately does
`ChangeTracker.Clear(); Update(record)`, which is what actually persists — and which also means the
`BeforeUpdate` hook's changes to the old record are discarded, and a client that omits a field
writes `null` over it.

**`IAfterCreate` calls `BeforeCreate`.** The after-create branch casts to `IBeforeCreate<TEntity>`
and invokes `BeforeCreate` a second time.

**`Find` dereferences `cacheOptions` unconditionally.** `string.Format(cacheOptions.cacheKey, id)`
runs whenever an `ICacheService` is registered, but `cacheOptions` is only non-null when the entity
carries `[Cachable]` — a `NullReferenceException` for every uncached entity in a Redis-enabled app.

**`Get(id)` compares `e.Id.ToString() == id.ToString()`.** Either it fails to translate to SQL and
loads the table, or it translates to a cast that cannot use the primary key index.

**Exception detail on the wire.** Both the controller (`return BadRequest(ex.Message)`) and
`ExceptionMiddleware` (`Detail = ex.Message`) hand raw exception text to the caller. Ours maps to a
stable `{code, error}` pair and logs the exception server-side.

**The Postgres provider does not use Postgres.** `TCDev.APIGenerator.Data.Postgres`'s
`ProviderConfig.OnConfiguring` calls `optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(...)`, and its `AddDataContextSQL`
extension is `private`, so it is unreachable from outside the assembly. The `src/Data/**` tree looks
like a half-finished restructure of `src/TCDev.APIGenerator.*`; both copies are in the solution.

## What this leaves us

The architecture is Tim's, and it survives the assessment intact:

> generic machinery written once and compiled into a library; thin, regenerable, per-entity types;
> `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as the mapping seam; lifecycle hooks as the extension point;
> EF migrations as the schema story.

What changes is that **registration is generated rather than discovered**, **hooks live in the
container rather than on the entity**, **tracking fields are set once where the type system can check
it**, and **migrations are files the user owns**. Those four are the difference between a runtime
framework and a code generator, which is the difference between the two projects.

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <RootNamespace>Cordango.Standalone</RootNamespace>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    THIS PROJECT IS NOT A DEPENDENCY OF A GENERATED APPLICATION. IT IS ITS SOURCE.

    Every .cs file here is compiled twice. Once into this assembly, where the repository's own tests
    exercise it — so the code a generated app runs is code with tests behind it rather than a string
    literal nobody ever ran. And once inside the user's application, because
    Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue emits these same files verbatim into `Cordango/` under the generated
    project.

    Emitting source rather than referencing a package is deliberate for v1. There is no published
    NuGet feed yet, and more importantly a generated application is supposed to be one the owner can
    read end to end, build offline, step into with a debugger and fork if we disappear. A binary they
    cannot open would undercut the whole point of the standalone target. When a package does exist,
    swapping to it is one PackageReference line in the emitted csproj — the same trade the vendored
    web-controls dist makes on the JavaScript side.

    These files keep their Apache-2.0 headers when they land in a user's repository. They are our
    code under our licence; the GENERATED files beside them are the user's and carry no header.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!--
    Templates/ is what a generated application looks like BEFORE any entity exists: its Program.cs,
    its project file, its configuration, its Docker packaging, its Vue shell. It is the user's code,
    so it is not compiled here and carries no licence header — only the instantiation test proves it
    builds, by materialising it and running the real SDK over it.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Remove="Templates/**" />
    <None Include="Templates/**" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <RootNamespace>Cordango.Standalone</RootNamespace>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    THIS PROJECT IS NOT A DEPENDENCY OF A GENERATED APPLICATION. IT IS ITS SOURCE.

    Every .cs file here is compiled twice. Once into this assembly, where the repository's own tests
    exercise it — so the code a generated app runs is code with tests behind it rather than a string
    literal nobody ever ran. And once inside the user's application, because
    Cordango.SourceGen.DotNetVue emits these same files verbatim into `Cordango/` under the generated
    project.

    Emitting source rather than referencing a package is deliberate for v1. There is no published
    NuGet feed yet, and more importantly a generated application is supposed to be one the owner can
    read end to end, build offline, step into with a debugger and fork if we disappear. A binary they
    cannot open would undercut the whole point of the standalone target. When a package does exist,
    swapping to it is one PackageReference line in the emitted csproj — the same trade the vendored
    web-controls dist makes on the JavaScript side.

    These files keep their Apache-2.0 headers when they land in a user's repository. They are our
    code under our licence; the GENERATED files beside them are the user's and carry no header.
  -->
  <!--
    Two dependencies, and they are the two a generated application already has: the web framework it
    is hosted by and the ORM it stores rows with. The database PROVIDER is not among them — this
    library never names Postgres, so the same runtime source compiles in an application somebody
    repointed at SQL Server or SQLite without touching a line of it.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore" Version="10.0.9" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!--
    Templates/ is what a generated application looks like BEFORE any entity exists: its Program.cs,
    its project file, its configuration, its Docker packaging, its Vue shell. It is the user's code,
    so it is not compiled here and carries no licence header — only the instantiation test proves it
    builds, by materialising it and running the real SDK over it.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Remove="Templates/**" />
    <None Include="Templates/**" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

import { CordangoControls } from '@cordango/web-controls'
import '@cordango/web-controls/styles'
import 'vuetify/styles'

import App from './App.vue'
import { router } from './router.js'
import { api, mediaUrl, loadPeople } from './api.js'
import { messages } from './i18n.js'

const i18n = createI18n({
  legacy: false,
  locale: localStorage.getItem('{{AppKey}}.locale') || 'en',
  fallbackLocale: 'en',
  messages,
})

const vuetify = createVuetify()

createApp(App)
  .use(router)
  .use(vuetify)
  .use(i18n)
  // The five things a control cannot work out for itself. Every one is optional and falls back to
  // something inert, so a control renders with or without them — an unwired directory shows an id
  // instead of a name rather than throwing.
  .use(CordangoControls, {
    locale: () => i18n.global.locale.value,
    people: loadPeople,
    media: mediaUrl,
    route: (target, id) => `/${target.entity}/${id}`,
    loadTableSettings: (handle, table) =>
      api.get(`/api/settings/table/${handle}/${table}`).catch(() => null),
    saveTableSettings: (handle, table, settings) =>
      api.put(`/api/settings/table/${handle}/${table}`, settings).catch(() => {}),
    toast: (message) => window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('{{AppKey}}:toast', { detail: message })),
  })
  .mount('#app')

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n'
import { useRoute, useRouter } from 'vue-router'
import { signIn } from '../session.js'

const { t } = useI18n()
const route = useRoute()
const router = useRouter()

const email = ref('')
const password = ref('')
const remember = ref(false)
const busy = ref(false)
const error = ref(null)

async function submit() {
  busy.value = true
  error.value = null
  try {
    await signIn(email.value, password.value, remember.value)
    router.push(route.query.redirect || { name: 'home' })
  } catch (failure) {
    // The server's message, because it already says the right thing in the reader's language and
    // distinguishes "wrong password" from "locked out" without saying which accounts exist.
    error.value = failure.message || t('auth.failed')
  } finally {
    busy.value = false
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <v-container class="d-flex justify-center align-center" style="min-height: 80vh">
    <v-card width="420" class="pa-4">
      <v-card-title>{{ t('auth.title') }}</v-card-title>
      <v-card-text>
        <v-form @submit.prevent="submit">
          <v-text-field
            v-model="email"
            :label="t('auth.email')"
            type="email"
            autocomplete="username"
            autofocus
          />
          <v-text-field
            v-model="password"
            :label="t('auth.password')"
            type="password"
            autocomplete="current-password"
          />
          <v-checkbox v-model="remember" :label="t('auth.remember')" density="compact" />
          <v-alert v-if="error" type="error" variant="tonal" class="mb-4">{{ error }}</v-alert>
          <v-btn type="submit" color="primary" block :loading="busy">{{ t('auth.submit') }}</v-btn>
        </v-form>
      </v-card-text>
    </v-card>
  </v-container>
</template>

# {{AppName}} — one image serving the API and the single-page app from the same origin.
#
# Same origin is a decision, not an accident. It is what lets the session live in a cookie with no
# CORS configuration to get wrong, and what lets the antiforgery token be read by this application's
# own script and by nothing else. Splitting the two across origins is possible and costs you both.

# ---- the front end -------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM node:22-alpine AS web
WORKDIR /src/web

# Dependencies first, so that editing a component does not re-run the install. `npm ci` rather than
# `npm install`: it installs exactly the lock file and fails if the two have drifted, which is what
# you want from a build you expect to reproduce.
COPY web/package.json web/package-lock.json* ./
COPY web/vendor ./vendor
RUN npm ci

COPY web/ ./
RUN npm run build

# ---- the back end --------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS api
WORKDIR /src

COPY api/*.csproj ./api/
RUN dotnet restore ./api

COPY api/ ./api/
COPY --from=web /src/api/wwwroot ./api/wwwroot
RUN dotnet publish ./api -c Release -o /app --no-restore

# ---- what actually ships -------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0
WORKDIR /app

# Not root. A web process has no business being able to write to its own binaries, and the one
# directory it does need to write to is named below.
RUN useradd --uid 5678 --create-home app \
    && mkdir -p /appdata/media \
    && chown -R app /appdata
USER app

COPY --from=api /app .

ENV ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080 \
    Storage__Path=/appdata/media
EXPOSE 8080

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=20s \
    CMD wget --spider -q http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "{{AppNamespace}}.Api.dll"]

# Everything {{AppName}} needs to run, on one machine.
#
# Two services and one volume. The database version is pinned rather than floating on `latest`,
# because a Postgres major upgrade is a decision to make deliberately on a Tuesday morning and not
# one to discover after a `docker compose pull`.

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17.5-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: {{AppKey}}
      POSTGRES_USER: {{AppKey}}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U {{AppKey}}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  app:
    build: .
    depends_on:
      # The application migrates its own schema at startup, so it needs a database that is ready to
      # answer rather than merely a container that has been created.

# {{AppName}}

Generated by [Cordango](https://github.com/cordango/cordango) from an App Definition, and yours from
here on.

This is an ordinary ASP.NET Core + EF Core + PostgreSQL application with a Vue 3 and Vuetify front
end. Nothing in it calls home, nothing requires the tool that produced it, and every file is one you
can read, change and deploy anywhere .NET runs.
{{PartialBuildSection}}
## Running it

```
cp .env.example .env      # set DB_PASSWORD, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD
docker compose up --build
```

Then open <http://localhost:8080> and sign in as the administrator you named in `.env`.

`ADMIN_EMAIL` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` are read once, on the first start with an empty database, to
create the first account. There is no default password: an application that shipped with one would
ship compromised.

## Running it without Docker

```
# database
docker compose up -d db

# back end
cd api && dotnet run

# front end, in another terminal
cd web && npm install && npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` proxies `/api` to the back end so the two behave as one origin, which is how they are
served in production.

## How it is laid out

```
api/                  the ASP.NET Core application
  Program.cs          startup: database, identity, the runtime, the pipeline
  AppSetup.cs         every entity, hook and permission, registered — generated
  Data/               the DbContext and one configuration per entity — generated
  Entities/           one plain class per entity — generated
  Controllers/        one per entity — generated
  Migrations/         EF migrations. Ordinary ones: read them, edit them, review them
  Identity/           sign-in, accounts, the first administrator
  Cordango/           the Cordango runtime, as source (Apache-2.0)
  Resources/          messages.en.json, messages.de.json
web/                  the Vue application
  src/views/          one page per screen — generated
  vendor/             @cordango/web-controls, vendored so the build works offline

docker-compose.yml    the application and a pinned Postgres
cordango.build.json   what produced this, and every file it wrote
```

Running the generator again over the same output directory replaces the files it wrote last time and
leaves everything else alone. `cordango.build.json` lists exactly which files those are, so there is
never a guess about what is safe to edit.
